A: Employees are entitled to 24 privileged leaves, 8 casual leaves and 12 sick leaves per calendar year. Privileged leaves must be planned at least 7 working days in advance and can be availed up to 3 times a year. Unused privileged leaves are carried forward up to a cap of 60 days.

RETRIEVED CONTEXT (cite as [S1], [S2], ...):
[S1] What is the leave policy at Axis Bank?
Q: What is the leave policy at Axis Bank?
A: Employees are entitled to 24 privileged leaves, 8 casual leaves and 12 sick leaves per calendar year. Privileged leaves must be planned at least 7 working days in advance and can be availed up to 3 times a year. Unused privileged leaves are carried forward up to a cap of 60 days.

[S2] Leave Policy 2026
# Leave Policy — 2026

## Applicability
This policy applies to all permanent employees of Axis Bank across corporate offices,
branches and contact centres. Contractual and third-party staff are governed by the
terms of their engagement contracts.

## Types of Leave

### Privileged Leave (PL)
- 24 working days per calendar year, credited quarterly (6 per quarter).
- Can be availed up to 3 times a year.
- Minimum block of 3 continuous days per instance.
- Requests must be raised on the HR self-service portal at least 7 working days in
  advance for domestic travel and 14 working days for international travel.
- Unused PL carries forward up to a cap of 60 days.

### Casual Leave (CL)
- 8 working days per calendar year, credited on 1st January.
- Cannot be carried forward.
- Maximum block of 2 continuous days.
- Requires reporting manager approval; can be applied on the same day for genuine
  emergencies.

### Sick Leave (SL)
- 12 working days per calendar year, credited on 1st January.
- Medical certificate mandatory for any block of 3 or more continuous days.
- Cannot be carried forward.

### Maternity Leave
- 26 weeks of paid leave for the first two children.
- 12 weeks of paid leave from the third child onwards.
- Adoption leave of 12 weeks for children below 3 months of age.
- Requests must be raised at least 8 weeks before the expected date, with the
  medical certificate attached.

### Paternity Leave
- 10 working days of paid leave available within 90 days of the child's birth.
- Can be split into 2 blocks.

### Bereavement Leave
- 5 working days for immediate family (spouse, child, parent, sibling).
- 2 working days for extended family.

## Compensatory Off
- Employees working on declared holidays are eligible for compensatory off within 45 days.
- Compensatory off cannot be encashed.

## Encashment
- On separation, up to 60 days of PL balance is encashed at basic + DA.
- CL and SL are not encashable.

## Escalation
For any dispute regarding leave balance, raise a ticket on HResponse under
`HR > Leave Balance`. First-level SLA is 2 business days.

# SME Banking Leave Planning Guide 2026

## Purpose

This guide helps SME Banking teams plan leave without compromising coverage during peak periods such as quarter-end disbursement pushes.

## Planning Rules

Privileged leave needs at least 7 working days of notice and manager approval.

At least 70 percent of the team must be available during declared peak windows.

Backfill plans must be agreed before overlapping leave is approved.

## Seasonal Guidance

Anticipate demand around quarter-end disbursement pushes and open early leave planning.

Rotate preferred holiday weeks across the team from year to year.

## Manager Duties

Publish the unit leave calendar quarterly.

Review pending balances and prompt planned usage.

Escalate conflicts to the HR business partner.

## Policy code

HR-LVG-SME-2026-01 | Owner: HR Operations.

[S2] Leave Policy 2026
# Leave Policy — 2026

## Applicability
This policy applies to all permanent employees of Axis Bank across corporate offices,
branches and contact centres. Contractual and third-party staff are governed by the
terms of their engagement contracts.

## Types of Leave

### Privileged Leave (PL)
- 24 working days per calendar year, credited quarterly (6 per quarter).
- Can be availed up to 3 times a year.
- Minimum block of 3 continuous days per instance.
- Requests must be raised on the HR self-service portal at least 7 working days in
  advance for domestic travel and 14 working days for international travel.
- Unused PL carries forward up to a cap of 60 days.

### Casual Leave (CL)
- 8 working days per calendar year, credited on 1st January.
- Cannot be carried forward.
- Maximum block of 2 continuous days.
- Requires reporting manager approval; can be applied on the same day for genuine
  emergencies.

### Sick Leave (SL)
- 12 working days per calendar year, credited on 1st January.
- Medical certificate mandatory for any block of 3 or more continuous days.
- Cannot be carried forward.

### Maternity Leave
- 26 weeks of paid leave for the first two children.
- 12 weeks of paid leave from the third child onwards.
- Adoption leave of 12 weeks for children below 3 months of age.
- Requests must be raised at least 8 weeks before the expected date, with the
  medical certificate attached.

### Paternity Leave
- 10 working days of paid leave available within 90 days of the child's birth.
- Can be split into 2 blocks.

### Bereavement Leave
- 5 working days for immediate family (spouse, child, parent, sibling).
- 2 working days for extended family.

## Compensatory Off
- Employees working on declared holidays are eligible for compensatory off within 45 days.
- Compensatory off cannot be encashed.

## Encashment
- On separation, up to 60 days of PL balance is encashed at basic + DA.
- CL and SL are not encashable.

## Escalation
For any dispute regarding leave balance, raise a ticket on HResponse under
`HR > Leave Balance`. First-level SLA is 2 business days.

# Leave Policy — 2026

## Applicability
This policy applies to all permanent employees of Axis Bank across corporate offices,
branches and contact centres. Contractual and third-party staff are governed by the
terms of their engagement contracts.

## Types of Leave

### Privileged Leave (PL)
- 24 working days per calendar year, credited quarterly (6 per quarter).
- Can be availed up to 3 times a year.
- Minimum block of 3 continuous days per instance.
- Requests must be raised on the HR self-service portal at least 7 working days in
  advance for domestic travel and 14 working days for international travel.
- Unused PL carries forward up to a cap of 60 days.

### Casual Leave (CL)
- 8 working days per calendar year, credited on 1st January.
- Cannot be carried forward.
- Maximum block of 2 continuous days.
- Requires reporting manager approval; can be applied on the same day for genuine
  emergencies.

### Sick Leave (SL)
- 12 working days per calendar year, credited on 1st January.
- Medical certificate mandatory for any block of 3 or more continuous days.
- Cannot be carried forward.

### Maternity Leave
- 26 weeks of paid leave for the first two children.
- 12 weeks of paid leave from the third child onwards.
- Adoption leave of 12 weeks for children below 3 months of age.
- Requests must be raised at least 8 weeks before the expected date, with the
  medical certificate attached.

### Paternity Leave
- 10 working days of paid leave available within 90 days of the child's birth.
- Can be split into 2 blocks.

### Bereavement Leave
- 5 working days for immediate family (spouse, child, parent, sibling).
- 2 working days for extended family.

## Compensatory Off
- Employees working on declared holidays are eligible for compensatory off within 45 days.
- Compensatory off cannot be encashed.

## Encashment
- On separation, up to 60 days of PL balance is encashed at basic + DA.
- CL and SL are not encashable.

## Escalation
For any dispute regarding leave balance, raise a ticket on HResponse under
`HR > Leave Balance`. First-level SLA is 2 business days.

# Leave Policy — 2026

## Applicability
This policy applies to all permanent employees of Axis Bank across corporate offices,
branches and contact centres. Contractual and third-party staff are governed by the
terms of their engagement contracts.

## Types of Leave

### Privileged Leave (PL)
- 24 working days per calendar year, credited quarterly (6 per quarter).
- Can be availed up to 3 times a year.
- Minimum block of 3 continuous days per instance.
- Requests must be raised on the HR self-service portal at least 7 working days in
  advance for domestic travel and 14 working days for international travel.
- Unused PL carries forward up to a cap of 60 days.

### Casual Leave (CL)
- 8 working days per calendar year, credited on 1st January.
- Cannot be carried forward.
- Maximum block of 2 continuous days.
- Requires reporting manager approval; can be applied on the same day for genuine
  emergencies.

### Sick Leave (SL)
- 12 working days per calendar year, credited on 1st January.
- Medical certificate mandatory for any block of 3 or more continuous days.
- Cannot be carried forward.

### Maternity Leave
- 26 weeks of paid leave for the first two children.
- 12 weeks of paid leave from the third child onwards.
- Adoption leave of 12 weeks for children below 3 months of age.
- Requests must be raised at least 8 weeks before the expected date, with the
  medical certificate attached.

### Paternity Leave
- 10 working days of paid leave available within 90 days of the child's birth.
- Can be split into 2 blocks.

### Bereavement Leave
- 5 working days for immediate family (spouse, child, parent, sibling).
- 2 working days for extended family.

## Compensatory Off
- Employees working on declared holidays are eligible for compensatory off within 45 days.
- Compensatory off cannot be encashed.

## Encashment
- On separation, up to 60 days of PL balance is encashed at basic + DA.
- CL and SL are not encashable.

## Escalation
For any dispute regarding leave balance, raise a ticket on HResponse under
`HR > Leave Balance`. First-level SLA is 2 business days.

A: The minimum block for Maternity Leave is continuous.

[S1] How do I apply for maternity leave?
Q: How do I apply for maternity leave?
A: Maternity leave of 26 weeks is available to eligible female employees. Raise a request via the HR self-service portal at least 8 weeks before the expected delivery date. Attach the medical certificate and reporting-manager approval before submission.

[S2] What is the minimum block for Maternity Leave?
Q: What is the minimum block for Maternity Leave?
A: The minimum block for Maternity Leave is continuous.

[S3] Medical Insurance Cover
# Group Medical Insurance Cover

## Coverage
The group medical policy covers the employee, spouse, up to two dependent children and
dependent parents. Sum insured is defined by grade in the annual benefit summary.

## Inclusions
Hospitalisation, pre and post-hospitalisation expenses, daycare procedures, and
ambulance charges. Maternity is covered for eligible dependants as per policy terms.

## Cashless and Reimbursement
Cashless treatment is available at network hospitals on presentation of the health card.
Reimbursement claims follow the insurer's claim process.

## Addition of Dependants
New dependants must be added within 30 days of the life event (marriage, birth) through
the benefits portal with documentary proof.

Policy code: HR-BEN-M-2026-01 | Owner: Benefits team.

[S4] What happens to Maternity Leave if I resign?
Q: What happens to Maternity Leave if I resign?
A: On separation, Maternity Leave is settled per the full-and-final rules; the balance does not carry forward.

[S5] Leave Policy 2026
# Leave Policy — 2026

## Applicability
This policy applies to all permanent employees of Axis Bank across corporate offices,
branches and contact centres. Contractual and third-party staff are governed by the
terms of their engagement contracts.

## Types of Leave

### Privileged Leave (PL)
- 24 working days per calendar year, credited quarterly (6 per quarter).
- Can be availed up to 3 times a year.
- Minimum block of 3 continuous days per instance.
- Requests must be raised on the HR self-service portal at least 7 working days in
  advance for domestic travel and 14 working days for international travel.
- Unused PL carries forward up to a cap of 60 days.

### Casual Leave (CL)
- 8 working days per calendar year, credited on 1st January.
- Cannot be carried forward.
- Maximum block of 2 continuous days.
- Requires reporting manager approval; can be applied on the same day for genuine
  emergencies.

### Sick Leave (SL)
- 12 working days per calendar year, credited on 1st January.
- Medical certificate mandatory for any block of 3 or more continuous days.
- Cannot be carried forward.

### Maternity Leave
- 26 weeks of paid leave for the first two children.
- 12 weeks of paid leave from the third child onwards.
- Adoption leave of 12 weeks for children below 3 months of age.
- Requests must be raised at least 8 weeks before the expected date, with the
  medical certificate attached.

### Paternity Leave
- 10 working days of paid leave available within 90 days of the child's birth.
- Can be split into 2 blocks.

### Bereavement Leave
- 5 working days for immediate family (spouse, child, parent, sibling).
- 2 working days for extended family.

## Compensatory Off
- Employees working on declared holidays are eligible for compensatory off within 45 days.
- Compensatory off cannot be encashed.

## Encashment
- On separation, up to 60 days of PL balance is encashed at basic + DA.
- CL and SL are not encashable.

## Escalation
For any dispute regarding leave balance, raise a ticket on HResponse under
`HR > Leave Balance`. First-level SLA is 2 business days.

A: Maternity leave of 26 weeks is available to eligible female employees. Raise a request via the HR self-service portal at least 8 weeks before the expected delivery date. Attach the medical certificate and reporting-manager approval before submission.

[S2] What is the minimum block for Maternity Leave?
Q: What is the minimum block for Maternity Leave?
A: The minimum block for Maternity Leave is continuous.

[S3] Medical Insurance Cover
# Group Medical Insurance Cover

## Coverage
The group medical policy covers the employee, spouse, up to two dependent children and
dependent parents. Sum insured is defined by grade in the annual benefit summary.

## Inclusions
Hospitalisation, pre and post-hospitalisation expenses, daycare procedures, and
ambulance charges. Maternity is covered for eligible dependants as per policy terms.

## Cashless and Reimbursement
Cashless treatment is available at network hospitals on presentation of the health card.
Reimbursement claims follow the insurer's claim process.

## Addition of Dependants
New dependants must be added within 30 days of the life event (marriage, birth) through
the benefits portal with documentary proof.

Policy code: HR-BEN-M-2026-01 | Owner: Benefits team.

[S4] What happens to Maternity Leave if I resign?
Q: What happens to Maternity Leave if I resign?
A: On separation, Maternity Leave is settled per the full-and-final rules; the balance does not carry forward.

[S5] Leave Policy 2026
# Leave Policy — 2026

## Applicability
This policy applies to all permanent employees of Axis Bank across corporate offices,
branches and contact centres. Contractual and third-party staff are governed by the
terms of their engagement contracts.

## Types of Leave

### Privileged Leave (PL)
- 24 working days per calendar year, credited quarterly (6 per quarter).
- Can be availed up to 3 times a year.
- Minimum block of 3 continuous days per instance.
- Requests must be raised on the HR self-service portal at least 7 working days in
  advance for domestic travel and 14 working days for international travel.
- Unused PL carries forward up to a cap of 60 days.

### Casual Leave (CL)
- 8 working days per calendar year, credited on 1st January.
- Cannot be carried forward.
- Maximum block of 2 continuous days.
- Requires reporting manager approval; can be applied on the same day for genuine
  emergencies.

### Sick Leave (SL)
- 12 working days per calendar year, credited on 1st January.
- Medical certificate mandatory for any block of 3 or more continuous days.
- Cannot be carried forward.

### Maternity Leave
- 26 weeks of paid leave for the first two children.
- 12 weeks of paid leave from the third child onwards.
- Adoption leave of 12 weeks for children below 3 months of age.
- Requests must be raised at least 8 weeks before the expected date, with the
  medical certificate attached.

### Paternity Leave
- 10 working days of paid leave available within 90 days of the child's birth.
- Can be split into 2 blocks.

### Bereavement Leave
- 5 working days for immediate family (spouse, child, parent, sibling).
- 2 working days for extended family.

## Compensatory Off
- Employees working on declared holidays are eligible for compensatory off within 45 days.
- Compensatory off cannot be encashed.

## Encashment
- On separation, up to 60 days of PL balance is encashed at basic + DA.
- CL and SL are not encashable.

## Escalation
For any dispute regarding leave balance, raise a ticket on HResponse under
`HR > Leave Balance`. First-level SLA is 2 business days.

# Leave Policy — 2026

## Applicability
This policy applies to all permanent employees of Axis Bank across corporate offices,
branches and contact centres. Contractual and third-party staff are governed by the
terms of their engagement contracts.

## Types of Leave

### Privileged Leave (PL)
- 24 working days per calendar year, credited quarterly (6 per quarter).
- Can be availed up to 3 times a year.
- Minimum block of 3 continuous days per instance.
- Requests must be raised on the HR self-service portal at least 7 working days in
  advance for domestic travel and 14 working days for international travel.
- Unused PL carries forward up to a cap of 60 days.

### Casual Leave (CL)
- 8 working days per calendar year, credited on 1st January.
- Cannot be carried forward.
- Maximum block of 2 continuous days.
- Requires reporting manager approval; can be applied on the same day for genuine
  emergencies.

### Sick Leave (SL)
- 12 working days per calendar year, credited on 1st January.
- Medical certificate mandatory for any block of 3 or more continuous days.
- Cannot be carried forward.

### Maternity Leave
- 26 weeks of paid leave for the first two children.
- 12 weeks of paid leave from the third child onwards.
- Adoption leave of 12 weeks for children below 3 months of age.
- Requests must be raised at least 8 weeks before the expected date, with the
  medical certificate attached.

### Paternity Leave
- 10 working days of paid leave available within 90 days of the child's birth.
- Can be split into 2 blocks.

### Bereavement Leave
- 5 working days for immediate family (spouse, child, parent, sibling).
- 2 working days for extended family.

## Compensatory Off
- Employees working on declared holidays are eligible for compensatory off within 45 days.
- Compensatory off cannot be encashed.

## Encashment
- On separation, up to 60 days of PL balance is encashed at basic + DA.
- CL and SL are not encashable.

## Escalation
For any dispute regarding leave balance, raise a ticket on HResponse under
`HR > Leave Balance`. First-level SLA is 2 business days.

[S5] What is the minimum block for Maternity Leave?
Q: What is the minimum block for Maternity Leave?
A: The minimum block for Maternity Leave is continuous.

# Leave Policy — 2026

## Applicability
This policy applies to all permanent employees of Axis Bank across corporate offices,
branches and contact centres. Contractual and third-party staff are governed by the
terms of their engagement contracts.

## Types of Leave

### Privileged Leave (PL)
- 24 working days per calendar year, credited quarterly (6 per quarter).
- Can be availed up to 3 times a year.
- Minimum block of 3 continuous days per instance.
- Requests must be raised on the HR self-service portal at least 7 working days in
  advance for domestic travel and 14 working days for international travel.
- Unused PL carries forward up to a cap of 60 days.

### Casual Leave (CL)
- 8 working days per calendar year, credited on 1st January.
- Cannot be carried forward.
- Maximum block of 2 continuous days.
- Requires reporting manager approval; can be applied on the same day for genuine
  emergencies.

### Sick Leave (SL)
- 12 working days per calendar year, credited on 1st January.
- Medical certificate mandatory for any block of 3 or more continuous days.
- Cannot be carried forward.

### Maternity Leave
- 26 weeks of paid leave for the first two children.
- 12 weeks of paid leave from the third child onwards.
- Adoption leave of 12 weeks for children below 3 months of age.
- Requests must be raised at least 8 weeks before the expected date, with the
  medical certificate attached.

### Paternity Leave

# Group Medical Insurance Cover

## Coverage
The group medical policy covers the employee, spouse, up to two dependent children and
dependent parents. Sum insured is defined by grade in the annual benefit summary.

Hospitalisation, pre and post-hospitalisation expenses, daycare procedures, and

## Cashless and Reimbursement
Cashless treatment is available at network hospitals on presentation of the health card.
Reimbursement claims follow the insurer's claim process.

## Addition of Dependants
New dependants must be added within 30 days of the life event (marriage, birth) through
the benefits portal with documentary proof.

# HR Operations Leave Planning Guide 2026

## Purpose

This guide helps HR Operations teams plan leave without compromising coverage during peak periods such as appraisal and year-end cycles.

## Planning Rules

Privileged leave needs at least 7 working days of notice and manager approval.

At least 70 percent of the team must be available during declared peak windows.

Backfill plans must be agreed before overlapping leave is approved.

## Seasonal Guidance

Anticipate demand around appraisal and year-end cycles and open early leave planning.

Rotate preferred holiday weeks across the team from year to year.

## Manager Duties

Publish the unit leave calendar quarterly.

Review pending balances and prompt planned usage.

Escalate conflicts to the HR business partner.

## Policy code

HR-LVG-HROPS-2026-01 | Owner: HR Operations.

# Leave Policy — 2026

## Applicability
This policy applies to all permanent employees of Axis Bank across corporate offices,
branches and contact centres. Contractual and third-party staff are governed by the
terms of their engagement contracts.

## Types of Leave

### Privileged Leave (PL)
- 24 working days per calendar year, credited quarterly (6 per quarter).
- Can be availed up to 3 times a year.
- Minimum block of 3 continuous days per instance.
- Requests must be raised on the HR self-service portal at least 7 working days in
  advance for domestic travel and 14 working days for international travel.
- Unused PL carries forward up to a cap of 60 days.

### Casual Leave (CL)
- 8 working days per calendar year, credited on 1st January.
- Cannot be carried forward.
- Maximum block of 2 continuous days.
- Requires reporting manager approval; can be applied on the same day for genuine
  emergencies.

### Sick Leave (SL)
- 12 working days per calendar year, credited on 1st January.
- Medical certificate mandatory for any block of 3 or more continuous days.
- Cannot be carried forward.

### Maternity Leave
- 26 weeks of paid leave for the first two children.
- 12 weeks of paid leave from the third child onwards.
- Adoption leave of 12 weeks for children below 3 months of age.
- Requests must be raised at least 8 weeks before the expected date, with the
  medical certificate attached.

### Paternity Leave
- 10 working days of paid leave available within 90 days of the child's birth.
- Can be split into 2 blocks.

### Bereavement Leave
- 5 working days for immediate family (spouse, child, parent, sibling).
- 2 working days for extended family.

## Compensatory Off
- Employees working on declared holidays are eligible for compensatory off within 45 days.
- Compensatory off cannot be encashed.

## Encashment
- On separation, up to 60 days of PL balance is encashed at basic + DA.
- CL and SL are not encashable.

## Escalation
For any dispute regarding leave balance, raise a ticket on HResponse under
`HR > Leave Balance`. First-level SLA is 2 business days.

- Medical certificate mandatory for any block of 3 or more continuous days.
- Cannot be carried forward.

### Maternity Leave
- 26 weeks of paid leave for the first two children.
- 12 weeks of paid leave from the third child onwards.
- Adoption leave of 12 weeks for children below 3 months of age.
- Requests must be raised at least 8 weeks before the expected date, with the
  medical certificate attached.

### Paternity Leave
- 10 working days of paid leave available within 90 days of the child's birth.
- Can be split into 2 blocks.

### Bereavement Leave
- 5 working days for immediate family (spouse, child, parent, sibling).
- 2 working days for extended family.

## Compensatory Off
- Employees working on declared holidays are eligible for compensatory off within 45 days.
- Compensatory off cannot be encashed.

## Encashment
- On separation, up to 60 days of PL balance is encashed at basic + DA.
- CL and SL are not encashable.

## Escalation
For any dispute regarding leave balance, raise a ticket on HResponse under
`HR > Leave Balance`. First-level SLA is 2 business days.

# Process Checklist: Promotion Review

## Entry Point

Start the process from Performance module > Promotion.

## Checklist

1. Confirm eligibility per the policy before starting.

2. Prepare the supporting documents listed in the form.

3. Obtain the required manager or HR approvals.

4. Submit and note the reference number.

5. Track the request and respond to queries within 2 business days.

## Common Rejections

Missing documents, incomplete fields, or approvals outside the authority matrix.

## SLA

Standard requests complete within 5 business days unless the policy states otherwise.

## Policy code

HR-CHK-PROMO-2026-01 | Owner: HR Operations.

[S5] Tax Declaration Process
# Income-Tax Declaration Process

## Declaration Window
Employees declare proposed investments and rent in April-May each financial year.
Declarations drive monthly tax deduction at source (TDS).

## Eligible Heads
- Section 80C: ELSS, PPF, EPF, life insurance, principal on home loan, tuition fees.
- Section 80D: medical insurance premiums.
- House rent allowance exemption under Section 10(13A).
- Home loan interest under Section 24(b).

## Proof Submission
Investment proofs must be uploaded by the first week of January. Shortfalls in proof
lead to tax recovery in February and March payrolls.

## Form 16
Form 16 is issued by 15 June. Part B includes employer-provided details; Part A carries
the TDS certificate.

Policy code: HR-TAX-2026-01 | Owner: Payroll team.

Q: How is the performance appraisal cycle structured?

events.content:
USER QUESTION:
Could you confirm: what does a rating of 5 mean in the appraisal cycle?

RETRIEVED CONTEXT (cite as [S1], [S2], ...):
[S1] How is the performance appraisal cycle structured?
Q: How is the performance appraisal cycle structured?
A: The appraisal cycle runs from April to March. Goal setting happens in April, mid-year review in September and final review in March-April. Ratings are on a 5-point scale with a normalisation step at the business-unit level.

[S2] Performance Appraisal
# Performance Appraisal Cycle

## Cycle Timeline
| Phase | Window | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Goal setting | 1 Apr – 30 Apr | Employee + reporting manager |
| Mid-year review | 1 Sep – 30 Sep | Employee + reporting manager |
| Self-appraisal | 1 Mar – 15 Mar | Employee |
| Manager appraisal | 16 Mar – 31 Mar | Reporting manager |
| Normalisation | 1 Apr – 15 Apr | Business-unit HRBP |
| Final letters | 20 Apr – 30 Apr | HR Operations |

## Rating Scale
| Rating | Label | Definition |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | Outstanding | Exceptional, sustained impact well beyond role expectations. |
| 4 | Exceeds | Consistently exceeds expectations across most goals. |
| 3 | Meets | Meets all critical expectations. |
| 2 | Partially Meets | Meets some but not all critical expectations. |
| 1 | Below | Below expected performance; performance-improvement plan triggered. |

## Normalisation
- Ratings are normalised at the business-unit level with recommended distribution:
  Outstanding <= 8 %, Exceeds <= 25 %, Meets 55 – 65 %, Partially Meets <= 8 %,
  Below <= 4 %.
- Deviations require CHRO sign-off.

## PIP (Performance Improvement Plan)
- Employees rated `Below` are placed on a 90-day PIP.
- HRBP reviews progress every 30 days.
- Continued rating of `Below` after PIP leads to separation.

## References
- Policy code: HR-PMS-2026-01
- Owner: Talent Management team

# Compensation Review Cycle

## Annual Cycle
Compensation review is effective 1 April. Rating inputs from the appraisal close in March
feed the increment matrix published by the Rewards team.

## Market Benchmarking
Every role is benchmarked against the banking sector median using annual market surveys.
Positions below the 25th percentile are prioritised for corrections.

## Increment Drivers
Increment is driven by performance rating, position-in-range and business affordability.
The matrix is approved by the compensation committee.

## Communication
Revised compensation letters are released in June. Any query must be raised through the
HR service portal within 30 days of release.

Policy code: HR-COMP-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

[S4] Annual Increment Cycle
# Annual Increment Cycle

## Timing
The increment cycle runs from April to June. Performance inputs close in March, calibration
in April, and letters are issued in June.

## Eligibility
Employees who joined on or before 31 December of the previous financial year and are not
under a performance improvement plan are eligible.

## Calibration
Ratings are calibrated at business-unit level before increments are computed. Calibration
adjusts rating distribution, never individual compensation directly.

## Promotion During Cycle
Employees promoted in the same cycle receive the higher of the promotion increment or the
annual increment, not both.

Policy code: HR-COMP-I-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

[S5] How does the promotion review process work?
Q: How does the promotion review process work?
A: For the promotion review process: promotions are reviewed in March-April against performance, tenure and panel feedback.

RECENT CHAT HISTORY:
USER: Could you confirm: when does the mid-year performance review happen?
ASSISTANT: The mid-year review runs from 1 September to 30 September.

[S1] Performance Appraisal
# Performance Appraisal Cycle

## Cycle Timeline
| Phase | Window | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Goal setting | 1 Apr – 30 Apr | Employee + reporting manager |
| Mid-year review | 1 Sep – 30 Sep | Employee + reporting manager |
| Self-appraisal | 1 Mar – 15 Mar | Employee |
| Manager appraisal | 16 Mar – 31 Mar | Reporting manager |
| Normalisation | 1 Apr – 15 Apr | Business-unit HRBP |
| Final letters | 20 Apr – 30 Apr | HR Operations |

## Rating Scale
| Rating | Label | Definition |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | Outstanding | Exceptional, sustained impact well beyond role expectations. |
| 4 | Exceeds | Consistently exceeds expectations across most goals. |
| 3 | Meets | Meets all critical expectations. |
| 2 | Partially Meets | Meets some but not all critical expectations. |
| 1 | Below | Below expected performance; performance-improvement plan triggered. |

## Normalisation
- Ratings are normalised at the business-unit level with recommended distribution:
  Outstanding <= 8 %, Exceeds <= 25 %, Meets 55 – 65 %, Partially Meets <= 8 %,
  Below <= 4 %.
- Deviations require CHRO sign-off.

## PIP (Performance Improvement Plan)
- Employees rated `Below` are placed on a 90-day PIP.
- HRBP reviews progress every 30 days.
- Continued rating of `Below` after PIP leads to separation.

## References
- Policy code: HR-PMS-2026-01
- Owner: Talent Management team

[S2] Code Of Conduct
# Code of Conduct

## Core Principles
- Act with integrity in all dealings.
- Treat customers, colleagues and partners with respect.
- Protect confidential information and customer data.
- Avoid conflicts of interest; declare them promptly.

## Conflict of Interest
Employees must disclose outside business interests, family relationships with vendors,
and board positions in other entities through the declaration portal annually.

## Reporting Misconduct
Misconduct may be reported to the manager, HR, compliance or the whistleblower channel.
Good-faith reports are protected.

## Consequences
Violations lead to disciplinary action up to and including termination, and may be
reported to regulators where applicable.

Policy code: HR-CC-2026-01 | Owner: Employee Relations team.

[S3] Compensation Review
# Compensation Review Cycle

## Annual Cycle
Compensation review is effective 1 April. Rating inputs from the appraisal close in March
feed the increment matrix published by the Rewards team.

## Market Benchmarking
Every role is benchmarked against the banking sector median using annual market surveys.
Positions below the 25th percentile are prioritised for corrections.

## Increment Drivers
Increment is driven by performance rating, position-in-range and business affordability.
The matrix is approved by the compensation committee.

## Communication
Revised compensation letters are released in June. Any query must be raised through the
HR service portal within 30 days of release.

Policy code: HR-COMP-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

[S4] Annual Increment Cycle
# Annual Increment Cycle

## Timing
The increment cycle runs from April to June. Performance inputs close in March, calibration
in April, and letters are issued in June.

## Eligibility
Employees who joined on or before 31 December of the previous financial year and are not
under a performance improvement plan are eligible.

## Calibration
Ratings are calibrated at business-unit level before increments are computed. Calibration
adjusts rating distribution, never individual compensation directly.

## Promotion During Cycle
Employees promoted in the same cycle receive the higher of the promotion increment or the
annual increment, not both.

Policy code: HR-COMP-I-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

[S5] Variable Pay Policy
# Variable Pay Policy

## Eligibility
Variable pay applies to grades M3 and above. It is paid annually against business, unit
and individual scorecard achievement.

## Payout Formula
Payout = target variable × business multiplier × unit multiplier × individual multiplier.
Multipliers range from 0 to 1.5 as per the approved scorecard.

## Timing
Variable pay for a financial year is paid in June of the following year. Employees who
resign before the payout date are not eligible unless the separation policy states otherwise.

## Disputes
Scorecard disputes must be raised within 30 days of scorecard communication to the
business review committee.

Policy code: HR-COMP-V-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

RETRIEVED CONTEXT (cite as [S1], [S2], ...):
[S1] Performance Appraisal
# Performance Appraisal Cycle

## Cycle Timeline
| Phase | Window | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Goal setting | 1 Apr – 30 Apr | Employee + reporting manager |
| Mid-year review | 1 Sep – 30 Sep | Employee + reporting manager |
| Self-appraisal | 1 Mar – 15 Mar | Employee |
| Manager appraisal | 16 Mar – 31 Mar | Reporting manager |
| Normalisation | 1 Apr – 15 Apr | Business-unit HRBP |
| Final letters | 20 Apr – 30 Apr | HR Operations |

## Rating Scale
| Rating | Label | Definition |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | Outstanding | Exceptional, sustained impact well beyond role expectations. |
| 4 | Exceeds | Consistently exceeds expectations across most goals. |
| 3 | Meets | Meets all critical expectations. |
| 2 | Partially Meets | Meets some but not all critical expectations. |
| 1 | Below | Below expected performance; performance-improvement plan triggered. |

## Normalisation
- Ratings are normalised at the business-unit level with recommended distribution:
  Outstanding <= 8 %, Exceeds <= 25 %, Meets 55 – 65 %, Partially Meets <= 8 %,
  Below <= 4 %.
- Deviations require CHRO sign-off.

## PIP (Performance Improvement Plan)
- Employees rated `Below` are placed on a 90-day PIP.
- HRBP reviews progress every 30 days.
- Continued rating of `Below` after PIP leads to separation.

## References
- Policy code: HR-PMS-2026-01
- Owner: Talent Management team

[S2] Code Of Conduct
# Code of Conduct

## Core Principles
- Act with integrity in all dealings.
- Treat customers, colleagues and partners with respect.
- Protect confidential information and customer data.
- Avoid conflicts of interest; declare them promptly.

## Conflict of Interest
Employees must disclose outside business interests, family relationships with vendors,
and board positions in other entities through the declaration portal annually.

## Reporting Misconduct
Misconduct may be reported to the manager, HR, compliance or the whistleblower channel.
Good-faith reports are protected.

## Consequences
Violations lead to disciplinary action up to and including termination, and may be
reported to regulators where applicable.

Policy code: HR-CC-2026-01 | Owner: Employee Relations team.

[S3] Compensation Review
# Compensation Review Cycle

## Annual Cycle
Compensation review is effective 1 April. Rating inputs from the appraisal close in March
feed the increment matrix published by the Rewards team.

## Market Benchmarking
Every role is benchmarked against the banking sector median using annual market surveys.
Positions below the 25th percentile are prioritised for corrections.

## Increment Drivers
Increment is driven by performance rating, position-in-range and business affordability.
The matrix is approved by the compensation committee.

## Communication
Revised compensation letters are released in June. Any query must be raised through the
HR service portal within 30 days of release.

Policy code: HR-COMP-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

[S4] Annual Increment Cycle
# Annual Increment Cycle

## Timing
The increment cycle runs from April to June. Performance inputs close in March, calibration
in April, and letters are issued in June.

## Eligibility
Employees who joined on or before 31 December of the previous financial year and are not
under a performance improvement plan are eligible.

## Calibration
Ratings are calibrated at business-unit level before increments are computed. Calibration
adjusts rating distribution, never individual compensation directly.

## Promotion During Cycle
Employees promoted in the same cycle receive the higher of the promotion increment or the
annual increment, not both.

Policy code: HR-COMP-I-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

[S5] Variable Pay Policy
# Variable Pay Policy

## Eligibility
Variable pay applies to grades M3 and above. It is paid annually against business, unit
and individual scorecard achievement.

## Payout Formula
Payout = target variable × business multiplier × unit multiplier × individual multiplier.
Multipliers range from 0 to 1.5 as per the approved scorecard.

## Timing
Variable pay for a financial year is paid in June of the following year. Employees who
resign before the payout date are not eligible unless the separation policy states otherwise.

## Disputes
Scorecard disputes must be raised within 30 days of scorecard communication to the
business review committee.

Policy code: HR-COMP-V-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

# Provident Fund (PF) & Gratuity — Quick Reference

## Provident Fund
- Contribution: **12% of basic + DA** by the employee, matched by the employer.
- Employer contribution split: 8.33% to EPS (Employee Pension Scheme, capped
  on ₹15,000 basic) + balance to EPF.
- Interest is credited annually as declared by the EPFO.
- Withdrawals: partial withdrawals allowed for defined reasons (marriage,
  higher education, home purchase, medical emergency) subject to service
  tenure thresholds.
- Universal Account Number (UAN) is issued at joining and is portable across
  employers.

## Gratuity
- Payable on separation after continuous service of at least **5 years**
  (waived for death / permanent disability).
- Formula: `(Last drawn basic + DA) × 15 / 26 × completed years of service`.
- Statutory cap: ₹20,00,000 (tax-exempt limit).
- Paid within 30 days of the last working day; delays attract simple interest
  at the notified rate.

## Nomination
Employees must nominate their PF and gratuity beneficiaries within 30 days of
joining and update nominations after any life event (marriage, birth of
child, divorce).

## Related Forms
Download from `Download > HR > Statutory Forms`:
- `PF-NOM-1` — PF nomination
- `GRAT-NOM-2` — Gratuity nomination
- `PF-WD-31` — Partial PF withdrawal

## Policy Code
`HR-STAT-2026-03` · Owner: Employee Services team.

# Certification Reimbursement Policy

## Approved List
Reimbursement applies to certifications on the approved list published annually, such as
CAIIB, CFA, FRM, cloud certifications and role-specific technical certifications.

## Reimbursement Amount
Up to 100 percent of exam fees for certifications on the approved list, capped per grade.
Renewal and membership fees are reimbursed for active certifications.

## Conditions
- Certification must be passed, not merely attempted.
- Employee must be in service on the date of the claim.
- Reimbursement is paid against the fee receipt only.

## Bond
For certifications above the cap threshold, a service commitment of 12 months applies.
Early exit triggers pro-rata recovery.

Policy code: HR-LND-C-2026-01 | Owner: Learning & Development team.

RETRIEVED CONTEXT (cite as [S1], [S2], ...):
[S1] How is the performance appraisal cycle structured?
Q: How is the performance appraisal cycle structured?
A: The appraisal cycle runs from April to March. Goal setting happens in April, mid-year review in September and final review in March-April. Ratings are on a 5-point scale with a normalisation step at the business-unit level.

[S2] Performance Appraisal
# Performance Appraisal Cycle

## Cycle Timeline
| Phase | Window | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Goal setting | 1 Apr – 30 Apr | Employee + reporting manager |
| Mid-year review | 1 Sep – 30 Sep | Employee + reporting manager |
| Self-appraisal | 1 Mar – 15 Mar | Employee |
| Manager appraisal | 16 Mar – 31 Mar | Reporting manager |
| Normalisation | 1 Apr – 15 Apr | Business-unit HRBP |
| Final letters | 20 Apr – 30 Apr | HR Operations |

## Rating Scale
| Rating | Label | Definition |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | Outstanding | Exceptional, sustained impact well beyond role expectations. |
| 4 | Exceeds | Consistently exceeds expectations across most goals. |
| 3 | Meets | Meets all critical expectations. |
| 2 | Partially Meets | Meets some but not all critical expectations. |
| 1 | Below | Below expected performance; performance-improvement plan triggered. |

## Normalisation
- Ratings are normalised at the business-unit level with recommended distribution:
  Outstanding <= 8 %, Exceeds <= 25 %, Meets 55 – 65 %, Partially Meets <= 8 %,
  Below <= 4 %.
- Deviations require CHRO sign-off.

## PIP (Performance Improvement Plan)
- Employees rated `Below` are placed on a 90-day PIP.
- HRBP reviews progress every 30 days.
- Continued rating of `Below` after PIP leads to separation.

## References
- Policy code: HR-PMS-2026-01
- Owner: Talent Management team

## Annual Cycle

USER QUESTION:
For my situation, what does a rating of 5 mean in the appraisal cycle?

RETRIEVED CONTEXT (cite as [S1], [S2], ...):
[S1] How is the performance appraisal cycle structured?
Q: How is the performance appraisal cycle structured?
A: The appraisal cycle runs from April to March. Goal setting happens in April, mid-year review in September and final review in March-April. Ratings are on a 5-point scale with a normalisation step at the business-unit level.

[S2] Performance Appraisal
# Performance Appraisal Cycle

## Cycle Timeline
| Phase | Window | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Goal setting | 1 Apr – 30 Apr | Employee + reporting manager |
| Mid-year review | 1 Sep – 30 Sep | Employee + reporting manager |
| Self-appraisal | 1 Mar – 15 Mar | Employee |
| Manager appraisal | 16 Mar – 31 Mar | Reporting manager |
| Normalisation | 1 Apr – 15 Apr | Business-unit HRBP |
| Final letters | 20 Apr – 30 Apr | HR Operations |

## Rating Scale
| Rating | Label | Definition |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | Outstanding | Exceptional, sustained impact well beyond role expectations. |
| 4 | Exceeds | Consistently exceeds expectations across most goals. |
| 3 | Meets | Meets all critical expectations. |
| 2 | Partially Meets | Meets some but not all critical expectations. |
| 1 | Below | Below expected performance; performance-improvement plan triggered. |

## Normalisation
- Ratings are normalised at the business-unit level with recommended distribution:
  Outstanding <= 8 %, Exceeds <= 25 %, Meets 55 – 65 %, Partially Meets <= 8 %,
  Below <= 4 %.
- Deviations require CHRO sign-off.

## PIP (Performance Improvement Plan)
- Employees rated `Below` are placed on a 90-day PIP.
- HRBP reviews progress every 30 days.
- Continued rating of `Below` after PIP leads to separation.

## References
- Policy code: HR-PMS-2026-01
- Owner: Talent Management team

[S3] Compensation Review
# Compensation Review Cycle

## Annual Cycle
Compensation review is effective 1 April. Rating inputs from the appraisal close in March
feed the increment matrix published by the Rewards team.

## Market Benchmarking
Every role is benchmarked against the banking sector median using annual market surveys.
Positions below the 25th percentile are prioritised for corrections.

## Increment Drivers
Increment is driven by performance rating, position-in-range and business affordability.
The matrix is approved by the compensation committee.

## Communication
Revised compensation letters are released in June. Any query must be raised through the
HR service portal within 30 days of release.

Policy code: HR-COMP-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

[S4] Annual Increment Cycle
# Annual Increment Cycle

## Timing
The increment cycle runs from April to June. Performance inputs close in March, calibration
in April, and letters are issued in June.

## Eligibility
Employees who joined on or before 31 December of the previous financial year and are not
under a performance improvement plan are eligible.

## Calibration
Ratings are calibrated at business-unit level before increments are computed. Calibration
adjusts rating distribution, never individual compensation directly.

## Promotion During Cycle
Employees promoted in the same cycle receive the higher of the promotion increment or the
annual increment, not both.

Policy code: HR-COMP-I-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

[S5] Variable Pay Policy
# Variable Pay Policy

## Eligibility
Variable pay applies to grades M3 and above. It is paid annually against business, unit
and individual scorecard achievement.

## Payout Formula
Payout = target variable × business multiplier × unit multiplier × individual multiplier.
Multipliers range from 0 to 1.5 as per the approved scorecard.

## Timing
Variable pay for a financial year is paid in June of the following year. Employees who
resign before the payout date are not eligible unless the separation policy states otherwise.

## Disputes
Scorecard disputes must be raised within 30 days of scorecard communication to the
business review committee.

Policy code: HR-COMP-V-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

# Process Checklist: Promotion Review

## Entry Point

Start the process from Performance module > Promotion.

## Checklist

1. Confirm eligibility per the policy before starting.

2. Prepare the supporting documents listed in the form.

3. Obtain the required manager or HR approvals.

4. Submit and note the reference number.

5. Track the request and respond to queries within 2 business days.

Missing documents, incomplete fields, or approvals outside the authority matrix.

Standard requests complete within 5 business days unless the policy states otherwise.

HR-CHK-PROMO-2026-01 | Owner: HR Operations.

# Income-Tax Declaration Process

## Declaration Window
Employees declare proposed investments and rent in April-May each financial year.
Declarations drive monthly tax deduction at source (TDS).

## Eligible Heads
- Section 80C: ELSS, PPF, EPF, life insurance, principal on home loan, tuition fees.
- Section 80D: medical insurance premiums.
- House rent allowance exemption under Section 10(13A).
- Home loan interest under Section 24(b).

## Proof Submission
Investment proofs must be uploaded by the first week of January. Shortfalls in proof
lead to tax recovery in February and March payrolls.

## Form 16
Form 16 is issued by 15 June. Part B includes employer-provided details; Part A carries
the TDS certificate.

Policy code: HR-TAX-2026-01 | Owner: Payroll team.

USER QUESTION:
What does a rating of 5 mean in the appraisal cycle?

RETRIEVED CONTEXT (cite as [S1], [S2], ...):
[S1] How is the performance appraisal cycle structured?
Q: How is the performance appraisal cycle structured?
A: The appraisal cycle runs from April to March. Goal setting happens in April, mid-year review in September and final review in March-April. Ratings are on a 5-point scale with a normalisation step at the business-unit level.

[S2] Performance Appraisal
# Performance Appraisal Cycle

## Cycle Timeline
| Phase | Window | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Goal setting | 1 Apr – 30 Apr | Employee + reporting manager |
| Mid-year review | 1 Sep – 30 Sep | Employee + reporting manager |
| Self-appraisal | 1 Mar – 15 Mar | Employee |
| Manager appraisal | 16 Mar – 31 Mar | Reporting manager |
| Normalisation | 1 Apr – 15 Apr | Business-unit HRBP |
| Final letters | 20 Apr – 30 Apr | HR Operations |

## Rating Scale
| Rating | Label | Definition |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | Outstanding | Exceptional, sustained impact well beyond role expectations. |
| 4 | Exceeds | Consistently exceeds expectations across most goals. |
| 3 | Meets | Meets all critical expectations. |
| 2 | Partially Meets | Meets some but not all critical expectations. |
| 1 | Below | Below expected performance; performance-improvement plan triggered. |

## Normalisation
- Ratings are normalised at the business-unit level with recommended distribution:
  Outstanding <= 8 %, Exceeds <= 25 %, Meets 55 – 65 %, Partially Meets <= 8 %,
  Below <= 4 %.
- Deviations require CHRO sign-off.

## PIP (Performance Improvement Plan)
- Employees rated `Below` are placed on a 90-day PIP.
- HRBP reviews progress every 30 days.
- Continued rating of `Below` after PIP leads to separation.

## References
- Policy code: HR-PMS-2026-01
- Owner: Talent Management team

[S3] Compensation Review
# Compensation Review Cycle

## Annual Cycle
Compensation review is effective 1 April. Rating inputs from the appraisal close in March
feed the increment matrix published by the Rewards team.

## Market Benchmarking
Every role is benchmarked against the banking sector median using annual market surveys.
Positions below the 25th percentile are prioritised for corrections.

## Increment Drivers
Increment is driven by performance rating, position-in-range and business affordability.
The matrix is approved by the compensation committee.

## Communication
Revised compensation letters are released in June. Any query must be raised through the
HR service portal within 30 days of release.

Policy code: HR-COMP-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

[S4] Annual Increment Cycle
# Annual Increment Cycle

## Timing
The increment cycle runs from April to June. Performance inputs close in March, calibration
in April, and letters are issued in June.

## Eligibility
Employees who joined on or before 31 December of the previous financial year and are not
under a performance improvement plan are eligible.

## Calibration
Ratings are calibrated at business-unit level before increments are computed. Calibration
adjusts rating distribution, never individual compensation directly.

## Promotion During Cycle
Employees promoted in the same cycle receive the higher of the promotion increment or the
annual increment, not both.

Policy code: HR-COMP-I-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

[S5] Promotion Guidelines
# Promotion Guidelines

## Criteria
Promotion requires sustained performance at or above "Exceeds Expectations" for two
consecutive cycles, role readiness and a vacancy or business case at the higher grade.

## Readiness Assessments
For people-manager moves, a manager-readiness assessment and structured panel interview
are mandatory.

## Timing
Promotions are effective 1 April or 1 October. Off-cycle promotions are rare and require
CHRO approval.

## Communication
Promotion decisions are communicated by the manager with HR support. Unsuccessful
candidates receive structured feedback.

Policy code: HR-PROM-2026-01 | Owner: Talent Management team.

[S1] Performance Appraisal
# Performance Appraisal Cycle

## Cycle Timeline
| Phase | Window | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Goal setting | 1 Apr – 30 Apr | Employee + reporting manager |
| Mid-year review | 1 Sep – 30 Sep | Employee + reporting manager |
| Self-appraisal | 1 Mar – 15 Mar | Employee |
| Manager appraisal | 16 Mar – 31 Mar | Reporting manager |
| Normalisation | 1 Apr – 15 Apr | Business-unit HRBP |
| Final letters | 20 Apr – 30 Apr | HR Operations |

## Rating Scale
| Rating | Label | Definition |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | Outstanding | Exceptional, sustained impact well beyond role expectations. |
| 4 | Exceeds | Consistently exceeds expectations across most goals. |
| 3 | Meets | Meets all critical expectations. |
| 2 | Partially Meets | Meets some but not all critical expectations. |
| 1 | Below | Below expected performance; performance-improvement plan triggered. |

## Normalisation
- Ratings are normalised at the business-unit level with recommended distribution:
  Outstanding <= 8 %, Exceeds <= 25 %, Meets 55 – 65 %, Partially Meets <= 8 %,
  Below <= 4 %.
- Deviations require CHRO sign-off.

## PIP (Performance Improvement Plan)
- Employees rated `Below` are placed on a 90-day PIP.
- HRBP reviews progress every 30 days.
- Continued rating of `Below` after PIP leads to separation.

## References
- Policy code: HR-PMS-2026-01
- Owner: Talent Management team

[S2] Annual Increment Cycle
# Annual Increment Cycle

## Timing
The increment cycle runs from April to June. Performance inputs close in March, calibration
in April, and letters are issued in June.

## Eligibility
Employees who joined on or before 31 December of the previous financial year and are not
under a performance improvement plan are eligible.

## Calibration
Ratings are calibrated at business-unit level before increments are computed. Calibration
adjusts rating distribution, never individual compensation directly.

## Promotion During Cycle
Employees promoted in the same cycle receive the higher of the promotion increment or the
annual increment, not both.

Policy code: HR-COMP-I-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

[S3] Code Of Conduct
# Code of Conduct

## Core Principles
- Act with integrity in all dealings.
- Treat customers, colleagues and partners with respect.
- Protect confidential information and customer data.
- Avoid conflicts of interest; declare them promptly.

## Conflict of Interest
Employees must disclose outside business interests, family relationships with vendors,
and board positions in other entities through the declaration portal annually.

## Reporting Misconduct
Misconduct may be reported to the manager, HR, compliance or the whistleblower channel.
Good-faith reports are protected.

## Consequences
Violations lead to disciplinary action up to and including termination, and may be
reported to regulators where applicable.

Policy code: HR-CC-2026-01 | Owner: Employee Relations team.

[S4] Variable Pay Policy
# Variable Pay Policy

## Eligibility
Variable pay applies to grades M3 and above. It is paid annually against business, unit
and individual scorecard achievement.

## Payout Formula
Payout = target variable × business multiplier × unit multiplier × individual multiplier.
Multipliers range from 0 to 1.5 as per the approved scorecard.

## Timing
Variable pay for a financial year is paid in June of the following year. Employees who
resign before the payout date are not eligible unless the separation policy states otherwise.

## Disputes
Scorecard disputes must be raised within 30 days of scorecard communication to the
business review committee.

Policy code: HR-COMP-V-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

[S5] Compensation Review
# Compensation Review Cycle

## Annual Cycle
Compensation review is effective 1 April. Rating inputs from the appraisal close in March
feed the increment matrix published by the Rewards team.

## Market Benchmarking
Every role is benchmarked against the banking sector median using annual market surveys.
Positions below the 25th percentile are prioritised for corrections.

## Increment Drivers
Increment is driven by performance rating, position-in-range and business affordability.
The matrix is approved by the compensation committee.

## Communication
Revised compensation letters are released in June. Any query must be raised through the
HR service portal within 30 days of release.

Policy code: HR-COMP-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

USER: What does a rating of 5 mean in the appraisal cycle?
ASSISTANT: A rating of 5 is Outstanding: exceptional, sustained impact well beyond role expectations.

USER QUESTION:
What happens to employees rated Below?

RETRIEVED CONTEXT (cite as [S1], [S2], ...):
[S1] Performance Appraisal
# Performance Appraisal Cycle

## Cycle Timeline
| Phase | Window | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Goal setting | 1 Apr – 30 Apr | Employee + reporting manager |
| Mid-year review | 1 Sep – 30 Sep | Employee + reporting manager |
| Self-appraisal | 1 Mar – 15 Mar | Employee |
| Manager appraisal | 16 Mar – 31 Mar | Reporting manager |
| Normalisation | 1 Apr – 15 Apr | Business-unit HRBP |
| Final letters | 20 Apr – 30 Apr | HR Operations |

## Rating Scale
| Rating | Label | Definition |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | Outstanding | Exceptional, sustained impact well beyond role expectations. |
| 4 | Exceeds | Consistently exceeds expectations across most goals. |
| 3 | Meets | Meets all critical expectations. |
| 2 | Partially Meets | Meets some but not all critical expectations. |
| 1 | Below | Below expected performance; performance-improvement plan triggered. |

## Normalisation
- Ratings are normalised at the business-unit level with recommended distribution:
  Outstanding <= 8 %, Exceeds <= 25 %, Meets 55 – 65 %, Partially Meets <= 8 %,
  Below <= 4 %.
- Deviations require CHRO sign-off.

## PIP (Performance Improvement Plan)
- Employees rated `Below` are placed on a 90-day PIP.
- HRBP reviews progress every 30 days.
- Continued rating of `Below` after PIP leads to separation.

## References
- Policy code: HR-PMS-2026-01
- Owner: Talent Management team

[S2] Annual Increment Cycle
# Annual Increment Cycle

## Timing
The increment cycle runs from April to June. Performance inputs close in March, calibration
in April, and letters are issued in June.

## Eligibility
Employees who joined on or before 31 December of the previous financial year and are not
under a performance improvement plan are eligible.

## Calibration
Ratings are calibrated at business-unit level before increments are computed. Calibration
adjusts rating distribution, never individual compensation directly.

## Promotion During Cycle
Employees promoted in the same cycle receive the higher of the promotion increment or the
annual increment, not both.

Policy code: HR-COMP-I-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

[S3] Code Of Conduct
# Code of Conduct

## Core Principles
- Act with integrity in all dealings.
- Treat customers, colleagues and partners with respect.
- Protect confidential information and customer data.
- Avoid conflicts of interest; declare them promptly.

## Conflict of Interest
Employees must disclose outside business interests, family relationships with vendors,
and board positions in other entities through the declaration portal annually.

## Reporting Misconduct
Misconduct may be reported to the manager, HR, compliance or the whistleblower channel.
Good-faith reports are protected.

## Consequences
Violations lead to disciplinary action up to and including termination, and may be
reported to regulators where applicable.

Policy code: HR-CC-2026-01 | Owner: Employee Relations team.

[S4] Variable Pay Policy
# Variable Pay Policy

## Eligibility
Variable pay applies to grades M3 and above. It is paid annually against business, unit
and individual scorecard achievement.

## Payout Formula
Payout = target variable × business multiplier × unit multiplier × individual multiplier.
Multipliers range from 0 to 1.5 as per the approved scorecard.

## Timing
Variable pay for a financial year is paid in June of the following year. Employees who
resign before the payout date are not eligible unless the separation policy states otherwise.

## Disputes
Scorecard disputes must be raised within 30 days of scorecard communication to the
business review committee.

# Income-Tax Declaration Process

## Declaration Window
Employees declare proposed investments and rent in April-May each financial year.
Declarations drive monthly tax deduction at source (TDS).

## Eligible Heads
- Section 80C: ELSS, PPF, EPF, life insurance, principal on home loan, tuition fees.
- Section 80D: medical insurance premiums.
- House rent allowance exemption under Section 10(13A).
- Home loan interest under Section 24(b).

## Proof Submission
Investment proofs must be uploaded by the first week of January. Shortfalls in proof
lead to tax recovery in February and March payrolls.

## Form 16
Form 16 is issued by 15 June. Part B includes employer-provided details; Part A carries
the TDS certificate.

Policy code: HR-TAX-2026-01 | Owner: Payroll team.

USER QUESTION:
Please clarify: what does a rating of 5 mean in the appraisal cycle?

RETRIEVED CONTEXT (cite as [S1], [S2], ...):
[S1] How is the performance appraisal cycle structured?
Q: How is the performance appraisal cycle structured?
A: The appraisal cycle runs from April to March. Goal setting happens in April, mid-year review in September and final review in March-April. Ratings are on a 5-point scale with a normalisation step at the business-unit level.

[S2] Performance Appraisal
# Performance Appraisal Cycle

## Cycle Timeline
| Phase | Window | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Goal setting | 1 Apr – 30 Apr | Employee + reporting manager |
| Mid-year review | 1 Sep – 30 Sep | Employee + reporting manager |
| Self-appraisal | 1 Mar – 15 Mar | Employee |
| Manager appraisal | 16 Mar – 31 Mar | Reporting manager |
| Normalisation | 1 Apr – 15 Apr | Business-unit HRBP |
| Final letters | 20 Apr – 30 Apr | HR Operations |

## Rating Scale
| Rating | Label | Definition |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | Outstanding | Exceptional, sustained impact well beyond role expectations. |
| 4 | Exceeds | Consistently exceeds expectations across most goals. |
| 3 | Meets | Meets all critical expectations. |
| 2 | Partially Meets | Meets some but not all critical expectations. |
| 1 | Below | Below expected performance; performance-improvement plan triggered. |

## Normalisation
- Ratings are normalised at the business-unit level with recommended distribution:
  Outstanding <= 8 %, Exceeds <= 25 %, Meets 55 – 65 %, Partially Meets <= 8 %,
  Below <= 4 %.
- Deviations require CHRO sign-off.

## PIP (Performance Improvement Plan)
- Employees rated `Below` are placed on a 90-day PIP.
- HRBP reviews progress every 30 days.
- Continued rating of `Below` after PIP leads to separation.

## References
- Policy code: HR-PMS-2026-01
- Owner: Talent Management team

[S3] Compensation Review
# Compensation Review Cycle

## Annual Cycle
Compensation review is effective 1 April. Rating inputs from the appraisal close in March
feed the increment matrix published by the Rewards team.

## Market Benchmarking
Every role is benchmarked against the banking sector median using annual market surveys.
Positions below the 25th percentile are prioritised for corrections.

## Increment Drivers
Increment is driven by performance rating, position-in-range and business affordability.
The matrix is approved by the compensation committee.

## Communication
Revised compensation letters are released in June. Any query must be raised through the
HR service portal within 30 days of release.

Policy code: HR-COMP-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

[S4] Annual Increment Cycle
# Annual Increment Cycle

## Timing
The increment cycle runs from April to June. Performance inputs close in March, calibration
in April, and letters are issued in June.

## Eligibility
Employees who joined on or before 31 December of the previous financial year and are not
under a performance improvement plan are eligible.

## Calibration
Ratings are calibrated at business-unit level before increments are computed. Calibration
adjusts rating distribution, never individual compensation directly.

## Promotion During Cycle
Employees promoted in the same cycle receive the higher of the promotion increment or the
annual increment, not both.

Policy code: HR-COMP-I-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

[S5] How many days of Bereavement Leave am I entitled to each year?
Q: How many days of Bereavement Leave am I entitled to each year?
A: You are entitled to 5 working days of Bereavement Leave per calendar year.

# Variable Pay Policy

Variable pay applies to grades M3 and above. It is paid annually against business, unit

resign before the payout date are not eligible unless the separation policy states otherwise.

business review committee.

Employees must disclose outside business interests, family relationships with vendors,
and board positions in other entities through the declaration portal annually.

## Reporting Misconduct
Misconduct may be reported to the manager, HR, compliance or the whistleblower channel.
Good-faith reports are protected.

Violations lead to disciplinary action up to and including termination, and may be
reported to regulators where applicable.

# Performance Appraisal Cycle

## Cycle Timeline
| Phase | Window | Owner |

| Final letters | 20 Apr – 30 Apr | HR Operations |

## Rating Scale
| Rating | Label | Definition |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | Outstanding | Exceptional, sustained impact well beyond role expectations. |
| 4 | Exceeds | Consistently exceeds expectations across most goals. |
| 3 | Meets | Meets all critical expectations. |
| 2 | Partially Meets | Meets some but not all critical expectations. |
| 1 | Below | Below expected performance; performance-improvement plan triggered. |

## Normalisation
- Ratings are normalised at the business-unit level with recommended distribution:
  Outstanding <= 8 %, Exceeds <= 25 %, Meets 55 – 65 %, Partially Meets <= 8 %,
  Below <= 4 %.
- Deviations require CHRO sign-off.

- Employees rated `Below` are placed on a 90-day PIP.
- HRBP reviews progress every 30 days.
- Continued rating of `Below` after PIP leads to separation.

## References
- Policy code: HR-PMS-2026-01
- Owner: Talent Management team

[S2] Variable Pay Policy
# Variable Pay Policy

## Eligibility
Variable pay applies to grades M3 and above. It is paid annually against business, unit
and individual scorecard achievement.

## Payout Formula
Payout = target variable × business multiplier × unit multiplier × individual multiplier.
Multipliers range from 0 to 1.5 as per the approved scorecard.

## Timing
Variable pay for a financial year is paid in June of the following year. Employees who
resign before the payout date are not eligible unless the separation policy states otherwise.

## Disputes
Scorecard disputes must be raised within 30 days of scorecard communication to the
business review committee.

Policy code: HR-COMP-V-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

[S3] Annual Increment Cycle
# Annual Increment Cycle

## Timing
The increment cycle runs from April to June. Performance inputs close in March, calibration
in April, and letters are issued in June.

## Eligibility
Employees who joined on or before 31 December of the previous financial year and are not
under a performance improvement plan are eligible.

## Calibration
Ratings are calibrated at business-unit level before increments are computed. Calibration
adjusts rating distribution, never individual compensation directly.

## Promotion During Cycle
Employees promoted in the same cycle receive the higher of the promotion increment or the
annual increment, not both.

Policy code: HR-COMP-I-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

[S4] Code Of Conduct
# Code of Conduct

## Core Principles
- Act with integrity in all dealings.
- Treat customers, colleagues and partners with respect.
- Protect confidential information and customer data.
- Avoid conflicts of interest; declare them promptly.

## Conflict of Interest
Employees must disclose outside business interests, family relationships with vendors,
and board positions in other entities through the declaration portal annually.

## Reporting Misconduct
Misconduct may be reported to the manager, HR, compliance or the whistleblower channel.
Good-faith reports are protected.

## Consequences
Violations lead to disciplinary action up to and including termination, and may be
reported to regulators where applicable.

Policy code: HR-CC-2026-01 | Owner: Employee Relations team.

[S5] Compensation Review
# Compensation Review Cycle

## Annual Cycle
Compensation review is effective 1 April. Rating inputs from the appraisal close in March
feed the increment matrix published by the Rewards team.

## Market Benchmarking
Every role is benchmarked against the banking sector median using annual market surveys.
Positions below the 25th percentile are prioritised for corrections.

## Increment Drivers
Increment is driven by performance rating, position-in-range and business affordability.
The matrix is approved by the compensation committee.

## Communication
Revised compensation letters are released in June. Any query must be raised through the
HR service portal within 30 days of release.

Policy code: HR-COMP-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

# Provident Fund (PF) & Gratuity — Quick Reference

## Provident Fund
- Contribution: **12% of basic + DA** by the employee, matched by the employer.
- Employer contribution split: 8.33% to EPS (Employee Pension Scheme, capped
  on ₹15,000 basic) + balance to EPF.
- Interest is credited annually as declared by the EPFO.
- Withdrawals: partial withdrawals allowed for defined reasons (marriage,
  higher education, home purchase, medical emergency) subject to service
  tenure thresholds.
- Universal Account Number (UAN) is issued at joining and is portable across
  employers.

## Gratuity
- Payable on separation after continuous service of at least **5 years**
  (waived for death / permanent disability).
- Formula: `(Last drawn basic + DA) × 15 / 26 × completed years of service`.
- Statutory cap: ₹20,00,000 (tax-exempt limit).
- Paid within 30 days of the last working day; delays attract simple interest
  at the notified rate.

## Nomination
Employees must nominate their PF and gratuity beneficiaries within 30 days of
joining and update nominations after any life event (marriage, birth of
child, divorce).

## Related Forms
Download from `Download > HR > Statutory Forms`:
- `PF-NOM-1` — PF nomination
- `GRAT-NOM-2` — Gratuity nomination
- `PF-WD-31` — Partial PF withdrawal

## Policy Code
`HR-STAT-2026-03` · Owner: Employee Services team.

# Certification Reimbursement Policy

## Approved List
Reimbursement applies to certifications on the approved list published annually, such as
CAIIB, CFA, FRM, cloud certifications and role-specific technical certifications.

## Reimbursement Amount
Up to 100 percent of exam fees for certifications on the approved list, capped per grade.
Renewal and membership fees are reimbursed for active certifications.

## Conditions
- Certification must be passed, not merely attempted.
- Employee must be in service on the date of the claim.
- Reimbursement is paid against the fee receipt only.

## Bond

child, divorce).

# Income-Tax Declaration Process

## Declaration Window
Employees declare proposed investments and rent in April-May each financial year.
Declarations drive monthly tax deduction at source (TDS).

## Eligible Heads
- Section 80C: ELSS, PPF, EPF, life insurance, principal on home loan, tuition fees.
- Section 80D: medical insurance premiums.
- House rent allowance exemption under Section 10(13A).
- Home loan interest under Section 24(b).

## Proof Submission
Investment proofs must be uploaded by the first week of January. Shortfalls in proof
lead to tax recovery in February and March payrolls.

## Form 16
Form 16 is issued by 15 June. Part B includes employer-provided details; Part A carries
the TDS certificate.

Policy code: HR-TAX-2026-01 | Owner: Payroll team.

# Process Checklist: Promotion Review

## Entry Point

Start the process from Performance module > Promotion.

## Checklist

1. Confirm eligibility per the policy before starting.

2. Prepare the supporting documents listed in the form.

3. Obtain the required manager or HR approvals.

4. Submit and note the reference number.

5. Track the request and respond to queries within 2 business days.

Missing documents, incomplete fields, or approvals outside the authority matrix.

## SLA

Standard requests complete within 5 business days unless the policy states otherwise.

## Policy code

HR-CHK-PROMO-2026-01 | Owner: HR Operations.

USER QUESTION:
I need guidance on this: what does a rating of 5 mean in the appraisal cycle?

RETRIEVED CONTEXT (cite as [S1], [S2], ...):
[S1] How is the performance appraisal cycle structured?
Q: How is the performance appraisal cycle structured?
A: The appraisal cycle runs from April to March. Goal setting happens in April, mid-year review in September and final review in March-April. Ratings are on a 5-point scale with a normalisation step at the business-unit level.

[S2] Performance Appraisal
# Performance Appraisal Cycle

## Cycle Timeline
| Phase | Window | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Goal setting | 1 Apr – 30 Apr | Employee + reporting manager |
| Mid-year review | 1 Sep – 30 Sep | Employee + reporting manager |
| Self-appraisal | 1 Mar – 15 Mar | Employee |
| Manager appraisal | 16 Mar – 31 Mar | Reporting manager |
| Normalisation | 1 Apr – 15 Apr | Business-unit HRBP |
| Final letters | 20 Apr – 30 Apr | HR Operations |

## Rating Scale
| Rating | Label | Definition |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | Outstanding | Exceptional, sustained impact well beyond role expectations. |
| 4 | Exceeds | Consistently exceeds expectations across most goals. |
| 3 | Meets | Meets all critical expectations. |
| 2 | Partially Meets | Meets some but not all critical expectations. |
| 1 | Below | Below expected performance; performance-improvement plan triggered. |

## Normalisation
- Ratings are normalised at the business-unit level with recommended distribution:
  Outstanding <= 8 %, Exceeds <= 25 %, Meets 55 – 65 %, Partially Meets <= 8 %,
  Below <= 4 %.
- Deviations require CHRO sign-off.

## PIP (Performance Improvement Plan)
- Employees rated `Below` are placed on a 90-day PIP.
- HRBP reviews progress every 30 days.
- Continued rating of `Below` after PIP leads to separation.

## References
- Policy code: HR-PMS-2026-01
- Owner: Talent Management team

[S3] Compensation Review
# Compensation Review Cycle

## Annual Cycle
Compensation review is effective 1 April. Rating inputs from the appraisal close in March
feed the increment matrix published by the Rewards team.

## Market Benchmarking
Every role is benchmarked against the banking sector median using annual market surveys.
Positions below the 25th percentile are prioritised for corrections.

## Increment Drivers
Increment is driven by performance rating, position-in-range and business affordability.
The matrix is approved by the compensation committee.

## Communication
Revised compensation letters are released in June. Any query must be raised through the
HR service portal within 30 days of release.

Policy code: HR-COMP-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

[S4] Annual Increment Cycle
# Annual Increment Cycle

## Timing
The increment cycle runs from April to June. Performance inputs close in March, calibration
in April, and letters are issued in June.

## Eligibility
Employees who joined on or before 31 December of the previous financial year and are not
under a performance improvement plan are eligible.

## Calibration
Ratings are calibrated at business-unit level before increments are computed. Calibration
adjusts rating distribution, never individual compensation directly.

## Promotion During Cycle
Employees promoted in the same cycle receive the higher of the promotion increment or the
annual increment, not both.

Policy code: HR-COMP-I-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

[S5] Promotion Guidelines
# Promotion Guidelines

## Criteria
Promotion requires sustained performance at or above "Exceeds Expectations" for two
consecutive cycles, role readiness and a vacancy or business case at the higher grade.

## Readiness Assessments
For people-manager moves, a manager-readiness assessment and structured panel interview
are mandatory.

## Timing
Promotions are effective 1 April or 1 October. Off-cycle promotions are rare and require
CHRO approval.

## Communication
Promotion decisions are communicated by the manager with HR support. Unsuccessful
candidates receive structured feedback.

Policy code: HR-PROM-2026-01 | Owner: Talent Management team.

# Compensation Review Cycle

## Annual Cycle
Compensation review is effective 1 April. Rating inputs from the appraisal close in March
feed the increment matrix published by the Rewards team.

## Market Benchmarking
Every role is benchmarked against the banking sector median using annual market surveys.
Positions below the 25th percentile are prioritised for corrections.

## Increment Drivers
Increment is driven by performance rating, position-in-range and business affordability.
The matrix is approved by the compensation committee.

## Communication
Revised compensation letters are released in June. Any query must be raised through the
HR service portal within 30 days of release.

Policy code: HR-COMP-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

A: For TDS declaration: submit investment declarations by 15 June and proof documents by 15 January.

| Rating | Label | Definition |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | Outstanding | Exceptional, sustained impact well beyond role expectations. |
| 4 | Exceeds | Consistently exceeds expectations across most goals. |
| 3 | Meets | Meets all critical expectations. |
| 2 | Partially Meets | Meets some but not all critical expectations. |
| 1 | Below | Below expected performance; performance-improvement plan triggered. |

## Normalisation
- Ratings are normalised at the business-unit level with recommended distribution:
  Outstanding <= 8 %, Exceeds <= 25 %, Meets 55 – 65 %, Partially Meets <= 8 %,
  Below <= 4 %.

- Employees rated `Below` are placed on a 90-day PIP.
- HRBP reviews progress every 30 days.

- Owner: Talent Management team
