# Code of Conduct

## Core Principles
- Act with integrity in all dealings.
- Treat customers, colleagues and partners with respect.
- Protect confidential information and customer data.
- Avoid conflicts of interest; declare them promptly.

## Conflict of Interest
Employees must disclose outside business interests, family relationships with vendors,
and board positions in other entities through the declaration portal annually.

## Reporting Misconduct
Misconduct may be reported to the manager, HR, compliance or the whistleblower channel.
Good-faith reports are protected.

## Consequences
Violations lead to disciplinary action up to and including termination, and may be
reported to regulators where applicable.

Policy code: HR-CC-2026-01 | Owner: Employee Relations team.

[S2] Performance Appraisal
# Performance Appraisal Cycle

## Cycle Timeline
| Phase | Window | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Goal setting | 1 Apr – 30 Apr | Employee + reporting manager |
| Mid-year review | 1 Sep – 30 Sep | Employee + reporting manager |
| Self-appraisal | 1 Mar – 15 Mar | Employee |
| Manager appraisal | 16 Mar – 31 Mar | Reporting manager |
| Normalisation | 1 Apr – 15 Apr | Business-unit HRBP |
| Final letters | 20 Apr – 30 Apr | HR Operations |

## Rating Scale
| Rating | Label | Definition |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | Outstanding | Exceptional, sustained impact well beyond role expectations. |
| 4 | Exceeds | Consistently exceeds expectations across most goals. |
| 3 | Meets | Meets all critical expectations. |
| 2 | Partially Meets | Meets some but not all critical expectations. |
| 1 | Below | Below expected performance; performance-improvement plan triggered. |

## Normalisation
- Ratings are normalised at the business-unit level with recommended distribution:
  Outstanding <= 8 %, Exceeds <= 25 %, Meets 55 – 65 %, Partially Meets <= 8 %,
  Below <= 4 %.
- Deviations require CHRO sign-off.

## PIP (Performance Improvement Plan)
- Employees rated `Below` are placed on a 90-day PIP.
- HRBP reviews progress every 30 days.
- Continued rating of `Below` after PIP leads to separation.

## References
- Policy code: HR-PMS-2026-01
- Owner: Talent Management team

[S3] Compensation Review
# Compensation Review Cycle

## Annual Cycle
Compensation review is effective 1 April. Rating inputs from the appraisal close in March
feed the increment matrix published by the Rewards team.

## Market Benchmarking
Every role is benchmarked against the banking sector median using annual market surveys.
Positions below the 25th percentile are prioritised for corrections.

## Increment Drivers
Increment is driven by performance rating, position-in-range and business affordability.
The matrix is approved by the compensation committee.

## Communication
Revised compensation letters are released in June. Any query must be raised through the
HR service portal within 30 days of release.

Policy code: HR-COMP-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

[S4] Annual Increment Cycle
# Annual Increment Cycle

## Timing
The increment cycle runs from April to June. Performance inputs close in March, calibration
in April, and letters are issued in June.

## Eligibility
Employees who joined on or before 31 December of the previous financial year and are not
under a performance improvement plan are eligible.

## Calibration
Ratings are calibrated at business-unit level before increments are computed. Calibration
adjusts rating distribution, never individual compensation directly.

## Promotion During Cycle
Employees promoted in the same cycle receive the higher of the promotion increment or the
annual increment, not both.

Policy code: HR-COMP-I-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

[S5] Variable Pay Policy
# Variable Pay Policy

## Eligibility
Variable pay applies to grades M3 and above. It is paid annually against business, unit
and individual scorecard achievement.

## Payout Formula
Payout = target variable × business multiplier × unit multiplier × individual multiplier.
Multipliers range from 0 to 1.5 as per the approved scorecard.

## Timing
Variable pay for a financial year is paid in June of the following year. Employees who
resign before the payout date are not eligible unless the separation policy states otherwise.

## Disputes
Scorecard disputes must be raised within 30 days of scorecard communication to the
business review committee.

Policy code: HR-COMP-V-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

USER QUESTION:
For my situation, what does a rating of 5 mean in the appraisal cycle? (ref VBLK-0015)

RETRIEVED CONTEXT (cite as [S1], [S2], ...):
[S1] How is the performance appraisal cycle structured?
Q: How is the performance appraisal cycle structured?
A: The appraisal cycle runs from April to March. Goal setting happens in April, mid-year review in September and final review in March-April. Ratings are on a 5-point scale with a normalisation step at the business-unit level.

[S2] Performance Appraisal
# Performance Appraisal Cycle

## Cycle Timeline
| Phase | Window | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Goal setting | 1 Apr – 30 Apr | Employee + reporting manager |
| Mid-year review | 1 Sep – 30 Sep | Employee + reporting manager |
| Self-appraisal | 1 Mar – 15 Mar | Employee |
| Manager appraisal | 16 Mar – 31 Mar | Reporting manager |
| Normalisation | 1 Apr – 15 Apr | Business-unit HRBP |
| Final letters | 20 Apr – 30 Apr | HR Operations |

## Rating Scale
| Rating | Label | Definition |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | Outstanding | Exceptional, sustained impact well beyond role expectations. |
| 4 | Exceeds | Consistently exceeds expectations across most goals. |
| 3 | Meets | Meets all critical expectations. |
| 2 | Partially Meets | Meets some but not all critical expectations. |
| 1 | Below | Below expected performance; performance-improvement plan triggered. |

## Normalisation
- Ratings are normalised at the business-unit level with recommended distribution:
  Outstanding <= 8 %, Exceeds <= 25 %, Meets 55 – 65 %, Partially Meets <= 8 %,
  Below <= 4 %.
- Deviations require CHRO sign-off.

## PIP (Performance Improvement Plan)
- Employees rated `Below` are placed on a 90-day PIP.
- HRBP reviews progress every 30 days.
- Continued rating of `Below` after PIP leads to separation.

## References
- Policy code: HR-PMS-2026-01
- Owner: Talent Management team

[S3] Compensation Review
# Compensation Review Cycle

## Annual Cycle
Compensation review is effective 1 April. Rating inputs from the appraisal close in March
feed the increment matrix published by the Rewards team.

## Market Benchmarking
Every role is benchmarked against the banking sector median using annual market surveys.
Positions below the 25th percentile are prioritised for corrections.

## Increment Drivers
Increment is driven by performance rating, position-in-range and business affordability.
The matrix is approved by the compensation committee.

## Communication
Revised compensation letters are released in June. Any query must be raised through the
HR service portal within 30 days of release.

Policy code: HR-COMP-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

[S4] Annual Increment Cycle
# Annual Increment Cycle

## Timing
The increment cycle runs from April to June. Performance inputs close in March, calibration
in April, and letters are issued in June.

## Eligibility
Employees who joined on or before 31 December of the previous financial year and are not
under a performance improvement plan are eligible.

## Calibration
Ratings are calibrated at business-unit level before increments are computed. Calibration
adjusts rating distribution, never individual compensation directly.

## Promotion During Cycle
Employees promoted in the same cycle receive the higher of the promotion increment or the
annual increment, not both.

Policy code: HR-COMP-I-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

[S5] Variable Pay Policy
# Variable Pay Policy

## Eligibility
Variable pay applies to grades M3 and above. It is paid annually against business, unit
and individual scorecard achievement.

## Payout Formula
Payout = target variable × business multiplier × unit multiplier × individual multiplier.
Multipliers range from 0 to 1.5 as per the approved scorecard.

## Timing
Variable pay for a financial year is paid in June of the following year. Employees who
resign before the payout date are not eligible unless the separation policy states otherwise.

## Disputes
Scorecard disputes must be raised within 30 days of scorecard communication to the
business review committee.

Policy code: HR-COMP-V-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

For my situation, what happens to employees rated Below?

[S1] Performance Appraisal
# Performance Appraisal Cycle

## Cycle Timeline
| Phase | Window | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Goal setting | 1 Apr – 30 Apr | Employee + reporting manager |
| Mid-year review | 1 Sep – 30 Sep | Employee + reporting manager |
| Self-appraisal | 1 Mar – 15 Mar | Employee |
| Manager appraisal | 16 Mar – 31 Mar | Reporting manager |
| Normalisation | 1 Apr – 15 Apr | Business-unit HRBP |
| Final letters | 20 Apr – 30 Apr | HR Operations |

## Rating Scale
| Rating | Label | Definition |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | Outstanding | Exceptional, sustained impact well beyond role expectations. |
| 4 | Exceeds | Consistently exceeds expectations across most goals. |
| 3 | Meets | Meets all critical expectations. |
| 2 | Partially Meets | Meets some but not all critical expectations. |
| 1 | Below | Below expected performance; performance-improvement plan triggered. |

## Normalisation
- Ratings are normalised at the business-unit level with recommended distribution:
  Outstanding <= 8 %, Exceeds <= 25 %, Meets 55 – 65 %, Partially Meets <= 8 %,
  Below <= 4 %.
- Deviations require CHRO sign-off.

## PIP (Performance Improvement Plan)
- Employees rated `Below` are placed on a 90-day PIP.
- HRBP reviews progress every 30 days.
- Continued rating of `Below` after PIP leads to separation.

## References
- Policy code: HR-PMS-2026-01
- Owner: Talent Management team

[S2] Code Of Conduct
# Code of Conduct

## Core Principles
- Act with integrity in all dealings.
- Treat customers, colleagues and partners with respect.
- Protect confidential information and customer data.
- Avoid conflicts of interest; declare them promptly.

## Conflict of Interest
Employees must disclose outside business interests, family relationships with vendors,
and board positions in other entities through the declaration portal annually.

## Reporting Misconduct
Misconduct may be reported to the manager, HR, compliance or the whistleblower channel.
Good-faith reports are protected.

## Consequences
Violations lead to disciplinary action up to and including termination, and may be
reported to regulators where applicable.

Policy code: HR-CC-2026-01 | Owner: Employee Relations team.

[S3] Variable Pay Policy
# Variable Pay Policy

## Eligibility
Variable pay applies to grades M3 and above. It is paid annually against business, unit
and individual scorecard achievement.

## Payout Formula
Payout = target variable × business multiplier × unit multiplier × individual multiplier.
Multipliers range from 0 to 1.5 as per the approved scorecard.

## Timing
Variable pay for a financial year is paid in June of the following year. Employees who
resign before the payout date are not eligible unless the separation policy states otherwise.

## Disputes
Scorecard disputes must be raised within 30 days of scorecard communication to the
business review committee.

Policy code: HR-COMP-V-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

[S4] Annual Increment Cycle
# Annual Increment Cycle

## Timing
The increment cycle runs from April to June. Performance inputs close in March, calibration
in April, and letters are issued in June.

## Eligibility
Employees who joined on or before 31 December of the previous financial year and are not
under a performance improvement plan are eligible.

## Calibration
Ratings are calibrated at business-unit level before increments are computed. Calibration
adjusts rating distribution, never individual compensation directly.

## Promotion During Cycle
Employees promoted in the same cycle receive the higher of the promotion increment or the
annual increment, not both.

Policy code: HR-COMP-I-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

[S5] Compensation Review
# Compensation Review Cycle

## Annual Cycle
Compensation review is effective 1 April. Rating inputs from the appraisal close in March
feed the increment matrix published by the Rewards team.

## Market Benchmarking
Every role is benchmarked against the banking sector median using annual market surveys.
Positions below the 25th percentile are prioritised for corrections.

## Increment Drivers
Increment is driven by performance rating, position-in-range and business affordability.
The matrix is approved by the compensation committee.

## Communication
Revised compensation letters are released in June. Any query must be raised through the
HR service portal within 30 days of release.

Policy code: HR-COMP-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

[S1] Performance Appraisal
# Performance Appraisal Cycle

## Cycle Timeline
| Phase | Window | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Goal setting | 1 Apr – 30 Apr | Employee + reporting manager |
| Mid-year review | 1 Sep – 30 Sep | Employee + reporting manager |
| Self-appraisal | 1 Mar – 15 Mar | Employee |
| Manager appraisal | 16 Mar – 31 Mar | Reporting manager |
| Normalisation | 1 Apr – 15 Apr | Business-unit HRBP |
| Final letters | 20 Apr – 30 Apr | HR Operations |

## Rating Scale
| Rating | Label | Definition |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | Outstanding | Exceptional, sustained impact well beyond role expectations. |
| 4 | Exceeds | Consistently exceeds expectations across most goals. |
| 3 | Meets | Meets all critical expectations. |
| 2 | Partially Meets | Meets some but not all critical expectations. |
| 1 | Below | Below expected performance; performance-improvement plan triggered. |

## Normalisation
- Ratings are normalised at the business-unit level with recommended distribution:
  Outstanding <= 8 %, Exceeds <= 25 %, Meets 55 – 65 %, Partially Meets <= 8 %,
  Below <= 4 %.
- Deviations require CHRO sign-off.

## PIP (Performance Improvement Plan)
- Employees rated `Below` are placed on a 90-day PIP.
- HRBP reviews progress every 30 days.
- Continued rating of `Below` after PIP leads to separation.

## References
- Policy code: HR-PMS-2026-01
- Owner: Talent Management team

[S2] Code Of Conduct
# Code of Conduct

## Core Principles
- Act with integrity in all dealings.
- Treat customers, colleagues and partners with respect.
- Protect confidential information and customer data.
- Avoid conflicts of interest; declare them promptly.

## Conflict of Interest
Employees must disclose outside business interests, family relationships with vendors,
and board positions in other entities through the declaration portal annually.

## Reporting Misconduct
Misconduct may be reported to the manager, HR, compliance or the whistleblower channel.
Good-faith reports are protected.

## Consequences
Violations lead to disciplinary action up to and including termination, and may be
reported to regulators where applicable.

Policy code: HR-CC-2026-01 | Owner: Employee Relations team.

[S3] Variable Pay Policy
# Variable Pay Policy

## Eligibility
Variable pay applies to grades M3 and above. It is paid annually against business, unit
and individual scorecard achievement.

## Payout Formula
Payout = target variable × business multiplier × unit multiplier × individual multiplier.
Multipliers range from 0 to 1.5 as per the approved scorecard.

## Timing
Variable pay for a financial year is paid in June of the following year. Employees who
resign before the payout date are not eligible unless the separation policy states otherwise.

## Disputes
Scorecard disputes must be raised within 30 days of scorecard communication to the
business review committee.

Policy code: HR-COMP-V-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

[S4] Annual Increment Cycle
# Annual Increment Cycle

## Timing
The increment cycle runs from April to June. Performance inputs close in March, calibration
in April, and letters are issued in June.

## Eligibility
Employees who joined on or before 31 December of the previous financial year and are not
under a performance improvement plan are eligible.

## Calibration
Ratings are calibrated at business-unit level before increments are computed. Calibration
adjusts rating distribution, never individual compensation directly.

## Promotion During Cycle
Employees promoted in the same cycle receive the higher of the promotion increment or the
annual increment, not both.

Policy code: HR-COMP-I-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

[S5] Compensation Review
# Compensation Review Cycle

## Annual Cycle
Compensation review is effective 1 April. Rating inputs from the appraisal close in March
feed the increment matrix published by the Rewards team.

## Market Benchmarking
Every role is benchmarked against the banking sector median using annual market surveys.
Positions below the 25th percentile are prioritised for corrections.

## Increment Drivers
Increment is driven by performance rating, position-in-range and business affordability.
The matrix is approved by the compensation committee.

## Communication
Revised compensation letters are released in June. Any query must be raised through the
HR service portal within 30 days of release.

Policy code: HR-COMP-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

# Provident Fund (PF) & Gratuity — Quick Reference

## Provident Fund
- Contribution: **12% of basic + DA** by the employee, matched by the employer.
- Employer contribution split: 8.33% to EPS (Employee Pension Scheme, capped
  on ₹15,000 basic) + balance to EPF.
- Interest is credited annually as declared by the EPFO.
- Withdrawals: partial withdrawals allowed for defined reasons (marriage,
  higher education, home purchase, medical emergency) subject to service
  tenure thresholds.
- Universal Account Number (UAN) is issued at joining and is portable across
  employers.

## Gratuity
- Payable on separation after continuous service of at least **5 years**
  (waived for death / permanent disability).
- Formula: `(Last drawn basic + DA) × 15 / 26 × completed years of service`.
- Statutory cap: ₹20,00,000 (tax-exempt limit).
- Paid within 30 days of the last working day; delays attract simple interest
  at the notified rate.

## Nomination
Employees must nominate their PF and gratuity beneficiaries within 30 days of
joining and update nominations after any life event (marriage, birth of
child, divorce).

## Related Forms
Download from `Download > HR > Statutory Forms`:
- `PF-NOM-1` — PF nomination
- `GRAT-NOM-2` — Gratuity nomination
- `PF-WD-31` — Partial PF withdrawal

## Reimbursement Amount
Up to 100 percent of exam fees for certifications on the approved list, capped per grade.
Renewal and membership fees are reimbursed for active certifications.

## Conditions
- Certification must be passed, not merely attempted.
- Employee must be in service on the date of the claim.
- Reimbursement is paid against the fee receipt only.

## Bond
For certifications above the cap threshold, a service commitment of 12 months applies.
Early exit triggers pro-rata recovery.

[S2] How is the performance appraisal cycle structured?
Q: How is the performance appraisal cycle structured?
A: The appraisal cycle runs from April to March. Goal setting happens in April, mid-year review in September and final review in March-April. Ratings are on a 5-point scale with a normalisation step at the business-unit level.

[S3] Compensation Review
# Compensation Review Cycle

## Annual Cycle
Compensation review is effective 1 April. Rating inputs from the appraisal close in March
feed the increment matrix published by the Rewards team.

## Market Benchmarking
Every role is benchmarked against the banking sector median using annual market surveys.
Positions below the 25th percentile are prioritised for corrections.

## Increment Drivers
Increment is driven by performance rating, position-in-range and business affordability.
The matrix is approved by the compensation committee.

## Communication
Revised compensation letters are released in June. Any query must be raised through the
HR service portal within 30 days of release.

Policy code: HR-COMP-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

[S4] Tax Declaration Process
# Income-Tax Declaration Process

## Declaration Window
Employees declare proposed investments and rent in April-May each financial year.
Declarations drive monthly tax deduction at source (TDS).

## Eligible Heads
- Section 80C: ELSS, PPF, EPF, life insurance, principal on home loan, tuition fees.
- Section 80D: medical insurance premiums.
- House rent allowance exemption under Section 10(13A).
- Home loan interest under Section 24(b).

## Proof Submission
Investment proofs must be uploaded by the first week of January. Shortfalls in proof
lead to tax recovery in February and March payrolls.

## Form 16
Form 16 is issued by 15 June. Part B includes employer-provided details; Part A carries
the TDS certificate.

Policy code: HR-TAX-2026-01 | Owner: Payroll team.

USER QUESTION:
What does a rating of 5 mean in the appraisal cycle? (ref VBLK-0016)

RETRIEVED CONTEXT (cite as [S1], [S2], ...):
[S1] How is the performance appraisal cycle structured?
Q: How is the performance appraisal cycle structured?
A: The appraisal cycle runs from April to March. Goal setting happens in April, mid-year review in September and final review in March-April. Ratings are on a 5-point scale with a normalisation step at the business-unit level.

[S2] Performance Appraisal
# Performance Appraisal Cycle

## Cycle Timeline
| Phase | Window | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Goal setting | 1 Apr – 30 Apr | Employee + reporting manager |
| Mid-year review | 1 Sep – 30 Sep | Employee + reporting manager |
| Self-appraisal | 1 Mar – 15 Mar | Employee |
| Manager appraisal | 16 Mar – 31 Mar | Reporting manager |
| Normalisation | 1 Apr – 15 Apr | Business-unit HRBP |
| Final letters | 20 Apr – 30 Apr | HR Operations |

## Rating Scale
| Rating | Label | Definition |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | Outstanding | Exceptional, sustained impact well beyond role expectations. |
| 4 | Exceeds | Consistently exceeds expectations across most goals. |
| 3 | Meets | Meets all critical expectations. |
| 2 | Partially Meets | Meets some but not all critical expectations. |
| 1 | Below | Below expected performance; performance-improvement plan triggered. |

## Normalisation
- Ratings are normalised at the business-unit level with recommended distribution:
  Outstanding <= 8 %, Exceeds <= 25 %, Meets 55 – 65 %, Partially Meets <= 8 %,
  Below <= 4 %.
- Deviations require CHRO sign-off.

## PIP (Performance Improvement Plan)
- Employees rated `Below` are placed on a 90-day PIP.
- HRBP reviews progress every 30 days.
- Continued rating of `Below` after PIP leads to separation.

## References
- Policy code: HR-PMS-2026-01
- Owner: Talent Management team

[S3] Compensation Review
# Compensation Review Cycle

## Annual Cycle
Compensation review is effective 1 April. Rating inputs from the appraisal close in March
feed the increment matrix published by the Rewards team.

## Market Benchmarking
Every role is benchmarked against the banking sector median using annual market surveys.
Positions below the 25th percentile are prioritised for corrections.

## Increment Drivers
Increment is driven by performance rating, position-in-range and business affordability.
The matrix is approved by the compensation committee.

## Communication
Revised compensation letters are released in June. Any query must be raised through the
HR service portal within 30 days of release.

Policy code: HR-COMP-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

[S4] Annual Increment Cycle
# Annual Increment Cycle

## Timing
The increment cycle runs from April to June. Performance inputs close in March, calibration
in April, and letters are issued in June.

## Eligibility
Employees who joined on or before 31 December of the previous financial year and are not
under a performance improvement plan are eligible.

## Calibration
Ratings are calibrated at business-unit level before increments are computed. Calibration
adjusts rating distribution, never individual compensation directly.

## Promotion During Cycle
Employees promoted in the same cycle receive the higher of the promotion increment or the
annual increment, not both.

Policy code: HR-COMP-I-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

[S5] Promotion Guidelines
# Promotion Guidelines

## Criteria
Promotion requires sustained performance at or above "Exceeds Expectations" for two
consecutive cycles, role readiness and a vacancy or business case at the higher grade.

## Readiness Assessments
For people-manager moves, a manager-readiness assessment and structured panel interview
are mandatory.

## Timing
Promotions are effective 1 April or 1 October. Off-cycle promotions are rare and require
CHRO approval.

## Communication
Promotion decisions are communicated by the manager with HR support. Unsuccessful
candidates receive structured feedback.

Policy code: HR-PROM-2026-01 | Owner: Talent Management team.

# Provident Fund (PF) & Gratuity — Quick Reference

## Provident Fund
- Contribution: **12% of basic + DA** by the employee, matched by the employer.
- Employer contribution split: 8.33% to EPS (Employee Pension Scheme, capped
  on ₹15,000 basic) + balance to EPF.
- Interest is credited annually as declared by the EPFO.
- Withdrawals: partial withdrawals allowed for defined reasons (marriage,
  higher education, home purchase, medical emergency) subject to service
  tenure thresholds.
- Universal Account Number (UAN) is issued at joining and is portable across
  employers.

## Gratuity
- Payable on separation after continuous service of at least **5 years**
  (waived for death / permanent disability).
- Formula: `(Last drawn basic + DA) × 15 / 26 × completed years of service`.
- Statutory cap: ₹20,00,000 (tax-exempt limit).
- Paid within 30 days of the last working day; delays attract simple interest
  at the notified rate.

## Nomination
Employees must nominate their PF and gratuity beneficiaries within 30 days of
joining and update nominations after any life event (marriage, birth of
child, divorce).

## Related Forms
Download from `Download > HR > Statutory Forms`:
- `PF-NOM-1` — PF nomination
- `GRAT-NOM-2` — Gratuity nomination
- `PF-WD-31` — Partial PF withdrawal

Q: How does PF contribution work?
A: For PF contribution: 12 percent of basic pay is contributed by both employer and employee; the UAN is on the payslip.

[S3] Where can I verify PF contribution?
Q: Where can I verify PF contribution?
A: Check the HR portal under Pay & Benefits; supporting details appear on the payslip.

[S4] How much can I claim under books and learning reimbursement?
Q: How much can I claim under books and learning reimbursement?
A: The limit for books and learning reimbursement is INR 5,000 per year.

[S5] Who should I contact about PF contribution?
Q: Who should I contact about PF contribution?
A: Use the payroll helpdesk in the HR portal; the SLA is 2 business days.

# Salary Advance Policy

## Eligibility
Salary advance is available for genuine emergencies after six months of service. Maximum
advance is one month's net salary.

## Repayment
The advance is recovered over three payrolls by default, or a shorter period agreed in
writing. Recovery cannot reduce take-home below statutory minimums.

## Approval
Advances require reporting-manager and HRBP approval.

Q: What is the eligibility for gratuity?
A: Gratuity is payable after 5 years of continuous service, waived on death or permanent disability. The formula is (last drawn basic + DA) x 15 / 26 x completed years. Statutory tax-exempt cap is INR 20 lakh.

[S2] Retirement And Superannuation
# Retirement & Superannuation

## Retirement Age
Superannuation is at 60 years. Extensions may be offered for identified specialists in
one-year increments up to age 62, approved by the CHRO.

## Pension and Provident Fund
Statutory provident fund and pension scheme benefits are settled as per EPFO rules on
superannuation.

## Gratuity
Gratuity is payable as per the Payment of Gratuity Act on superannuation without the
five-year minimum service condition.

## Transition Support
A pre-retirement counselling session and benefits orientation are offered in the final
year of service.

Policy code: HR-RET-2026-01 | Owner: Benefits team.

[S3] Pf Gratuity
# Provident Fund (PF) & Gratuity — Quick Reference

## Provident Fund
- Contribution: **12% of basic + DA** by the employee, matched by the employer.
- Employer contribution split: 8.33% to EPS (Employee Pension Scheme, capped
  on ₹15,000 basic) + balance to EPF.
- Interest is credited annually as declared by the EPFO.
- Withdrawals: partial withdrawals allowed for defined reasons (marriage,
  higher education, home purchase, medical emergency) subject to service
  tenure thresholds.
- Universal Account Number (UAN) is issued at joining and is portable across
  employers.

## Gratuity
- Payable on separation after continuous service of at least **5 years**
  (waived for death / permanent disability).
- Formula: `(Last drawn basic + DA) × 15 / 26 × completed years of service`.
- Statutory cap: ₹20,00,000 (tax-exempt limit).
- Paid within 30 days of the last working day; delays attract simple interest
  at the notified rate.

## Nomination
Employees must nominate their PF and gratuity beneficiaries within 30 days of
joining and update nominations after any life event (marriage, birth of
child, divorce).

## Related Forms
Download from `Download > HR > Statutory Forms`:
- `PF-NOM-1` — PF nomination
- `GRAT-NOM-2` — Gratuity nomination
- `PF-WD-31` — Partial PF withdrawal

advance is one month's net salary.

## Repayment
The advance is recovered over three payrolls by default, or a shorter period agreed in
writing. Recovery cannot reduce take-home below statutory minimums.

## Approval
Advances require reporting-manager and HRBP approval. A second advance is not sanctioned
while a previous one is outstanding.

## Documentation
Supporting documentation of the emergency is required for advances above 50 percent of
net salary.

Policy code: HR-PAY-A-2026-01 | Owner: Payroll team.

[S5] Joining And Retention Bonus
# Joining & Retention Bonus

## Joining Bonus
Joining bonuses are limited to niche skills and candidate-negotiated cases approved by the
business head and Rewards. Payment is with the first payroll.

## Retention Bonus
Retention bonuses are paid in milestone tranches against a written retention agreement
approved by the business head and HR.

## Recovery
Joining bonuses are recovered in full if the employee leaves within 12 months. Retention
bonuses are recovered pro-rata for the unserved period of the agreement.

## Documentation
Every bonus must have a signed agreement recording amount, conditions and recovery terms.

Policy code: HR-COMP-B-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

# Provident Fund (PF) & Gratuity — Quick Reference

## Provident Fund
- Contribution: **12% of basic + DA** by the employee, matched by the employer.
- Employer contribution split: 8.33% to EPS (Employee Pension Scheme, capped
  on ₹15,000 basic) + balance to EPF.
- Interest is credited annually as declared by the EPFO.
- Withdrawals: partial withdrawals allowed for defined reasons (marriage,
  higher education, home purchase, medical emergency) subject to service
  tenure thresholds.
- Universal Account Number (UAN) is issued at joining and is portable across
  employers.

## Gratuity
- Payable on separation after continuous service of at least **5 years**
  (waived for death / permanent disability).
- Formula: `(Last drawn basic + DA) × 15 / 26 × completed years of service`.
- Statutory cap: ₹20,00,000 (tax-exempt limit).
- Paid within 30 days of the last working day; delays attract simple interest
  at the notified rate.

## Nomination
Employees must nominate their PF and gratuity beneficiaries within 30 days of
joining and update nominations after any life event (marriage, birth of
child, divorce).

## Related Forms
Download from `Download > HR > Statutory Forms`:
- `PF-NOM-1` — PF nomination
- `GRAT-NOM-2` — Gratuity nomination
- `PF-WD-31` — Partial PF withdrawal

# Retirement & Superannuation

## Retirement Age
Superannuation is at 60 years. Extensions may be offered for identified specialists in
one-year increments up to age 62, approved by the CHRO.

## Pension and Provident Fund
Statutory provident fund and pension scheme benefits are settled as per EPFO rules on
superannuation.

## Gratuity
Gratuity is payable as per the Payment of Gratuity Act on superannuation without the
five-year minimum service condition.

## Transition Support
A pre-retirement counselling session and benefits orientation are offered in the final
year of service.

Policy code: HR-RET-2026-01 | Owner: Benefits team.

[S4] Variable Pay Policy
# Variable Pay Policy

## Eligibility
Variable pay applies to grades M3 and above. It is paid annually against business, unit
and individual scorecard achievement.

## Payout Formula
Payout = target variable × business multiplier × unit multiplier × individual multiplier.
Multipliers range from 0 to 1.5 as per the approved scorecard.

## Timing
Variable pay for a financial year is paid in June of the following year. Employees who
resign before the payout date are not eligible unless the separation policy states otherwise.

## Disputes
Scorecard disputes must be raised within 30 days of scorecard communication to the
business review committee.

Policy code: HR-COMP-V-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

# Provident Fund (PF) & Gratuity — Quick Reference

## Provident Fund
- Contribution: **12% of basic + DA** by the employee, matched by the employer.
- Employer contribution split: 8.33% to EPS (Employee Pension Scheme, capped
  on ₹15,000 basic) + balance to EPF.
- Interest is credited annually as declared by the EPFO.
- Withdrawals: partial withdrawals allowed for defined reasons (marriage,
  higher education, home purchase, medical emergency) subject to service
  tenure thresholds.
- Universal Account Number (UAN) is issued at joining and is portable across
  employers.

## Gratuity
- Payable on separation after continuous service of at least **5 years**
  (waived for death / permanent disability).
- Formula: `(Last drawn basic + DA) × 15 / 26 × completed years of service`.
- Statutory cap: ₹20,00,000 (tax-exempt limit).
- Paid within 30 days of the last working day; delays attract simple interest
  at the notified rate.

## Nomination
Employees must nominate their PF and gratuity beneficiaries within 30 days of
joining and update nominations after any life event (marriage, birth of
child, divorce).

## Related Forms
Download from `Download > HR > Statutory Forms`:
- `PF-NOM-1` — PF nomination
- `GRAT-NOM-2` — Gratuity nomination
- `PF-WD-31` — Partial PF withdrawal

## Policy Code
`HR-STAT-2026-03` · Owner: Employee Services team.

[S2] How does PF contribution work?
Q: How does PF contribution work?
A: For PF contribution: 12 percent of basic pay is contributed by both employer and employee; the UAN is on the payslip.

[S3] Where can I verify PF contribution?
Q: Where can I verify PF contribution?
A: Check the HR portal under Pay & Benefits; supporting details appear on the payslip.

[S4] How much can I claim under books and learning reimbursement?
Q: How much can I claim under books and learning reimbursement?
A: The limit for books and learning reimbursement is INR 5,000 per year.

[S5] Who should I contact about PF contribution?
Q: Who should I contact about PF contribution?
A: Use the payroll helpdesk in the HR portal; the SLA is 2 business days.

USER QUESTION:
I need guidance on this: after how many years of service is gratuity payable?

RETRIEVED CONTEXT (cite as [S1], [S2], ...):
[S1] What is the eligibility for gratuity?
Q: What is the eligibility for gratuity?
A: Gratuity is payable after 5 years of continuous service, waived on death or permanent disability. The formula is (last drawn basic + DA) x 15 / 26 x completed years. Statutory tax-exempt cap is INR 20 lakh.

[S2] Retirement And Superannuation
# Retirement & Superannuation

## Retirement Age
Superannuation is at 60 years. Extensions may be offered for identified specialists in
one-year increments up to age 62, approved by the CHRO.

## Pension and Provident Fund
Statutory provident fund and pension scheme benefits are settled as per EPFO rules on
superannuation.

## Gratuity
Gratuity is payable as per the Payment of Gratuity Act on superannuation without the
five-year minimum service condition.

## Transition Support
A pre-retirement counselling session and benefits orientation are offered in the final
year of service.

Policy code: HR-RET-2026-01 | Owner: Benefits team.

[S3] Pf Gratuity
# Provident Fund (PF) & Gratuity — Quick Reference

## Provident Fund
- Contribution: **12% of basic + DA** by the employee, matched by the employer.
- Employer contribution split: 8.33% to EPS (Employee Pension Scheme, capped
  on ₹15,000 basic) + balance to EPF.
- Interest is credited annually as declared by the EPFO.
- Withdrawals: partial withdrawals allowed for defined reasons (marriage,
  higher education, home purchase, medical emergency) subject to service
  tenure thresholds.
- Universal Account Number (UAN) is issued at joining and is portable across
  employers.

## Gratuity
- Payable on separation after continuous service of at least **5 years**
  (waived for death / permanent disability).
- Formula: `(Last drawn basic + DA) × 15 / 26 × completed years of service`.
- Statutory cap: ₹20,00,000 (tax-exempt limit).
- Paid within 30 days of the last working day; delays attract simple interest
  at the notified rate.

## Nomination
Employees must nominate their PF and gratuity beneficiaries within 30 days of
joining and update nominations after any life event (marriage, birth of
child, divorce).

## Related Forms
Download from `Download > HR > Statutory Forms`:
- `PF-NOM-1` — PF nomination
- `GRAT-NOM-2` — Gratuity nomination
- `PF-WD-31` — Partial PF withdrawal

## Policy Code
`HR-STAT-2026-03` · Owner: Employee Services team.

[S4] Salary Advance Policy
# Salary Advance Policy

## Eligibility
Salary advance is available for genuine emergencies after six months of service. Maximum
advance is one month's net salary.

## Repayment
The advance is recovered over three payrolls by default, or a shorter period agreed in
writing. Recovery cannot reduce take-home below statutory minimums.

## Approval
Advances require reporting-manager and HRBP approval. A second advance is not sanctioned
while a previous one is outstanding.

## Documentation
Supporting documentation of the emergency is required for advances above 50 percent of
net salary.

Policy code: HR-PAY-A-2026-01 | Owner: Payroll team.

[S5] Joining And Retention Bonus
# Joining & Retention Bonus

## Joining Bonus
Joining bonuses are limited to niche skills and candidate-negotiated cases approved by the
business head and Rewards. Payment is with the first payroll.

## Retention Bonus
Retention bonuses are paid in milestone tranches against a written retention agreement
approved by the business head and HR.

## Recovery
Joining bonuses are recovered in full if the employee leaves within 12 months. Retention
bonuses are recovered pro-rata for the unserved period of the agreement.

## Documentation
Every bonus must have a signed agreement recording amount, conditions and recovery terms.

Policy code: HR-COMP-B-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

ASSISTANT: 12% of basic + DA is contributed by the employee and matched by the employer.

[S2] Pf Gratuity
# Provident Fund (PF) & Gratuity — Quick Reference

## Provident Fund
- Contribution: **12% of basic + DA** by the employee, matched by the employer.
- Employer contribution split: 8.33% to EPS (Employee Pension Scheme, capped
  on ₹15,000 basic) + balance to EPF.
- Interest is credited annually as declared by the EPFO.
- Withdrawals: partial withdrawals allowed for defined reasons (marriage,
  higher education, home purchase, medical emergency) subject to service
  tenure thresholds.
- Universal Account Number (UAN) is issued at joining and is portable across
  employers.

## Gratuity
- Payable on separation after continuous service of at least **5 years**
  (waived for death / permanent disability).
- Formula: `(Last drawn basic + DA) × 15 / 26 × completed years of service`.
- Statutory cap: ₹20,00,000 (tax-exempt limit).
- Paid within 30 days of the last working day; delays attract simple interest
  at the notified rate.

## Nomination
Employees must nominate their PF and gratuity beneficiaries within 30 days of
joining and update nominations after any life event (marriage, birth of
child, divorce).

## Related Forms
Download from `Download > HR > Statutory Forms`:
- `PF-NOM-1` — PF nomination
- `GRAT-NOM-2` — Gratuity nomination
- `PF-WD-31` — Partial PF withdrawal

year of service.

[S1] Pf Gratuity
# Provident Fund (PF) & Gratuity — Quick Reference

## Provident Fund
- Contribution: **12% of basic + DA** by the employee, matched by the employer.
- Employer contribution split: 8.33% to EPS (Employee Pension Scheme, capped
  on ₹15,000 basic) + balance to EPF.
- Interest is credited annually as declared by the EPFO.
- Withdrawals: partial withdrawals allowed for defined reasons (marriage,
  higher education, home purchase, medical emergency) subject to service
  tenure thresholds.
- Universal Account Number (UAN) is issued at joining and is portable across
  employers.

## Gratuity
- Payable on separation after continuous service of at least **5 years**
  (waived for death / permanent disability).
- Formula: `(Last drawn basic + DA) × 15 / 26 × completed years of service`.
- Statutory cap: ₹20,00,000 (tax-exempt limit).
- Paid within 30 days of the last working day; delays attract simple interest
  at the notified rate.

## Nomination
Employees must nominate their PF and gratuity beneficiaries within 30 days of
joining and update nominations after any life event (marriage, birth of
child, divorce).

## Related Forms
Download from `Download > HR > Statutory Forms`:
- `PF-NOM-1` — PF nomination
- `GRAT-NOM-2` — Gratuity nomination
- `PF-WD-31` — Partial PF withdrawal

## Policy Code
`HR-STAT-2026-03` · Owner: Employee Services team.

[S2] Who should I contact about PF contribution?
Q: Who should I contact about PF contribution?
A: Use the payroll helpdesk in the HR portal; the SLA is 2 business days.

[S3] What is the eligibility for gratuity?
Q: What is the eligibility for gratuity?
A: Gratuity is payable after 5 years of continuous service, waived on death or permanent disability. The formula is (last drawn basic + DA) x 15 / 26 x completed years. Statutory tax-exempt cap is INR 20 lakh.

[S4] Retirement And Superannuation
# Retirement & Superannuation

## Retirement Age
Superannuation is at 60 years. Extensions may be offered for identified specialists in
one-year increments up to age 62, approved by the CHRO.

## Pension and Provident Fund
Statutory provident fund and pension scheme benefits are settled as per EPFO rules on
superannuation.

## Gratuity
Gratuity is payable as per the Payment of Gratuity Act on superannuation without the
five-year minimum service condition.

## Transition Support
A pre-retirement counselling session and benefits orientation are offered in the final
year of service.

Policy code: HR-RET-2026-01 | Owner: Benefits team.

[S5] Employee Referral Program
# Employee Referral Programme

## Eligibility
All permanent employees except HR recruiters and the hiring manager for the specific role
may refer candidates. Referrals must be registered in the referral portal before application.

## Reward Structure
Referral rewards are paid in two instalments: 50 percent on joining and 50 percent after
the referred employee completes six months. Senior and niche roles carry higher rewards as
published in the quarterly referral bulletin.

## Clawback
Rewards are clawed back if the referred employee exits within six months or if the referral
is found to violate the anti-nepotism policy.

## Referral Process
1. Register the candidate in the referral portal.
2. Candidate is tagged to the employee for 180 days.
3. On selection, the referral bonus is processed automatically.

Policy code: HR-REF-2026-01 | Owner: Talent Acquisition team.

- Contribution: **12% of basic + DA** by the employee, matched by the employer.
- Employer contribution split: 8.33% to EPS (Employee Pension Scheme, capped
  on ₹15,000 basic) + balance to EPF.
- Interest is credited annually as declared by the EPFO.
- Withdrawals: partial withdrawals allowed for defined reasons (marriage,
  higher education, home purchase, medical emergency) subject to service
  tenure thresholds.
- Universal Account Number (UAN) is issued at joining and is portable across
  employers.

## Gratuity
- Payable on separation after continuous service of at least **5 years**
  (waived for death / permanent disability).
- Formula: `(Last drawn basic + DA) × 15 / 26 × completed years of service`.
- Statutory cap: ₹20,00,000 (tax-exempt limit).
- Paid within 30 days of the last working day; delays attract simple interest
  at the notified rate.

## Nomination
Employees must nominate their PF and gratuity beneficiaries within 30 days of
joining and update nominations after any life event (marriage, birth of
child, divorce).

## Related Forms
Download from `Download > HR > Statutory Forms`:
- `PF-NOM-1` — PF nomination
- `GRAT-NOM-2` — Gratuity nomination
- `PF-WD-31` — Partial PF withdrawal

## Policy Code
`HR-STAT-2026-03` · Owner: Employee Services team.

[S2] Who should I contact about PF contribution?
Q: Who should I contact about PF contribution?
A: Use the payroll helpdesk in the HR portal; the SLA is 2 business days.

[S3] What is the eligibility for gratuity?
Q: What is the eligibility for gratuity?
A: Gratuity is payable after 5 years of continuous service, waived on death or permanent disability. The formula is (last drawn basic + DA) x 15 / 26 x completed years. Statutory tax-exempt cap is INR 20 lakh.

[S4] Retirement And Superannuation
# Retirement & Superannuation

## Retirement Age
Superannuation is at 60 years. Extensions may be offered for identified specialists in
one-year increments up to age 62, approved by the CHRO.

## Pension and Provident Fund
Statutory provident fund and pension scheme benefits are settled as per EPFO rules on
superannuation.

## Gratuity
Gratuity is payable as per the Payment of Gratuity Act on superannuation without the
five-year minimum service condition.

## Transition Support
A pre-retirement counselling session and benefits orientation are offered in the final
year of service.

Policy code: HR-RET-2026-01 | Owner: Benefits team.

[S5] Employee Referral Program
# Employee Referral Programme

## Eligibility
All permanent employees except HR recruiters and the hiring manager for the specific role
may refer candidates. Referrals must be registered in the referral portal before application.

## Reward Structure
Referral rewards are paid in two instalments: 50 percent on joining and 50 percent after
the referred employee completes six months. Senior and niche roles carry higher rewards as
published in the quarterly referral bulletin.

## Clawback
Rewards are clawed back if the referred employee exits within six months or if the referral
is found to violate the anti-nepotism policy.

## Referral Process
1. Register the candidate in the referral portal.
2. Candidate is tagged to the employee for 180 days.
3. On selection, the referral bonus is processed automatically.

Policy code: HR-REF-2026-01 | Owner: Talent Acquisition team.

[S2] Retirement And Superannuation
# Retirement & Superannuation

## Retirement Age
Superannuation is at 60 years. Extensions may be offered for identified specialists in
one-year increments up to age 62, approved by the CHRO.

## Pension and Provident Fund
Statutory provident fund and pension scheme benefits are settled as per EPFO rules on
superannuation.

## Gratuity
Gratuity is payable as per the Payment of Gratuity Act on superannuation without the
five-year minimum service condition.

## Transition Support
A pre-retirement counselling session and benefits orientation are offered in the final
year of service.

Policy code: HR-RET-2026-01 | Owner: Benefits team.

[S3] Pf Gratuity
# Provident Fund (PF) & Gratuity — Quick Reference

## Provident Fund
- Contribution: **12% of basic + DA** by the employee, matched by the employer.
- Employer contribution split: 8.33% to EPS (Employee Pension Scheme, capped
  on ₹15,000 basic) + balance to EPF.
- Interest is credited annually as declared by the EPFO.
- Withdrawals: partial withdrawals allowed for defined reasons (marriage,
  higher education, home purchase, medical emergency) subject to service
  tenure thresholds.
- Universal Account Number (UAN) is issued at joining and is portable across
  employers.

## Gratuity
- Payable on separation after continuous service of at least **5 years**
  (waived for death / permanent disability).
- Formula: `(Last drawn basic + DA) × 15 / 26 × completed years of service`.
- Statutory cap: ₹20,00,000 (tax-exempt limit).
- Paid within 30 days of the last working day; delays attract simple interest
  at the notified rate.

## Nomination
Employees must nominate their PF and gratuity beneficiaries within 30 days of
joining and update nominations after any life event (marriage, birth of
child, divorce).

## Related Forms
Download from `Download > HR > Statutory Forms`:
- `PF-NOM-1` — PF nomination
- `GRAT-NOM-2` — Gratuity nomination
- `PF-WD-31` — Partial PF withdrawal

## Policy Code
`HR-STAT-2026-03` · Owner: Employee Services team.

[S4] Salary Advance Policy
# Salary Advance Policy

## Eligibility
Salary advance is available for genuine emergencies after six months of service. Maximum
advance is one month's net salary.

## Repayment
The advance is recovered over three payrolls by default, or a shorter period agreed in
writing. Recovery cannot reduce take-home below statutory minimums.

## Approval
Advances require reporting-manager and HRBP approval. A second advance is not sanctioned
while a previous one is outstanding.

## Documentation
Supporting documentation of the emergency is required for advances above 50 percent of
net salary.

Policy code: HR-PAY-A-2026-01 | Owner: Payroll team.

[S5] Joining And Retention Bonus
# Joining & Retention Bonus

## Joining Bonus
Joining bonuses are limited to niche skills and candidate-negotiated cases approved by the
business head and Rewards. Payment is with the first payroll.

## Retention Bonus
Retention bonuses are paid in milestone tranches against a written retention agreement
approved by the business head and HR.

## Recovery
Joining bonuses are recovered in full if the employee leaves within 12 months. Retention
bonuses are recovered pro-rata for the unserved period of the agreement.

## Documentation
Every bonus must have a signed agreement recording amount, conditions and recovery terms.

Policy code: HR-COMP-B-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

Superannuation is at 60 years. Extensions may be offered for identified specialists in
one-year increments up to age 62, approved by the CHRO.

## Pension and Provident Fund
Statutory provident fund and pension scheme benefits are settled as per EPFO rules on
superannuation.

## Gratuity
Gratuity is payable as per the Payment of Gratuity Act on superannuation without the
five-year minimum service condition.

## Transition Support
A pre-retirement counselling session and benefits orientation are offered in the final
year of service.

Policy code: HR-RET-2026-01 | Owner: Benefits team.

[S3] Pf Gratuity
# Provident Fund (PF) & Gratuity — Quick Reference

## Provident Fund
- Contribution: **12% of basic + DA** by the employee, matched by the employer.
- Employer contribution split: 8.33% to EPS (Employee Pension Scheme, capped
  on ₹15,000 basic) + balance to EPF.
- Interest is credited annually as declared by the EPFO.
- Withdrawals: partial withdrawals allowed for defined reasons (marriage,
  higher education, home purchase, medical emergency) subject to service
  tenure thresholds.
- Universal Account Number (UAN) is issued at joining and is portable across
  employers.

## Gratuity
- Payable on separation after continuous service of at least **5 years**
  (waived for death / permanent disability).
- Formula: `(Last drawn basic + DA) × 15 / 26 × completed years of service`.
- Statutory cap: ₹20,00,000 (tax-exempt limit).
- Paid within 30 days of the last working day; delays attract simple interest
  at the notified rate.

## Nomination
Employees must nominate their PF and gratuity beneficiaries within 30 days of
joining and update nominations after any life event (marriage, birth of
child, divorce).

## Related Forms
Download from `Download > HR > Statutory Forms`:
- `PF-NOM-1` — PF nomination
- `GRAT-NOM-2` — Gratuity nomination
- `PF-WD-31` — Partial PF withdrawal

## Policy Code
`HR-STAT-2026-03` · Owner: Employee Services team.

[S4] Salary Advance Policy
# Salary Advance Policy

## Eligibility
Salary advance is available for genuine emergencies after six months of service. Maximum
advance is one month's net salary.

## Repayment
The advance is recovered over three payrolls by default, or a shorter period agreed in
writing. Recovery cannot reduce take-home below statutory minimums.

## Approval
Advances require reporting-manager and HRBP approval. A second advance is not sanctioned
while a previous one is outstanding.

## Documentation
Supporting documentation of the emergency is required for advances above 50 percent of
net salary.

Policy code: HR-PAY-A-2026-01 | Owner: Payroll team.

[S5] Joining And Retention Bonus
# Joining & Retention Bonus

## Joining Bonus
Joining bonuses are limited to niche skills and candidate-negotiated cases approved by the
business head and Rewards. Payment is with the first payroll.

## Retention Bonus
Retention bonuses are paid in milestone tranches against a written retention agreement
approved by the business head and HR.

## Recovery
Joining bonuses are recovered in full if the employee leaves within 12 months. Retention
bonuses are recovered pro-rata for the unserved period of the agreement.

## Documentation
Every bonus must have a signed agreement recording amount, conditions and recovery terms.

Policy code: HR-COMP-B-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

- Certification must be passed, not merely attempted.
- Employee must be in service on the date of the claim.

## Retirement Age
Superannuation is at 60 years. Extensions may be offered for identified specialists in

[S4] Salary Advance Policy
# Salary Advance Policy

## Eligibility
Salary advance is available for genuine emergencies after six months of service. Maximum
advance is one month's net salary.

## Repayment
The advance is recovered over three payrolls by default, or a shorter period agreed in
writing. Recovery cannot reduce take-home below statutory minimums.

## Approval
Advances require reporting-manager and HRBP approval. A second advance is not sanctioned
while a previous one is outstanding.

## Documentation
Supporting documentation of the emergency is required for advances above 50 percent of
net salary.

Policy code: HR-PAY-A-2026-01 | Owner: Payroll team.

[S5] Joining And Retention Bonus
# Joining & Retention Bonus

## Joining Bonus
Joining bonuses are limited to niche skills and candidate-negotiated cases approved by the
business head and Rewards. Payment is with the first payroll.

## Retention Bonus
Retention bonuses are paid in milestone tranches against a written retention agreement
approved by the business head and HR.

## Recovery
Joining bonuses are recovered in full if the employee leaves within 12 months. Retention
bonuses are recovered pro-rata for the unserved period of the agreement.

## Documentation
Every bonus must have a signed agreement recording amount, conditions and recovery terms.

Policy code: HR-COMP-B-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

# Provident Fund (PF) & Gratuity — Quick Reference

## Provident Fund
- Contribution: **12% of basic + DA** by the employee, matched by the employer.
- Employer contribution split: 8.33% to EPS (Employee Pension Scheme, capped
  on ₹15,000 basic) + balance to EPF.
- Interest is credited annually as declared by the EPFO.
- Withdrawals: partial withdrawals allowed for defined reasons (marriage,
  higher education, home purchase, medical emergency) subject to service
  tenure thresholds.
- Universal Account Number (UAN) is issued at joining and is portable across
  employers.

## Gratuity
- Payable on separation after continuous service of at least **5 years**
  (waived for death / permanent disability).
- Formula: `(Last drawn basic + DA) × 15 / 26 × completed years of service`.
- Statutory cap: ₹20,00,000 (tax-exempt limit).
- Paid within 30 days of the last working day; delays attract simple interest
  at the notified rate.

## Nomination
Employees must nominate their PF and gratuity beneficiaries within 30 days of
joining and update nominations after any life event (marriage, birth of
child, divorce).

Salary advance is available for genuine emergencies after six months of service. Maximum
advance is one month's net salary.

## Repayment
The advance is recovered over three payrolls by default, or a shorter period agreed in
writing. Recovery cannot reduce take-home below statutory minimums.

## Approval
Advances require reporting-manager and HRBP approval. A second advance is not sanctioned
while a previous one is outstanding.

## Documentation
Supporting documentation of the emergency is required for advances above 50 percent of
net salary.

Policy code: HR-PAY-A-2026-01 | Owner: Payroll team.

# Joining & Retention Bonus

## Joining Bonus
Joining bonuses are limited to niche skills and candidate-negotiated cases approved by the
business head and Rewards. Payment is with the first payroll.

## Retention Bonus
Retention bonuses are paid in milestone tranches against a written retention agreement
approved by the business head and HR.

## Recovery
Joining bonuses are recovered in full if the employee leaves within 12 months. Retention
bonuses are recovered pro-rata for the unserved period of the agreement.

## Documentation
Every bonus must have a signed agreement recording amount, conditions and recovery terms.

[S4] Salary Advance Policy
# Salary Advance Policy

## Eligibility
Salary advance is available for genuine emergencies after six months of service. Maximum
advance is one month's net salary.

## Repayment
The advance is recovered over three payrolls by default, or a shorter period agreed in
writing. Recovery cannot reduce take-home below statutory minimums.

## Approval
Advances require reporting-manager and HRBP approval. A second advance is not sanctioned
while a previous one is outstanding.

## Documentation
Supporting documentation of the emergency is required for advances above 50 percent of
net salary.

Policy code: HR-PAY-A-2026-01 | Owner: Payroll team.

[S5] Joining And Retention Bonus
# Joining & Retention Bonus

## Joining Bonus
Joining bonuses are limited to niche skills and candidate-negotiated cases approved by the
business head and Rewards. Payment is with the first payroll.

## Retention Bonus
Retention bonuses are paid in milestone tranches against a written retention agreement
approved by the business head and HR.

## Recovery
Joining bonuses are recovered in full if the employee leaves within 12 months. Retention
bonuses are recovered pro-rata for the unserved period of the agreement.

## Documentation
Every bonus must have a signed agreement recording amount, conditions and recovery terms.

Policy code: HR-COMP-B-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

# Provident Fund (PF) & Gratuity — Quick Reference

## Provident Fund
- Contribution: **12% of basic + DA** by the employee, matched by the employer.
- Employer contribution split: 8.33% to EPS (Employee Pension Scheme, capped
  on ₹15,000 basic) + balance to EPF.
- Interest is credited annually as declared by the EPFO.
- Withdrawals: partial withdrawals allowed for defined reasons (marriage,
  higher education, home purchase, medical emergency) subject to service
  tenure thresholds.
- Universal Account Number (UAN) is issued at joining and is portable across
  employers.

## Gratuity
- Payable on separation after continuous service of at least **5 years**
  (waived for death / permanent disability).
- Formula: `(Last drawn basic + DA) × 15 / 26 × completed years of service`.
- Statutory cap: ₹20,00,000 (tax-exempt limit).
- Paid within 30 days of the last working day; delays attract simple interest
  at the notified rate.

## Nomination
Employees must nominate their PF and gratuity beneficiaries within 30 days of
joining and update nominations after any life event (marriage, birth of
child, divorce).

## Related Forms
Download from `Download > HR > Statutory Forms`:
- `PF-NOM-1` — PF nomination
- `GRAT-NOM-2` — Gratuity nomination
- `PF-WD-31` — Partial PF withdrawal

## Policy Code
`HR-STAT-2026-03` · Owner: Employee Services team.

[S4] Salary Advance Policy
# Salary Advance Policy

## Eligibility
Salary advance is available for genuine emergencies after six months of service. Maximum
advance is one month's net salary.

## Repayment
The advance is recovered over three payrolls by default, or a shorter period agreed in
writing. Recovery cannot reduce take-home below statutory minimums.

## Approval
Advances require reporting-manager and HRBP approval. A second advance is not sanctioned
while a previous one is outstanding.

## Documentation
Supporting documentation of the emergency is required for advances above 50 percent of
net salary.

Policy code: HR-PAY-A-2026-01 | Owner: Payroll team.

[S5] Joining And Retention Bonus
# Joining & Retention Bonus

## Joining Bonus
Joining bonuses are limited to niche skills and candidate-negotiated cases approved by the
business head and Rewards. Payment is with the first payroll.

## Retention Bonus
Retention bonuses are paid in milestone tranches against a written retention agreement
approved by the business head and HR.

## Recovery
Joining bonuses are recovered in full if the employee leaves within 12 months. Retention
bonuses are recovered pro-rata for the unserved period of the agreement.

## Documentation
Every bonus must have a signed agreement recording amount, conditions and recovery terms.

Policy code: HR-COMP-B-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

# Hotel & Accommodation Norms

## City-wise Caps
Metro cities: INR 8,000 per night. Tier-1 cities: INR 6,000 per night. Other cities:
INR 4,500 per night. Caps include taxes.

## Booking Preference
Accommodation must be booked through the approved corporate travel platform. Direct
bookings are reimbursed only with prior approval and valid justification.

## Shared Stay
Employees travelling together may share rooms for internal meetings. Room-sharing norms
apply only with mutual consent and are never mandatory.

## Invoice Requirements
Submit a GST invoice in the employee's name along with the stay dates. Payments to
unregistered properties are not reimbursable.

Policy code: HR-TRVL-H-2026-01 | Owner: Employee Services team.

[S5] Certification Reimbursement
# Certification Reimbursement Policy

## Approved List
Reimbursement applies to certifications on the approved list published annually, such as
CAIIB, CFA, FRM, cloud certifications and role-specific technical certifications.

## Reimbursement Amount
Up to 100 percent of exam fees for certifications on the approved list, capped per grade.
Renewal and membership fees are reimbursed for active certifications.

## Conditions
- Certification must be passed, not merely attempted.
- Employee must be in service on the date of the claim.
- Reimbursement is paid against the fee receipt only.

## Bond

- Contribution: **12% of basic + DA** by the employee, matched by the employer.
- Employer contribution split: 8.33% to EPS (Employee Pension Scheme, capped
  on ₹15,000 basic) + balance to EPF.
- Interest is credited annually as declared by the EPFO.

  higher education, home purchase, medical emergency) subject to service
  tenure thresholds.

  employers.

## Gratuity
- Payable on separation after continuous service of at least **5 years**
  (waived for death / permanent disability).

- Paid within 30 days of the last working day; delays attract simple interest
  at the notified rate.

joining and update nominations after any life event (marriage, birth of
child, divorce).

[S1] Pf Gratuity
# Provident Fund (PF) & Gratuity — Quick Reference

## Provident Fund
- Contribution: **12% of basic + DA** by the employee, matched by the employer.
- Employer contribution split: 8.33% to EPS (Employee Pension Scheme, capped
  on ₹15,000 basic) + balance to EPF.
- Interest is credited annually as declared by the EPFO.
- Withdrawals: partial withdrawals allowed for defined reasons (marriage,
  higher education, home purchase, medical emergency) subject to service
  tenure thresholds.
- Universal Account Number (UAN) is issued at joining and is portable across
  employers.

## Gratuity
- Payable on separation after continuous service of at least **5 years**
  (waived for death / permanent disability).
- Formula: `(Last drawn basic + DA) × 15 / 26 × completed years of service`.
- Statutory cap: ₹20,00,000 (tax-exempt limit).
- Paid within 30 days of the last working day; delays attract simple interest
  at the notified rate.

## Nomination
Employees must nominate their PF and gratuity beneficiaries within 30 days of
joining and update nominations after any life event (marriage, birth of
child, divorce).

## Related Forms
Download from `Download > HR > Statutory Forms`:
- `PF-NOM-1` — PF nomination
- `GRAT-NOM-2` — Gratuity nomination
- `PF-WD-31` — Partial PF withdrawal

## Policy Code
`HR-STAT-2026-03` · Owner: Employee Services team.

[S2] Who should I contact about PF contribution?
Q: Who should I contact about PF contribution?
A: Use the payroll helpdesk in the HR portal; the SLA is 2 business days.

[S3] What is the eligibility for gratuity?
Q: What is the eligibility for gratuity?
A: Gratuity is payable after 5 years of continuous service, waived on death or permanent disability. The formula is (last drawn basic + DA) x 15 / 26 x completed years. Statutory tax-exempt cap is INR 20 lakh.

Gratuity is payable as per the Payment of Gratuity Act on superannuation without the

is found to violate the anti-nepotism policy.

1. Register the candidate in the referral portal.
2. Candidate is tagged to the employee for 180 days.
3. On selection, the referral bonus is processed automatically.

# Provident Fund (PF) & Gratuity — Quick Reference

## Provident Fund
- Contribution: **12% of basic + DA** by the employee, matched by the employer.
- Employer contribution split: 8.33% to EPS (Employee Pension Scheme, capped
  on ₹15,000 basic) + balance to EPF.
- Interest is credited annually as declared by the EPFO.
- Withdrawals: partial withdrawals allowed for defined reasons (marriage,
  higher education, home purchase, medical emergency) subject to service
  tenure thresholds.
- Universal Account Number (UAN) is issued at joining and is portable across
  employers.

## Gratuity
- Payable on separation after continuous service of at least **5 years**
  (waived for death / permanent disability).
- Formula: `(Last drawn basic + DA) × 15 / 26 × completed years of service`.
- Statutory cap: ₹20,00,000 (tax-exempt limit).
- Paid within 30 days of the last working day; delays attract simple interest
  at the notified rate.

## Nomination
Employees must nominate their PF and gratuity beneficiaries within 30 days of
joining and update nominations after any life event (marriage, birth of
child, divorce).

## Related Forms
Download from `Download > HR > Statutory Forms`:
- `PF-NOM-1` — PF nomination
- `GRAT-NOM-2` — Gratuity nomination
- `PF-WD-31` — Partial PF withdrawal

Q: Who should I contact about PF contribution?

USER QUESTION:
Please clarify: after how many years of service is gratuity payable? (ref VBLK-0022)

RETRIEVED CONTEXT (cite as [S1], [S2], ...):
[S1] What is the eligibility for gratuity?
Q: What is the eligibility for gratuity?
A: Gratuity is payable after 5 years of continuous service, waived on death or permanent disability. The formula is (last drawn basic + DA) x 15 / 26 x completed years. Statutory tax-exempt cap is INR 20 lakh.

[S2] Retirement And Superannuation
# Retirement & Superannuation

## Retirement Age
Superannuation is at 60 years. Extensions may be offered for identified specialists in
one-year increments up to age 62, approved by the CHRO.

## Pension and Provident Fund
Statutory provident fund and pension scheme benefits are settled as per EPFO rules on
superannuation.

## Gratuity
Gratuity is payable as per the Payment of Gratuity Act on superannuation without the
five-year minimum service condition.

## Transition Support
A pre-retirement counselling session and benefits orientation are offered in the final
year of service.

Policy code: HR-RET-2026-01 | Owner: Benefits team.

[S3] Pf Gratuity
# Provident Fund (PF) & Gratuity — Quick Reference

## Provident Fund
- Contribution: **12% of basic + DA** by the employee, matched by the employer.
- Employer contribution split: 8.33% to EPS (Employee Pension Scheme, capped
  on ₹15,000 basic) + balance to EPF.
- Interest is credited annually as declared by the EPFO.
- Withdrawals: partial withdrawals allowed for defined reasons (marriage,
  higher education, home purchase, medical emergency) subject to service
  tenure thresholds.
- Universal Account Number (UAN) is issued at joining and is portable across
  employers.

## Gratuity
- Payable on separation after continuous service of at least **5 years**
  (waived for death / permanent disability).
- Formula: `(Last drawn basic + DA) × 15 / 26 × completed years of service`.
- Statutory cap: ₹20,00,000 (tax-exempt limit).
- Paid within 30 days of the last working day; delays attract simple interest
  at the notified rate.

## Nomination
Employees must nominate their PF and gratuity beneficiaries within 30 days of
joining and update nominations after any life event (marriage, birth of
child, divorce).

## Related Forms
Download from `Download > HR > Statutory Forms`:
- `PF-NOM-1` — PF nomination
- `GRAT-NOM-2` — Gratuity nomination
- `PF-WD-31` — Partial PF withdrawal

## Policy Code
`HR-STAT-2026-03` · Owner: Employee Services team.

[S4] Variable Pay Policy
# Variable Pay Policy

## Eligibility
Variable pay applies to grades M3 and above. It is paid annually against business, unit
and individual scorecard achievement.

## Payout Formula
Payout = target variable × business multiplier × unit multiplier × individual multiplier.
Multipliers range from 0 to 1.5 as per the approved scorecard.

## Timing
Variable pay for a financial year is paid in June of the following year. Employees who
resign before the payout date are not eligible unless the separation policy states otherwise.

## Disputes
Scorecard disputes must be raised within 30 days of scorecard communication to the
business review committee.

Policy code: HR-COMP-V-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

[S5] Salary Advance Policy
# Salary Advance Policy

## Eligibility
Salary advance is available for genuine emergencies after six months of service. Maximum
advance is one month's net salary.

## Repayment
The advance is recovered over three payrolls by default, or a shorter period agreed in
writing. Recovery cannot reduce take-home below statutory minimums.

## Approval
Advances require reporting-manager and HRBP approval. A second advance is not sanctioned
while a previous one is outstanding.

## Documentation
Supporting documentation of the emergency is required for advances above 50 percent of
net salary.

Policy code: HR-PAY-A-2026-01 | Owner: Payroll team.

ASSISTANT: 12% of basic + DA is contributed by the employee and matched by the employer.

Compose the final answer now.

# Provident Fund (PF) & Gratuity — Quick Reference

## Provident Fund
- Contribution: **12% of basic + DA** by the employee, matched by the employer.
- Employer contribution split: 8.33% to EPS (Employee Pension Scheme, capped
  on ₹15,000 basic) + balance to EPF.
- Interest is credited annually as declared by the EPFO.
- Withdrawals: partial withdrawals allowed for defined reasons (marriage,
  higher education, home purchase, medical emergency) subject to service
  tenure thresholds.
- Universal Account Number (UAN) is issued at joining and is portable across
  employers.

## Gratuity
- Payable on separation after continuous service of at least **5 years**
  (waived for death / permanent disability).
- Formula: `(Last drawn basic + DA) × 15 / 26 × completed years of service`.
- Statutory cap: ₹20,00,000 (tax-exempt limit).
- Paid within 30 days of the last working day; delays attract simple interest
  at the notified rate.

## Nomination
Employees must nominate their PF and gratuity beneficiaries within 30 days of
joining and update nominations after any life event (marriage, birth of
child, divorce).

## Related Forms
Download from `Download > HR > Statutory Forms`:
- `PF-NOM-1` — PF nomination
- `GRAT-NOM-2` — Gratuity nomination
- `PF-WD-31` — Partial PF withdrawal

# Salary Advance Policy

## Eligibility
Salary advance is available for genuine emergencies after six months of service. Maximum
advance is one month's net salary.

## Repayment
The advance is recovered over three payrolls by default, or a shorter period agreed in
writing. Recovery cannot reduce take-home below statutory minimums.

## Approval
Advances require reporting-manager and HRBP approval.

events.content:
USER QUESTION:
I need guidance on this: after how many years of service is gratuity payable? (ref VBLK-0023)

RETRIEVED CONTEXT (cite as [S1], [S2], ...):
[S1] What is the eligibility for gratuity?
Q: What is the eligibility for gratuity?
A: Gratuity is payable after 5 years of continuous service, waived on death or permanent disability. The formula is (last drawn basic + DA) x 15 / 26 x completed years. Statutory tax-exempt cap is INR 20 lakh.

[S2] Retirement And Superannuation
# Retirement & Superannuation

## Retirement Age
Superannuation is at 60 years. Extensions may be offered for identified specialists in
one-year increments up to age 62, approved by the CHRO.

## Pension and Provident Fund
Statutory provident fund and pension scheme benefits are settled as per EPFO rules on
superannuation.

## Gratuity
Gratuity is payable as per the Payment of Gratuity Act on superannuation without the
five-year minimum service condition.

## Transition Support
A pre-retirement counselling session and benefits orientation are offered in the final
year of service.

Policy code: HR-RET-2026-01 | Owner: Benefits team.

[S3] Pf Gratuity
# Provident Fund (PF) & Gratuity — Quick Reference

## Provident Fund
- Contribution: **12% of basic + DA** by the employee, matched by the employer.
- Employer contribution split: 8.33% to EPS (Employee Pension Scheme, capped
  on ₹15,000 basic) + balance to EPF.
- Interest is credited annually as declared by the EPFO.
- Withdrawals: partial withdrawals allowed for defined reasons (marriage,
  higher education, home purchase, medical emergency) subject to service
  tenure thresholds.
- Universal Account Number (UAN) is issued at joining and is portable across
  employers.

## Gratuity
- Payable on separation after continuous service of at least **5 years**
  (waived for death / permanent disability).
- Formula: `(Last drawn basic + DA) × 15 / 26 × completed years of service`.
- Statutory cap: ₹20,00,000 (tax-exempt limit).
- Paid within 30 days of the last working day; delays attract simple interest
  at the notified rate.

## Nomination
Employees must nominate their PF and gratuity beneficiaries within 30 days of
joining and update nominations after any life event (marriage, birth of
child, divorce).

## Related Forms
Download from `Download > HR > Statutory Forms`:
- `PF-NOM-1` — PF nomination
- `GRAT-NOM-2` — Gratuity nomination
- `PF-WD-31` — Partial PF withdrawal

## Policy Code
`HR-STAT-2026-03` · Owner: Employee Services team.

[S4] Variable Pay Policy
# Variable Pay Policy

## Eligibility
Variable pay applies to grades M3 and above. It is paid annually against business, unit
and individual scorecard achievement.

## Payout Formula
Payout = target variable × business multiplier × unit multiplier × individual multiplier.
Multipliers range from 0 to 1.5 as per the approved scorecard.

## Timing
Variable pay for a financial year is paid in June of the following year. Employees who
resign before the payout date are not eligible unless the separation policy states otherwise.

## Disputes
Scorecard disputes must be raised within 30 days of scorecard communication to the
business review committee.

Policy code: HR-COMP-V-2026-01 | Owner: Rewards team.

[S5] Salary Advance Policy
# Salary Advance Policy

## Eligibility
Salary advance is available for genuine emergencies after six months of service. Maximum
advance is one month's net salary.

## Repayment
The advance is recovered over three payrolls by default, or a shorter period agreed in
writing. Recovery cannot reduce take-home below statutory minimums.

## Approval
Advances require reporting-manager and HRBP approval. A second advance is not sanctioned
while a previous one is outstanding.

## Documentation
Supporting documentation of the emergency is required for advances above 50 percent of
net salary.

Policy code: HR-PAY-A-2026-01 | Owner: Payroll team.

USER: I need guidance on this: what percentage of basic plus DA is contributed to Provident Fund? (ref VBLK-0023)
ASSISTANT: 12% of basic + DA is contributed by the employee and matched by the employer.

Compose the final answer now.

[S1] What is the eligibility for gratuity?
Q: What is the eligibility for gratuity?
A: Gratuity is payable after 5 years of continuous service, waived on death or permanent disability. The formula is (last drawn basic + DA) x 15 / 26 x completed years. Statutory tax-exempt cap is INR 20 lakh.

[S2] Pf Gratuity
# Provident Fund (PF) & Gratuity — Quick Reference

## Provident Fund
- Contribution: **12% of basic + DA** by the employee, matched by the employer.
- Employer contribution split: 8.33% to EPS (Employee Pension Scheme, capped
  on ₹15,000 basic) + balance to EPF.
- Interest is credited annually as declared by the EPFO.
- Withdrawals: partial withdrawals allowed for defined reasons (marriage,
  higher education, home purchase, medical emergency) subject to service
  tenure thresholds.
- Universal Account Number (UAN) is issued at joining and is portable across
  employers.

## Gratuity
- Payable on separation after continuous service of at least **5 years**
  (waived for death / permanent disability).
- Formula: `(Last drawn basic + DA) × 15 / 26 × completed years of service`.
- Statutory cap: ₹20,00,000 (tax-exempt limit).
- Paid within 30 days of the last working day; delays attract simple interest
  at the notified rate.

## Nomination
Employees must nominate their PF and gratuity beneficiaries within 30 days of
joining and update nominations after any life event (marriage, birth of
child, divorce).

## Related Forms
Download from `Download > HR > Statutory Forms`:
- `PF-NOM-1` — PF nomination
- `GRAT-NOM-2` — Gratuity nomination
- `PF-WD-31` — Partial PF withdrawal
