[S1] Mutual Funds
# Mutual Funds — Advisor Playbook

## Product Suite
Axis Wealth offers execution-only and advisory access across the following
mutual fund categories:
- Equity: large-cap, flexi-cap, mid-cap, small-cap, ELSS, sector/thematic.
- Debt: liquid, ultra-short, money market, corporate bond, gilt, credit risk.
- Hybrid: aggressive, conservative, balanced advantage, multi-asset.
- International feeder funds (currency hedged and unhedged).

## Suitability Framework
An advisor must complete the customer's risk profile before recommending any
scheme:
1. Risk tolerance questionnaire (12 questions).
2. Time horizon and liquidity check.
3. KYC + FATCA declaration.
Recommendations must map to the resulting risk band (Conservative / Moderate
/ Aggressive). Deviations require written justification and a customer
consent letter.

## SIP Rules
- Minimum SIP: ₹500/month (except direct-plan schemes; check factsheet).
- SIP registration cut-off: 8 days before first debit date.
- Pause / cancel SIP: T-2 working days before the debit date.
- Skipping instalments is allowed up to 3 months in a rolling year without
  breaking the mandate.

## Exit Load Ready-Reckoner
- Equity funds: 1% if redeemed within 12 months of allocation, nil after.
- Liquid funds: graded exit load from day 1 to day 7 as per SEBI norms.
- ELSS: statutory 3-year lock-in — no early exit permitted.

## Advisor Do & Don'ts
Do: disclose commission, provide TER details, share KIM before purchase.
Don't: guarantee returns, make comparisons with fixed deposits without a
disclaimer, or process transactions without a signed suitability report.

## Reference
`FA-MF-2026-01` · Owner: Wealth Advisory desk.

[S2] Pf Gratuity
# Provident Fund (PF) & Gratuity — Quick Reference

## Provident Fund
- Contribution: **12% of basic + DA** by the employee, matched by the employer.
- Employer contribution split: 8.33% to EPS (Employee Pension Scheme, capped
  on ₹15,000 basic) + balance to EPF.
- Interest is credited annually as declared by the EPFO.
- Withdrawals: partial withdrawals allowed for defined reasons (marriage,
  higher education, home purchase, medical emergency) subject to service
  tenure thresholds.
- Universal Account Number (UAN) is issued at joining and is portable across
  employers.

## Gratuity
- Payable on separation after continuous service of at least **5 years**
  (waived for death / permanent disability).
- Formula: `(Last drawn basic + DA) × 15 / 26 × completed years of service`.
- Statutory cap: ₹20,00,000 (tax-exempt limit).
- Paid within 30 days of the last working day; delays attract simple interest
  at the notified rate.

## Nomination
Employees must nominate their PF and gratuity beneficiaries within 30 days of
joining and update nominations after any life event (marriage, birth of
child, divorce).

## Related Forms
Download from `Download > HR > Statutory Forms`:
- `PF-NOM-1` — PF nomination
- `GRAT-NOM-2` — Gratuity nomination
- `PF-WD-31` — Partial PF withdrawal

## Policy Code
`HR-STAT-2026-03` · Owner: Employee Services team.

[S3] Nps Guide
# National Pension System (NPS) Guide

## Structure
NPS is a defined-contribution retirement scheme regulated by PFRDA with
tier-I (retirement) and tier-II (voluntary) accounts.

## Asset Classes
Equity, corporate bonds, government securities and alternate assets with
allocation caps per PFRDA rules. Active and auto choice available.

## Tax Benefits
Contributions under 80CCD(1)/(1B) within limits; employer contributions
under 80CCD(2).

## Exit Rules
On maturity, up to the prescribed percentage may be withdrawn lump-sum
with the balance annuitised.

## Suitability
NPS suits investors seeking market-linked, low-cost retirement
accumulation with annuitisation at maturity.

Advisory note: explain lock-in and annuity purchase requirement.

[S4] Fixed Deposits
# Fixed Deposits — Product Note

## Product Variants
- **Regular FD:** interest paid monthly / quarterly / on maturity.
- **Reinvestment FD:** compounded quarterly, single maturity payout.
- **Tax Saver FD:** 5-year lock-in, deduction under Section 80C up to ₹1.5L.
- **Senior Citizen FD:** additional 0.50% over the applicable card rate.
- **NRE / NRO FD:** available to NRIs subject to source-of-fund controls.

## Booking Channels
- Internet banking (retail).
- Mobile app.
- Any branch during business hours.
- Relationship manager for HNI customers.

## Premature Withdrawal
- Allowed on all variants except the 5-year Tax Saver FD.
- Penalty: 1.00% below the applicable card rate for the period run OR the
  booking rate, whichever is lower.
- Sweep-in FDs are broken in FIFO order to fund the linked savings account.

## Nomination
Nomination is mandatory. It can be captured at booking or updated later via
the branch or internet banking. Joint holdings must specify the operating
mandate (either or survivor / former or survivor / joint).

## Auto Renewal
Auto renewal defaults to `Reinvestment` at the prevailing rate for the same
tenure. Customers can switch this off during booking.

## Reference
`FA-FD-2026-01` · Owner: Liabilities product team.

[S5] What is the SIP registration cut-off?
Q: What is the SIP registration cut-off?
A: SIP registration cut-off is 8 calendar days before the first debit date. Pausing or cancelling a running SIP requires the request at least 2 working days before the debit date.

the branch or internet banking. Joint holdings must specify the operating
mandate (either or survivor / former or survivor / joint).

Auto renewal defaults to `Reinvestment` at the prevailing rate for the same
tenure. Customers can switch this off during booking.

# Mutual Funds — Advisor Playbook

## Product Suite
Axis Wealth offers execution-only and advisory access across the following
mutual fund categories:
- Equity: large-cap, flexi-cap, mid-cap, small-cap, ELSS, sector/thematic.
- Debt: liquid, ultra-short, money market, corporate bond, gilt, credit risk.
- Hybrid: aggressive, conservative, balanced advantage, multi-asset.
- International feeder funds (currency hedged and unhedged).

## Suitability Framework
An advisor must complete the customer's risk profile before recommending any
scheme:
1. Risk tolerance questionnaire (12 questions).
2. Time horizon and liquidity check.
3. KYC + FATCA declaration.
Recommendations must map to the resulting risk band (Conservative / Moderate
/ Aggressive). Deviations require written justification and a customer
consent letter.

## SIP Rules
- Minimum SIP: ₹500/month (except direct-plan schemes; check factsheet).
- SIP registration cut-off: 8 days before first debit date.
- Pause / cancel SIP: T-2 working days before the debit date.
- Skipping instalments is allowed up to 3 months in a rolling year without
  breaking the mandate.

## Exit Load Ready-Reckoner
- Equity funds: 1% if redeemed within 12 months of allocation, nil after.
- Liquid funds: graded exit load from day 1 to day 7 as per SEBI norms.
- ELSS: statutory 3-year lock-in — no early exit permitted.

## Advisor Do & Don'ts
Do: disclose commission, provide TER details, share KIM before purchase.
Don't: guarantee returns, make comparisons with fixed deposits without a
disclaimer, or process transactions without a signed suitability report.

# Mutual Funds — Advisor Playbook

## Product Suite
Axis Wealth offers execution-only and advisory access across the following
mutual fund categories:
- Equity: large-cap, flexi-cap, mid-cap, small-cap, ELSS, sector/thematic.
- Debt: liquid, ultra-short, money market, corporate bond, gilt, credit risk.
- Hybrid: aggressive, conservative, balanced advantage, multi-asset.
- International feeder funds (currency hedged and unhedged).

## Suitability Framework
An advisor must complete the customer's risk profile before recommending any
scheme:
1. Risk tolerance questionnaire (12 questions).
2. Time horizon and liquidity check.
3. KYC + FATCA declaration.
Recommendations must map to the resulting risk band (Conservative / Moderate
/ Aggressive). Deviations require written justification and a customer
consent letter.

## SIP Rules
- Minimum SIP: ₹500/month (except direct-plan schemes; check factsheet).
- SIP registration cut-off: 8 days before first debit date.
- Pause / cancel SIP: T-2 working days before the debit date.
- Skipping instalments is allowed up to 3 months in a rolling year without
  breaking the mandate.

## Exit Load Ready-Reckoner
- Equity funds: 1% if redeemed within 12 months of allocation, nil after.
- Liquid funds: graded exit load from day 1 to day 7 as per SEBI norms.
- ELSS: statutory 3-year lock-in — no early exit permitted.

## Advisor Do & Don'ts
Do: disclose commission, provide TER details, share KIM before purchase.
Don't: guarantee returns, make comparisons with fixed deposits without a
disclaimer, or process transactions without a signed suitability report.

## Reference
`FA-MF-2026-01` · Owner: Wealth Advisory desk.

# Fixed Deposits — Product Note

## Product Variants
- **Regular FD:** interest paid monthly / quarterly / on maturity.
- **Reinvestment FD:** compounded quarterly, single maturity payout.
- **Tax Saver FD:** 5-year lock-in, deduction under Section 80C up to ₹1.5L.
- **Senior Citizen FD:** additional 0.50% over the applicable card rate.
- **NRE / NRO FD:** available to NRIs subject to source-of-fund controls.

## Booking Channels
- Internet banking (retail).
- Mobile app.
- Any branch during business hours.
- Relationship manager for HNI customers.

## Premature Withdrawal
- Allowed on all variants except the 5-year Tax Saver FD.
- Penalty: 1.00% below the applicable card rate for the period run OR the
  booking rate, whichever is lower.
- Sweep-in FDs are broken in FIFO order to fund the linked savings account.

## Nomination
Nomination is mandatory. It can be captured at booking or updated later via
the branch or internet banking. Joint holdings must specify the operating
mandate (either or survivor / former or survivor / joint).

## Auto Renewal
Auto renewal defaults to `Reinvestment` at the prevailing rate for the same
tenure. Customers can switch this off during booking.

## Reference
`FA-FD-2026-01` · Owner: Liabilities product team.

# Know Your Customer (KYC) Standard

## Purpose
This standard defines the mandatory identity and address verification a
banker must perform before onboarding any customer, in line with the RBI
Master Direction on KYC.

## Acceptable Officially Valid Documents (OVDs)
- Aadhaar (with masked number, per UIDAI guideline).
- PAN.
- Passport.
- Driving licence issued by an RTO.
- Voter ID issued by ECI.
- Job card issued by NREGA duly signed by the state government.

## Video KYC (V-CIP)
V-CIP is available for eligible savings account onboarding subject to:
- Genuine live video with the customer visible from mid-torso up.
- Random challenge (e.g., "Show your OVD now").
- Officer capturing at least 3 still frames during the call.
- Geo-tagging of the customer's location.

## Periodic Update Frequency
| Risk Category | Frequency |
|---|---|
| High risk | Every 2 years |
| Medium risk | Every 8 years |
| Low risk | Every 10 years |

## Deficient KYC
Accounts flagged with deficient KYC are moved to `PARTIAL FREEZE` after
two written reminders. All debits (excluding regulatory / statutory dues)
are blocked in this state.

## References
- Policy code: LAW-KYC-2026-01
- Aligned to RBI Master Direction on KYC (as amended).
- Owner: Compliance — Financial Crime unit.

are blocked in this state.

# BI Platform Architecture

## Layers
1. Sources: core banking, CRM, cards, payments and HR systems.
2. Lakehouse: raw, curated and semantic layers on the analytics platform.
3. Serving: semantic models consumed by dashboards, notebooks and the
   conversational BI assistant.

## Data Flow
Change-data-capture and batch pipelines land data within defined freshness
SLAs. Transformations produce the curated and semantic layers.

## Access Paths
The conversational BI assistant reads only the semantic layer. No query
touches source systems directly.

## Resilience
Pipelines carry retries, dead-letter handling and data-quality gates.

Policy code: BI-ARCH-2026-01 | Owner: Data Platform team.

[S5] Who supports data-as-of?
Q: Who supports data-as-of?
A: The Business Analytics CoE via the BI support queue.

[S3] Bi Intro
# Conversational BI — Getting Started

## What It Is
The `Conversational BI` bubble routes natural-language questions to the
Text-to-SQL agent, which drafts SQL against the reporting data mart, executes
it read-only, and returns a formatted result set.

## Available Datasets
- `customers` — one row per customer, with segment, branch, onboarding date.
- `accounts` — one row per account, product, balance, status.
- `transactions` — one row per transaction, txn_type, channel, amount.

Additional derived views are added quarterly; see the DDL under
`FINANCIAL_ADVISOR/mutual_funds.md` etc. for illustrative examples.

## Good Prompts
- "How many customers opened SAVINGS accounts?"
- "Top 5 customers by savings balance in Mumbai branches."
- "Average NEFT transaction amount last month by channel."
- "List customers with dormant SAVINGS accounts and balance under 5000."

## Guardrails
The engine will refuse to run SQL that:
- Writes data (INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / DROP / ALTER / ATTACH).
- References tables outside the whitelisted set.
- Returns more than 5,000 rows in a single call.

## Limitations
- Text2SQL cannot answer questions that depend on documents (use the RAG
  bubbles for those).
- It does not yet handle time-series joins across all history — restrict to
  90 days for stable results.

## Reference
`CBI-INTRO-2026-01` · Owner: BI Platform team.

[S3] Bi Intro
# Conversational BI — Getting Started

## What It Is
The `Conversational BI` bubble routes natural-language questions to the
Text-to-SQL agent, which drafts SQL against the reporting data mart, executes
it read-only, and returns a formatted result set.

## Available Datasets
- `customers` — one row per customer, with segment, branch, onboarding date.
- `accounts` — one row per account, product, balance, status.
- `transactions` — one row per transaction, txn_type, channel, amount.

Additional derived views are added quarterly; see the DDL under
`FINANCIAL_ADVISOR/mutual_funds.md` etc. for illustrative examples.

## Good Prompts
- "How many customers opened SAVINGS accounts?"
- "Top 5 customers by savings balance in Mumbai branches."
- "Average NEFT transaction amount last month by channel."
- "List customers with dormant SAVINGS accounts and balance under 5000."

## Guardrails
The engine will refuse to run SQL that:
- Writes data (INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / DROP / ALTER / ATTACH).
- References tables outside the whitelisted set.
- Returns more than 5,000 rows in a single call.

## Limitations
- Text2SQL cannot answer questions that depend on documents (use the RAG
  bubbles for those).
- It does not yet handle time-series joins across all history — restrict to
  90 days for stable results.

## Reference
`CBI-INTRO-2026-01` · Owner: BI Platform team.

A: Choose the Conversational BI bubble and ask a natural-language question about customers, accounts, or transactions. Vartalaap generates SQL, executes it read-only against the reporting mart, and returns a formatted table.

# Conversational BI — Getting Started

## What It Is
The `Conversational BI` bubble routes natural-language questions to the
Text-to-SQL agent, which drafts SQL against the reporting data mart, executes
it read-only, and returns a formatted result set.

## Available Datasets
- `customers` — one row per customer, with segment, branch, onboarding date.
- `accounts` — one row per account, product, balance, status.
- `transactions` — one row per transaction, txn_type, channel, amount.

Additional derived views are added quarterly; see the DDL under
`FINANCIAL_ADVISOR/mutual_funds.md` etc. for illustrative examples.

## Good Prompts
- "How many customers opened SAVINGS accounts?"
- "Top 5 customers by savings balance in Mumbai branches."
- "Average NEFT transaction amount last month by channel."
- "List customers with dormant SAVINGS accounts and balance under 5000."

## Guardrails
The engine will refuse to run SQL that:
- Writes data (INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / DROP / ALTER / ATTACH).
- References tables outside the whitelisted set.
- Returns more than 5,000 rows in a single call.

## Limitations
- Text2SQL cannot answer questions that depend on documents (use the RAG
  bubbles for those).
- It does not yet handle time-series joins across all history — restrict to
  90 days for stable results.

## Reference
`CBI-INTRO-2026-01` · Owner: BI Platform team.

[S3] Bi Intro
# Conversational BI — Getting Started

## What It Is
The `Conversational BI` bubble routes natural-language questions to the
Text-to-SQL agent, which drafts SQL against the reporting data mart, executes
it read-only, and returns a formatted result set.

## Available Datasets
- `customers` — one row per customer, with segment, branch, onboarding date.
- `accounts` — one row per account, product, balance, status.
- `transactions` — one row per transaction, txn_type, channel, amount.

Additional derived views are added quarterly; see the DDL under
`FINANCIAL_ADVISOR/mutual_funds.md` etc. for illustrative examples.

## Good Prompts
- "How many customers opened SAVINGS accounts?"
- "Top 5 customers by savings balance in Mumbai branches."
- "Average NEFT transaction amount last month by channel."
- "List customers with dormant SAVINGS accounts and balance under 5000."

## Guardrails
The engine will refuse to run SQL that:
- Writes data (INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / DROP / ALTER / ATTACH).
- References tables outside the whitelisted set.
- Returns more than 5,000 rows in a single call.

## Limitations
- Text2SQL cannot answer questions that depend on documents (use the RAG
  bubbles for those).
- It does not yet handle time-series joins across all history — restrict to
  90 days for stable results.

## Reference
`CBI-INTRO-2026-01` · Owner: BI Platform team.

# BI Platform Architecture

## Layers
1. Sources: core banking, CRM, cards, payments and HR systems.
2. Lakehouse: raw, curated and semantic layers on the analytics platform.

   conversational BI assistant.

The conversational BI assistant reads only the semantic layer. No query
touches source systems directly.

Pipelines carry retries, dead-letter handling and data-quality gates.

[S3] Bi Intro
# Conversational BI — Getting Started

## What It Is
The `Conversational BI` bubble routes natural-language questions to the
Text-to-SQL agent, which drafts SQL against the reporting data mart, executes
it read-only, and returns a formatted result set.

## Available Datasets
- `customers` — one row per customer, with segment, branch, onboarding date.
- `accounts` — one row per account, product, balance, status.
- `transactions` — one row per transaction, txn_type, channel, amount.

Additional derived views are added quarterly; see the DDL under
`FINANCIAL_ADVISOR/mutual_funds.md` etc. for illustrative examples.

## Good Prompts
- "How many customers opened SAVINGS accounts?"
- "Top 5 customers by savings balance in Mumbai branches."
- "Average NEFT transaction amount last month by channel."
- "List customers with dormant SAVINGS accounts and balance under 5000."

## Guardrails
The engine will refuse to run SQL that:
- Writes data (INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / DROP / ALTER / ATTACH).
- References tables outside the whitelisted set.
- Returns more than 5,000 rows in a single call.

## Limitations
- Text2SQL cannot answer questions that depend on documents (use the RAG
  bubbles for those).
- It does not yet handle time-series joins across all history — restrict to
  90 days for stable results.

## Reference
`CBI-INTRO-2026-01` · Owner: BI Platform team.

[S3] Bi Intro
# Conversational BI — Getting Started

## What It Is
The `Conversational BI` bubble routes natural-language questions to the
Text-to-SQL agent, which drafts SQL against the reporting data mart, executes
it read-only, and returns a formatted result set.

## Available Datasets
- `customers` — one row per customer, with segment, branch, onboarding date.
- `accounts` — one row per account, product, balance, status.
- `transactions` — one row per transaction, txn_type, channel, amount.

Additional derived views are added quarterly; see the DDL under
`FINANCIAL_ADVISOR/mutual_funds.md` etc. for illustrative examples.

## Good Prompts
- "How many customers opened SAVINGS accounts?"
- "Top 5 customers by savings balance in Mumbai branches."
- "Average NEFT transaction amount last month by channel."
- "List customers with dormant SAVINGS accounts and balance under 5000."

## Guardrails
The engine will refuse to run SQL that:
- Writes data (INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / DROP / ALTER / ATTACH).
- References tables outside the whitelisted set.
- Returns more than 5,000 rows in a single call.

## Limitations
- Text2SQL cannot answer questions that depend on documents (use the RAG
  bubbles for those).
- It does not yet handle time-series joins across all history — restrict to
  90 days for stable results.

[S5] Bi Intro
# Conversational BI — Getting Started

## What It Is
The `Conversational BI` bubble routes natural-language questions to the
Text-to-SQL agent, which drafts SQL against the reporting data mart, executes
it read-only, and returns a formatted result set.

## Available Datasets
- `customers` — one row per customer, with segment, branch, onboarding date.
- `accounts` — one row per account, product, balance, status.
- `transactions` — one row per transaction, txn_type, channel, amount.

Additional derived views are added quarterly; see the DDL under
`FINANCIAL_ADVISOR/mutual_funds.md` etc. for illustrative examples.

## Good Prompts
- "How many customers opened SAVINGS accounts?"
- "Top 5 customers by savings balance in Mumbai branches."
- "Average NEFT transaction amount last month by channel."
- "List customers with dormant SAVINGS accounts and balance under 5000."

## Guardrails
The engine will refuse to run SQL that:
- Writes data (INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / DROP / ALTER / ATTACH).
- References tables outside the whitelisted set.
- Returns more than 5,000 rows in a single call.

## Limitations
- Text2SQL cannot answer questions that depend on documents (use the RAG
  bubbles for those).
- It does not yet handle time-series joins across all history — restrict to
  90 days for stable results.

[S3] Bi Intro
# Conversational BI — Getting Started

## What It Is
The `Conversational BI` bubble routes natural-language questions to the
Text-to-SQL agent, which drafts SQL against the reporting data mart, executes
it read-only, and returns a formatted result set.

## Available Datasets
- `customers` — one row per customer, with segment, branch, onboarding date.
- `accounts` — one row per account, product, balance, status.
- `transactions` — one row per transaction, txn_type, channel, amount.

Additional derived views are added quarterly; see the DDL under
`FINANCIAL_ADVISOR/mutual_funds.md` etc. for illustrative examples.

## Good Prompts
- "How many customers opened SAVINGS accounts?"
- "Top 5 customers by savings balance in Mumbai branches."
- "Average NEFT transaction amount last month by channel."
- "List customers with dormant SAVINGS accounts and balance under 5000."

## Guardrails
The engine will refuse to run SQL that:
- Writes data (INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / DROP / ALTER / ATTACH).
- References tables outside the whitelisted set.
- Returns more than 5,000 rows in a single call.

## Limitations
- Text2SQL cannot answer questions that depend on documents (use the RAG
  bubbles for those).
- It does not yet handle time-series joins across all history — restrict to
  90 days for stable results.

## Reference
`CBI-INTRO-2026-01` · Owner: BI Platform team.

[S4] How do I use the Conversational BI bubble?
Q: How do I use the Conversational BI bubble?
A: Choose the Conversational BI bubble and ask a natural-language question about customers, accounts, or transactions. Vartalaap generates SQL, executes it read-only against the reporting mart, and returns a formatted table.

# Conversational BI — Getting Started

## What It Is
The `Conversational BI` bubble routes natural-language questions to the
Text-to-SQL agent, which drafts SQL against the reporting data mart, executes
it read-only, and returns a formatted result set.

## Available Datasets
- `customers` — one row per customer, with segment, branch, onboarding date.
- `accounts` — one row per account, product, balance, status.
- `transactions` — one row per transaction, txn_type, channel, amount.

Additional derived views are added quarterly; see the DDL under
`FINANCIAL_ADVISOR/mutual_funds.md` etc. for illustrative examples.

## Good Prompts
- "How many customers opened SAVINGS accounts?"
- "Top 5 customers by savings balance in Mumbai branches."
- "Average NEFT transaction amount last month by channel."
- "List customers with dormant SAVINGS accounts and balance under 5000."

## Guardrails
The engine will refuse to run SQL that:
- Writes data (INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / DROP / ALTER / ATTACH).
- References tables outside the whitelisted set.
- Returns more than 5,000 rows in a single call.

## Limitations
- Text2SQL cannot answer questions that depend on documents (use the RAG
  bubbles for those).
- It does not yet handle time-series joins across all history — restrict to
  90 days for stable results.

## Reference
`CBI-INTRO-2026-01` · Owner: BI Platform team.

The engine will refuse to run SQL that:
- Writes data (INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / DROP / ALTER / ATTACH).
- References tables outside the whitelisted set.
- Returns more than 5,000 rows in a single call.

- Text2SQL cannot answer questions that depend on documents (use the RAG
  bubbles for those).

# Conversational BI — Getting Started

## What It Is
The `Conversational BI` bubble routes natural-language questions to the
Text-to-SQL agent, which drafts SQL against the reporting data mart, executes
it read-only, and returns a formatted result set.

## Available Datasets
- `customers` — one row per customer, with segment, branch, onboarding date.
- `accounts` — one row per account, product, balance, status.
- `transactions` — one row per transaction, txn_type, channel, amount.

Additional derived views are added quarterly; see the DDL under
`FINANCIAL_ADVISOR/mutual_funds.md` etc. for illustrative examples.

## Good Prompts
- "How many customers opened SAVINGS accounts?"
- "Top 5 customers by savings balance in Mumbai branches."
- "Average NEFT transaction amount last month by channel."
- "List customers with dormant SAVINGS accounts and balance under 5000."

## Guardrails
The engine will refuse to run SQL that:
- Writes data (INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / DROP / ALTER / ATTACH).
- References tables outside the whitelisted set.
- Returns more than 5,000 rows in a single call.

## Limitations
- Text2SQL cannot answer questions that depend on documents (use the RAG
  bubbles for those).
- It does not yet handle time-series joins across all history — restrict to
  90 days for stable results.

# Conversational BI — Getting Started

## What It Is
The `Conversational BI` bubble routes natural-language questions to the
Text-to-SQL agent, which drafts SQL against the reporting data mart, executes
it read-only, and returns a formatted result set.

## Available Datasets
- `customers` — one row per customer, with segment, branch, onboarding date.
- `accounts` — one row per account, product, balance, status.
- `transactions` — one row per transaction, txn_type, channel, amount.

Additional derived views are added quarterly; see the DDL under
`FINANCIAL_ADVISOR/mutual_funds.md` etc. for illustrative examples.

## Good Prompts
- "How many customers opened SAVINGS accounts?"
- "Top 5 customers by savings balance in Mumbai branches."
- "Average NEFT transaction amount last month by channel."
- "List customers with dormant SAVINGS accounts and balance under 5000."

## Guardrails
The engine will refuse to run SQL that:
- Writes data (INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / DROP / ALTER / ATTACH).
- References tables outside the whitelisted set.
- Returns more than 5,000 rows in a single call.

## Limitations
- Text2SQL cannot answer questions that depend on documents (use the RAG
  bubbles for those).
- It does not yet handle time-series joins across all history — restrict to
  90 days for stable results.

## Reference
`CBI-INTRO-2026-01` · Owner: BI Platform team.

# Conversational BI — Getting Started

## What It Is
The `Conversational BI` bubble routes natural-language questions to the
Text-to-SQL agent, which drafts SQL against the reporting data mart, executes
it read-only, and returns a formatted result set.

## Available Datasets
- `customers` — one row per customer, with segment, branch, onboarding date.
- `accounts` — one row per account, product, balance, status.
- `transactions` — one row per transaction, txn_type, channel, amount.

Additional derived views are added quarterly; see the DDL under
`FINANCIAL_ADVISOR/mutual_funds.md` etc. for illustrative examples.

## Good Prompts
- "How many customers opened SAVINGS accounts?"
- "Top 5 customers by savings balance in Mumbai branches."
- "Average NEFT transaction amount last month by channel."
- "List customers with dormant SAVINGS accounts and balance under 5000."

## Guardrails
The engine will refuse to run SQL that:
- Writes data (INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / DROP / ALTER / ATTACH).
- References tables outside the whitelisted set.
- Returns more than 5,000 rows in a single call.

## Limitations
- Text2SQL cannot answer questions that depend on documents (use the RAG
  bubbles for those).
- It does not yet handle time-series joins across all history — restrict to
  90 days for stable results.

# Conversational BI — Getting Started

## What It Is
The `Conversational BI` bubble routes natural-language questions to the
Text-to-SQL agent, which drafts SQL against the reporting data mart, executes
it read-only, and returns a formatted result set.

## Available Datasets
- `customers` — one row per customer, with segment, branch, onboarding date.
- `accounts` — one row per account, product, balance, status.
- `transactions` — one row per transaction, txn_type, channel, amount.

Additional derived views are added quarterly; see the DDL under
`FINANCIAL_ADVISOR/mutual_funds.md` etc. for illustrative examples.

## Good Prompts
- "How many customers opened SAVINGS accounts?"
- "Top 5 customers by savings balance in Mumbai branches."
- "Average NEFT transaction amount last month by channel."
- "List customers with dormant SAVINGS accounts and balance under 5000."

## Guardrails
The engine will refuse to run SQL that:
- Writes data (INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / DROP / ALTER / ATTACH).
- References tables outside the whitelisted set.
- Returns more than 5,000 rows in a single call.

## Limitations
- Text2SQL cannot answer questions that depend on documents (use the RAG
  bubbles for those).
- It does not yet handle time-series joins across all history — restrict to
  90 days for stable results.

[S3] Bi Intro
# Conversational BI — Getting Started

## What It Is
The `Conversational BI` bubble routes natural-language questions to the
Text-to-SQL agent, which drafts SQL against the reporting data mart, executes
it read-only, and returns a formatted result set.

## Available Datasets
- `customers` — one row per customer, with segment, branch, onboarding date.
- `accounts` — one row per account, product, balance, status.
- `transactions` — one row per transaction, txn_type, channel, amount.

Additional derived views are added quarterly; see the DDL under
`FINANCIAL_ADVISOR/mutual_funds.md` etc. for illustrative examples.

## Good Prompts
- "How many customers opened SAVINGS accounts?"
- "Top 5 customers by savings balance in Mumbai branches."
- "Average NEFT transaction amount last month by channel."
- "List customers with dormant SAVINGS accounts and balance under 5000."

## Guardrails
The engine will refuse to run SQL that:
- Writes data (INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / DROP / ALTER / ATTACH).
- References tables outside the whitelisted set.
- Returns more than 5,000 rows in a single call.

## Limitations
- Text2SQL cannot answer questions that depend on documents (use the RAG
  bubbles for those).
- It does not yet handle time-series joins across all history — restrict to
  90 days for stable results.

## Reference
`CBI-INTRO-2026-01` · Owner: BI Platform team.

[S4] How do I use the Conversational BI bubble?
Q: How do I use the Conversational BI bubble?
A: Choose the Conversational BI bubble and ask a natural-language question about customers, accounts, or transactions. Vartalaap generates SQL, executes it read-only against the reporting mart, and returns a formatted table.

[S3] Bi Intro
# Conversational BI — Getting Started

## What It Is
The `Conversational BI` bubble routes natural-language questions to the
Text-to-SQL agent, which drafts SQL against the reporting data mart, executes
it read-only, and returns a formatted result set.

## Available Datasets
- `customers` — one row per customer, with segment, branch, onboarding date.
- `accounts` — one row per account, product, balance, status.
- `transactions` — one row per transaction, txn_type, channel, amount.

Additional derived views are added quarterly; see the DDL under
`FINANCIAL_ADVISOR/mutual_funds.md` etc. for illustrative examples.

## Good Prompts
- "How many customers opened SAVINGS accounts?"
- "Top 5 customers by savings balance in Mumbai branches."
- "Average NEFT transaction amount last month by channel."
- "List customers with dormant SAVINGS accounts and balance under 5000."

## Guardrails
The engine will refuse to run SQL that:
- Writes data (INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / DROP / ALTER / ATTACH).
- References tables outside the whitelisted set.
- Returns more than 5,000 rows in a single call.

## Limitations
- Text2SQL cannot answer questions that depend on documents (use the RAG
  bubbles for those).
- It does not yet handle time-series joins across all history — restrict to
  90 days for stable results.

## Reference
`CBI-INTRO-2026-01` · Owner: BI Platform team.

[S4] What is record retention?
Q: What is record retention?
A: record retention: maintain KYC and transaction records for the prescribed period after account closure.

[S5] Bi Data Freshness
# Data Freshness SLAs

## Tiers
- T0 (real-time/near-real-time): payment and fraud views, up to 15 minutes.
- T1 (daily): business performance and customer metrics, by 09:00 IST.
- T2 (weekly/monthly): HR and survey aggregates.

## Visibility
Each dashboard shows its last refresh timestamp. The assistant quotes
data-as-of dates in answers.

## Breach Handling
Freshness breaches alert the data engineering on-call and are tracked to
resolution.

Policy code: BI-FRESH-2026-01 | Owner: Data Platform team.

[S3] Bi Intro
# Conversational BI — Getting Started

## What It Is
The `Conversational BI` bubble routes natural-language questions to the
Text-to-SQL agent, which drafts SQL against the reporting data mart, executes
it read-only, and returns a formatted result set.

## Available Datasets
- `customers` — one row per customer, with segment, branch, onboarding date.
- `accounts` — one row per account, product, balance, status.
- `transactions` — one row per transaction, txn_type, channel, amount.

Additional derived views are added quarterly; see the DDL under
`FINANCIAL_ADVISOR/mutual_funds.md` etc. for illustrative examples.

## Good Prompts
- "How many customers opened SAVINGS accounts?"
- "Top 5 customers by savings balance in Mumbai branches."
- "Average NEFT transaction amount last month by channel."
- "List customers with dormant SAVINGS accounts and balance under 5000."

## Guardrails
The engine will refuse to run SQL that:
- Writes data (INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / DROP / ALTER / ATTACH).
- References tables outside the whitelisted set.
- Returns more than 5,000 rows in a single call.

## Limitations
- Text2SQL cannot answer questions that depend on documents (use the RAG
  bubbles for those).
- It does not yet handle time-series joins across all history — restrict to
  90 days for stable results.

## Reference
`CBI-INTRO-2026-01` · Owner: BI Platform team.

[S4] What is record retention?
Q: What is record retention?
A: record retention: maintain KYC and transaction records for the prescribed period after account closure.

[S5] Bi Data Freshness
# Data Freshness SLAs

## Tiers
- T0 (real-time/near-real-time): payment and fraud views, up to 15 minutes.
- T1 (daily): business performance and customer metrics, by 09:00 IST.
- T2 (weekly/monthly): HR and survey aggregates.

## Visibility
Each dashboard shows its last refresh timestamp. The assistant quotes
data-as-of dates in answers.

## Breach Handling
Freshness breaches alert the data engineering on-call and are tracked to
resolution.

Policy code: BI-FRESH-2026-01 | Owner: Data Platform team.

[S2] Bi Intro
# Conversational BI — Getting Started

## What It Is
The `Conversational BI` bubble routes natural-language questions to the
Text-to-SQL agent, which drafts SQL against the reporting data mart, executes
it read-only, and returns a formatted result set.

## Available Datasets
- `customers` — one row per customer, with segment, branch, onboarding date.
- `accounts` — one row per account, product, balance, status.
- `transactions` — one row per transaction, txn_type, channel, amount.

Additional derived views are added quarterly; see the DDL under
`FINANCIAL_ADVISOR/mutual_funds.md` etc. for illustrative examples.

## Good Prompts
- "How many customers opened SAVINGS accounts?"
- "Top 5 customers by savings balance in Mumbai branches."
- "Average NEFT transaction amount last month by channel."
- "List customers with dormant SAVINGS accounts and balance under 5000."

## Guardrails
The engine will refuse to run SQL that:
- Writes data (INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / DROP / ALTER / ATTACH).
- References tables outside the whitelisted set.
- Returns more than 5,000 rows in a single call.

## Limitations
- Text2SQL cannot answer questions that depend on documents (use the RAG
  bubbles for those).
- It does not yet handle time-series joins across all history — restrict to
  90 days for stable results.

## Reference
`CBI-INTRO-2026-01` · Owner: BI Platform team.

# वार्तालाप (Vartalaap) Assistant Overview

## What It Is
वार्तालाप is the bank's internal AI assistant that answers policy, product,
process and analytics questions by searching approved internal knowledge.

Questions are matched against indexed documents; relevant passages are
retrieved and used to compose grounded answers with citations.

- Policy lookup across HR, IT, legal, ops and finance.
- Product and process guidance from the knowledge base.

Available as a chat assistant on the intranet and via the API for embedded
experiences.

[S5] What is the Conversational BI bubble used for?
Q: What is the Conversational BI bubble used for?
A: The Conversational BI bubble is used for free-text analytics against the reporting data mart. It uses the Text2SQL agent to translate the question into SQL and executes it on the reporting DB.

[S3] Bi Intro
# Conversational BI — Getting Started

## What It Is
The `Conversational BI` bubble routes natural-language questions to the
Text-to-SQL agent, which drafts SQL against the reporting data mart, executes
it read-only, and returns a formatted result set.

## Available Datasets
- `customers` — one row per customer, with segment, branch, onboarding date.
- `accounts` — one row per account, product, balance, status.
- `transactions` — one row per transaction, txn_type, channel, amount.

Additional derived views are added quarterly; see the DDL under
`FINANCIAL_ADVISOR/mutual_funds.md` etc. for illustrative examples.

## Good Prompts
- "How many customers opened SAVINGS accounts?"
- "Top 5 customers by savings balance in Mumbai branches."
- "Average NEFT transaction amount last month by channel."
- "List customers with dormant SAVINGS accounts and balance under 5000."

## Guardrails
The engine will refuse to run SQL that:
- Writes data (INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / DROP / ALTER / ATTACH).
- References tables outside the whitelisted set.
- Returns more than 5,000 rows in a single call.

## Limitations
- Text2SQL cannot answer questions that depend on documents (use the RAG
  bubbles for those).
- It does not yet handle time-series joins across all history — restrict to
  90 days for stable results.

## Reference
`CBI-INTRO-2026-01` · Owner: BI Platform team.

# Conversational BI Training Guide

## Getting Started
Start with the sample questions and the data dictionary walkthrough.

- Name the measure: balance, disbursal, spend, activation.

[S2] Why did Conversational BI refuse my query?
Q: Why did Conversational BI refuse my query?
A: The Text-to-SQL agent refuses queries that write data, reference tables outside the whitelist, or would return more than 5000 rows. Restrict the query, add filters, or split the analysis into steps.

# BI Platform Architecture

## Layers
1. Sources: core banking, CRM, cards, payments and HR systems.
2. Lakehouse: raw, curated and semantic layers on the analytics platform.
3. Serving: semantic models consumed by dashboards, notebooks and the
   conversational BI assistant.

## Data Flow
Change-data-capture and batch pipelines land data within defined freshness
SLAs. Transformations produce the curated and semantic layers.

## Access Paths
The conversational BI assistant reads only the semantic layer. No query
touches source systems directly.

## Resilience
Pipelines carry retries, dead-letter handling and data-quality gates.

Policy code: BI-ARCH-2026-01 | Owner: Data Platform team.

[S4] What is the Conversational BI bubble used for?
Q: What is the Conversational BI bubble used for?
A: The Conversational BI bubble is used for free-text analytics against the reporting data mart. It uses the Text2SQL agent to translate the question into SQL and executes it on the reporting DB.

[S5] Where do I learn data-as-of?
Q: Where do I learn data-as-of?
A: The BI training guide and the data dictionary.

# Conversational BI — Getting Started

## What It Is
The `Conversational BI` bubble routes natural-language questions to the
Text-to-SQL agent, which drafts SQL against the reporting data mart, executes
it read-only, and returns a formatted result set.

## Available Datasets
- `customers` — one row per customer, with segment, branch, onboarding date.
- `accounts` — one row per account, product, balance, status.
- `transactions` — one row per transaction, txn_type, channel, amount.

Additional derived views are added quarterly; see the DDL under
`FINANCIAL_ADVISOR/mutual_funds.md` etc. for illustrative examples.

## Good Prompts
- "How many customers opened SAVINGS accounts?"
- "Top 5 customers by savings balance in Mumbai branches."
- "Average NEFT transaction amount last month by channel."
- "List customers with dormant SAVINGS accounts and balance under 5000."

## Guardrails
The engine will refuse to run SQL that:
- Writes data (INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / DROP / ALTER / ATTACH).
- References tables outside the whitelisted set.
- Returns more than 5,000 rows in a single call.

## Limitations
- Text2SQL cannot answer questions that depend on documents (use the RAG
  bubbles for those).
- It does not yet handle time-series joins across all history — restrict to
  90 days for stable results.

## Reference

# Conversational BI — Getting Started

## What It Is
The `Conversational BI` bubble routes natural-language questions to the
Text-to-SQL agent, which drafts SQL against the reporting data mart, executes
it read-only, and returns a formatted result set.

## Available Datasets
- `customers` — one row per customer, with segment, branch, onboarding date.
- `accounts` — one row per account, product, balance, status.
- `transactions` — one row per transaction, txn_type, channel, amount.

Additional derived views are added quarterly; see the DDL under
`FINANCIAL_ADVISOR/mutual_funds.md` etc. for illustrative examples.

## Good Prompts
- "How many customers opened SAVINGS accounts?"
- "Top 5 customers by savings balance in Mumbai branches."
- "Average NEFT transaction amount last month by channel."
- "List customers with dormant SAVINGS accounts and balance under 5000."

## Guardrails
The engine will refuse to run SQL that:
- Writes data (INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / DROP / ALTER / ATTACH).
- References tables outside the whitelisted set.
- Returns more than 5,000 rows in a single call.

## Limitations
- Text2SQL cannot answer questions that depend on documents (use the RAG
  bubbles for those).
- It does not yet handle time-series joins across all history — restrict to
  90 days for stable results.

## Reference
`CBI-INTRO-2026-01` · Owner: BI Platform team.

[S2] Bi Intro
# Conversational BI — Getting Started

## What It Is
The `Conversational BI` bubble routes natural-language questions to the
Text-to-SQL agent, which drafts SQL against the reporting data mart, executes
it read-only, and returns a formatted result set.

## Available Datasets
- `customers` — one row per customer, with segment, branch, onboarding date.
- `accounts` — one row per account, product, balance, status.
- `transactions` — one row per transaction, txn_type, channel, amount.

Additional derived views are added quarterly; see the DDL under
`FINANCIAL_ADVISOR/mutual_funds.md` etc. for illustrative examples.

## Good Prompts
- "How many customers opened SAVINGS accounts?"
- "Top 5 customers by savings balance in Mumbai branches."
- "Average NEFT transaction amount last month by channel."
- "List customers with dormant SAVINGS accounts and balance under 5000."

## Guardrails
The engine will refuse to run SQL that:
- Writes data (INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / DROP / ALTER / ATTACH).
- References tables outside the whitelisted set.
- Returns more than 5,000 rows in a single call.

## Limitations
- Text2SQL cannot answer questions that depend on documents (use the RAG
  bubbles for those).
- It does not yet handle time-series joins across all history — restrict to
  90 days for stable results.

## Reference
`CBI-INTRO-2026-01` · Owner: BI Platform team.

# Savings Account Products

## Product Range
- Basic savings: zero-balance variant per RBI guidelines.
- Regular savings with tiered interest.
- Salary accounts with bundled benefits.
- Premium savings with lifestyle and banking privileges.

## Eligibility
Resident individuals, HUFs in select variants, and minors through guardians.
NRI variants are offered under NRE/NRO schemes.

## Interest
Interest is credited quarterly based on daily balances, as per prevailing
rates published on the website.

## Value-Adds
Debit cards, digital banking, sweep facilities and insurance covers vary by
variant and are detailed in the product one-pager.

Advisory note: confirm the latest features from the product master before
quoting to customers.

# Senior Citizen Savings Scheme

## Eligibility
Individuals aged 60 and above; 55-60 for those who retired under
superannuation/VRS within the prescribed rules.

## Features
- Tenure of 5 years, extendable once by 3 years.
- Quarterly interest at government-notified rates.
- Deposit limits per scheme rules; joint accounts with spouse allowed.

## Tax
Deposits qualify under Section 80C. Interest is taxable and subject to TDS.

## Premature Closure
Allowed with penalty after the first year except death cases.

Advisory note: compare SCSS with the Senior Citizens Savings and monthly
income options.

CR-WALK-CAPACITY-2026-01 | Owner: Change Management Office.

[S2] Change Request Standard
# Change Request (CR) Standard

## Definition
A **Change Request** is any planned addition, modification or removal of a
production or production-adjacent component that could affect service
availability, integrity or compliance.

## CR Categories
| Category | Approval | Freeze windows apply? |
|---|---|---|
| Standard | Pre-approved template, no CAB | Yes |
| Normal | CAB approval | Yes |
| Emergency | Emergency CAB (E-CAB) | Yes, with waiver |

## Mandatory CR Fields
- Business justification.
- Impact assessment (services, users, data).
- Roll-back plan with owner and time budget.
- Test evidence (unit, integration, UAT sign-off).
- Communication plan.
- Downtime window (if any).

## Freeze Windows
No production CRs during:
- Financial year-end close (last week of March, first week of April).
- Half-yearly close (last week of September, first week of October).
- Regulatory reporting window (2 business days before submission deadline).

## Approval Matrix
| Change scope | Approver |
|---|---|
| Non-prod, single team | Team lead |
| Prod, single service | Service owner |
| Prod, cross-service or data | CAB |
| Regulatory / customer-facing | CAB + Compliance sign-off |

## References
- Standard code: CR-STD-2026-01
- Owner: Change Advisory Board (CAB) secretariat.

[S4] Bi Intro
# Conversational BI — Getting Started

## What It Is
The `Conversational BI` bubble routes natural-language questions to the
Text-to-SQL agent, which drafts SQL against the reporting data mart, executes
it read-only, and returns a formatted result set.

## Available Datasets
- `customers` — one row per customer, with segment, branch, onboarding date.
- `accounts` — one row per account, product, balance, status.
- `transactions` — one row per transaction, txn_type, channel, amount.

Additional derived views are added quarterly; see the DDL under
`FINANCIAL_ADVISOR/mutual_funds.md` etc. for illustrative examples.

## Good Prompts
- "How many customers opened SAVINGS accounts?"
- "Top 5 customers by savings balance in Mumbai branches."
- "Average NEFT transaction amount last month by channel."
- "List customers with dormant SAVINGS accounts and balance under 5000."

## Guardrails
The engine will refuse to run SQL that:
- Writes data (INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / DROP / ALTER / ATTACH).
- References tables outside the whitelisted set.
- Returns more than 5,000 rows in a single call.

## Limitations
- Text2SQL cannot answer questions that depend on documents (use the RAG
  bubbles for those).
- It does not yet handle time-series joins across all history — restrict to
  90 days for stable results.

## Reference
`CBI-INTRO-2026-01` · Owner: BI Platform team.

[S5] Senior Citizen Savings
# Senior Citizen Savings Scheme

## Eligibility
Individuals aged 60 and above; 55-60 for those who retired under
superannuation/VRS within the prescribed rules.

## Features
- Tenure of 5 years, extendable once by 3 years.
- Quarterly interest at government-notified rates.
- Deposit limits per scheme rules; joint accounts with spouse allowed.

## Tax
Deposits qualify under Section 80C. Interest is taxable and subject to TDS.

## Premature Closure
Allowed with penalty after the first year except death cases.

Advisory note: compare SCSS with the Senior Citizens Savings and monthly
income options.

# Change Request (CR) Standard

## Definition
A **Change Request** is any planned addition, modification or removal of a
production or production-adjacent component that could affect service
availability, integrity or compliance.

## CR Categories
| Category | Approval | Freeze windows apply? |
|---|---|---|
| Standard | Pre-approved template, no CAB | Yes |
| Normal | CAB approval | Yes |
| Emergency | Emergency CAB (E-CAB) | Yes, with waiver |

## Mandatory CR Fields
- Business justification.
- Impact assessment (services, users, data).
- Roll-back plan with owner and time budget.
- Test evidence (unit, integration, UAT sign-off).
- Communication plan.
- Downtime window (if any).

## Freeze Windows
No production CRs during:
- Financial year-end close (last week of March, first week of April).
- Half-yearly close (last week of September, first week of October).
- Regulatory reporting window (2 business days before submission deadline).

## Approval Matrix
| Change scope | Approver |
|---|---|
| Non-prod, single team | Team lead |
| Prod, single service | Service owner |
| Prod, cross-service or data | CAB |
| Regulatory / customer-facing | CAB + Compliance sign-off |

## References
- Standard code: CR-STD-2026-01
- Owner: Change Advisory Board (CAB) secretariat.

[S2] How do I raise a Change Request (CR) for a policy update?
Q: How do I raise a Change Request (CR) for a policy update?
A: Log a CR in the Change Management portal. Attach the impact assessment, business justification and roll-back plan. CRs affecting production data require CAB approval.

# Product Note: Savings Accounts

## Overview

Savings Accounts serve customers with daily-balance interest and variant-based value adds.

## Key Features

Features and limits are as per the current product master.

Interest, fees and charges follow the published tariff.

## Advisory Cues

Confirm the latest variant details before quoting to customers.

Explain fees and charges in plain language.

Document customer decisions and consent.

## Support

Product queries route to the product helpdesk via the CRM.

## Policy code

FA-NOTE-SAVINGS-2026-01 | Owner: Products & Advisory.

[S2] Bi Sample Queries
# Sample Conversational Queries

## Customer Metrics
"Show savings account balance trend for the last six months by region."

## Cards
"What was credit card spend last quarter compared to the previous quarter?"

## Branch Performance
"List the bottom five branches by current-account acquisition this month."

## Payments
"How many UPI transactions failed yesterday by failure code?"

## HR
"Show attrition rate for grade AVP and above in the last two quarters."

Mention the measure, dimension and time window explicitly for best results.

Policy code: BI-QUERY-2026-01 | Owner: Data Platform team.

[S3] Cr Kpi Metrics
# CR KPIs & Metrics

## Key Metrics
- Successful change rate.
- Unplanned/emergency change ratio.
- Change-induced incident rate.
- Post-implementation review completion.
- Calendar adherence.

## Targets
Targets are set annually by the Change Management Office and reviewed
with CAB monthly.

## Reporting
A monthly change dashboard is published to senior management.

## Drill-Down
Metrics drill to individual changes for root-cause analysis.

Policy code: CR-KPI-2026-01 | Owner: Change Management Office.

[S4] Savings Account Products
# Savings Account Products

## Product Range
- Basic savings: zero-balance variant per RBI guidelines.
- Regular savings with tiered interest.
- Salary accounts with bundled benefits.
- Premium savings with lifestyle and banking privileges.

## Eligibility
Resident individuals, HUFs in select variants, and minors through guardians.
NRI variants are offered under NRE/NRO schemes.

## Interest
Interest is credited quarterly based on daily balances, as per prevailing
rates published on the website.

## Value-Adds
Debit cards, digital banking, sweep facilities and insurance covers vary by
variant and are detailed in the product one-pager.

Advisory note: confirm the latest features from the product master before
quoting to customers.

[S5] Where can a customer check the interest-free period?
Q: Where can a customer check the interest-free period?
A: The mobile app, statements and the cardholder agreement.

Compose the final answer now.

[S4] Bi Intro
# Conversational BI — Getting Started

## What It Is
The `Conversational BI` bubble routes natural-language questions to the
Text-to-SQL agent, which drafts SQL against the reporting data mart, executes
it read-only, and returns a formatted result set.

## Available Datasets
- `customers` — one row per customer, with segment, branch, onboarding date.
- `accounts` — one row per account, product, balance, status.
- `transactions` — one row per transaction, txn_type, channel, amount.

Additional derived views are added quarterly; see the DDL under
`FINANCIAL_ADVISOR/mutual_funds.md` etc. for illustrative examples.

## Good Prompts
- "How many customers opened SAVINGS accounts?"
- "Top 5 customers by savings balance in Mumbai branches."
- "Average NEFT transaction amount last month by channel."
- "List customers with dormant SAVINGS accounts and balance under 5000."

## Guardrails
The engine will refuse to run SQL that:
- Writes data (INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / DROP / ALTER / ATTACH).
- References tables outside the whitelisted set.
- Returns more than 5,000 rows in a single call.

## Limitations
- Text2SQL cannot answer questions that depend on documents (use the RAG
  bubbles for those).
- It does not yet handle time-series joins across all history — restrict to
  90 days for stable results.

## Reference
`CBI-INTRO-2026-01` · Owner: BI Platform team.

[S4] Bi Intro
# Conversational BI — Getting Started

## What It Is
The `Conversational BI` bubble routes natural-language questions to the
Text-to-SQL agent, which drafts SQL against the reporting data mart, executes
it read-only, and returns a formatted result set.

## Available Datasets
- `customers` — one row per customer, with segment, branch, onboarding date.
- `accounts` — one row per account, product, balance, status.
- `transactions` — one row per transaction, txn_type, channel, amount.

Additional derived views are added quarterly; see the DDL under
`FINANCIAL_ADVISOR/mutual_funds.md` etc. for illustrative examples.

## Good Prompts
- "How many customers opened SAVINGS accounts?"
- "Top 5 customers by savings balance in Mumbai branches."
- "Average NEFT transaction amount last month by channel."
- "List customers with dormant SAVINGS accounts and balance under 5000."

## Guardrails
The engine will refuse to run SQL that:
- Writes data (INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / DROP / ALTER / ATTACH).
- References tables outside the whitelisted set.
- Returns more than 5,000 rows in a single call.

## Limitations
- Text2SQL cannot answer questions that depend on documents (use the RAG
  bubbles for those).
- It does not yet handle time-series joins across all history — restrict to
  90 days for stable results.

## Reference
`CBI-INTRO-2026-01` · Owner: BI Platform team.

# Conversational BI — Getting Started

## What It Is
The `Conversational BI` bubble routes natural-language questions to the
Text-to-SQL agent, which drafts SQL against the reporting data mart, executes
it read-only, and returns a formatted result set.

## Available Datasets
- `customers` — one row per customer, with segment, branch, onboarding date.
- `accounts` — one row per account, product, balance, status.
- `transactions` — one row per transaction, txn_type, channel, amount.

Additional derived views are added quarterly; see the DDL under
`FINANCIAL_ADVISOR/mutual_funds.md` etc. for illustrative examples.

## Good Prompts
- "How many customers opened SAVINGS accounts?"
- "Top 5 customers by savings balance in Mumbai branches."
- "Average NEFT transaction amount last month by channel."
- "List customers with dormant SAVINGS accounts and balance under 5000."

## Guardrails
The engine will refuse to run SQL that:
- Writes data (INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / DROP / ALTER / ATTACH).
- References tables outside the whitelisted set.
- Returns more than 5,000 rows in a single call.

## Limitations
- Text2SQL cannot answer questions that depend on documents (use the RAG
  bubbles for those).
- It does not yet handle time-series joins across all history — restrict to
  90 days for stable results.

## Reference

[S2] Bi Intro
# Conversational BI — Getting Started

## What It Is
The `Conversational BI` bubble routes natural-language questions to the
Text-to-SQL agent, which drafts SQL against the reporting data mart, executes
it read-only, and returns a formatted result set.

## Available Datasets
- `customers` — one row per customer, with segment, branch, onboarding date.
- `accounts` — one row per account, product, balance, status.
- `transactions` — one row per transaction, txn_type, channel, amount.

Additional derived views are added quarterly; see the DDL under
`FINANCIAL_ADVISOR/mutual_funds.md` etc. for illustrative examples.

## Good Prompts
- "How many customers opened SAVINGS accounts?"
- "Top 5 customers by savings balance in Mumbai branches."
- "Average NEFT transaction amount last month by channel."
- "List customers with dormant SAVINGS accounts and balance under 5000."

## Guardrails
The engine will refuse to run SQL that:
- Writes data (INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / DROP / ALTER / ATTACH).
- References tables outside the whitelisted set.
- Returns more than 5,000 rows in a single call.

## Limitations
- Text2SQL cannot answer questions that depend on documents (use the RAG
  bubbles for those).
- It does not yet handle time-series joins across all history — restrict to
  90 days for stable results.

## Reference
`CBI-INTRO-2026-01` · Owner: BI Platform team.

- `accounts` — one row per account, product, balance, status.
- `transactions` — one row per transaction, txn_type, channel, amount.

Additional derived views are added quarterly; see the DDL under
`FINANCIAL_ADVISOR/mutual_funds.md` etc. for illustrative examples.

## Good Prompts
- "How many customers opened SAVINGS accounts?"
- "Top 5 customers by savings balance in Mumbai branches."
- "Average NEFT transaction amount last month by channel."
- "List customers with dormant SAVINGS accounts and balance under 5000."

## Guardrails
The engine will refuse to run SQL that:
- Writes data (INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / DROP / ALTER / ATTACH).
- References tables outside the whitelisted set.
- Returns more than 5,000 rows in a single call.

## Limitations
- Text2SQL cannot answer questions that depend on documents (use the RAG
  bubbles for those).
- It does not yet handle time-series joins across all history — restrict to
  90 days for stable results.

## Reference
`CBI-INTRO-2026-01` · Owner: BI Platform team.

# Fixed Deposits — Product Note

## Product Variants
- **Regular FD:** interest paid monthly / quarterly / on maturity.
- **Reinvestment FD:** compounded quarterly, single maturity payout.
- **Tax Saver FD:** 5-year lock-in, deduction under Section 80C up to ₹1.5L.
- **Senior Citizen FD:** additional 0.50% over the applicable card rate.
- **NRE / NRO FD:** available to NRIs subject to source-of-fund controls.

## Booking Channels
- Internet banking (retail).
- Mobile app.
- Any branch during business hours.
- Relationship manager for HNI customers.

## Premature Withdrawal
- Allowed on all variants except the 5-year Tax Saver FD.
- Penalty: 1.00% below the applicable card rate for the period run OR the
  booking rate, whichever is lower.
- Sweep-in FDs are broken in FIFO order to fund the linked savings account.

## Nomination
Nomination is mandatory. It can be captured at booking or updated later via
the branch or internet banking. Joint holdings must specify the operating
mandate (either or survivor / former or survivor / joint).

## Auto Renewal
Auto renewal defaults to `Reinvestment` at the prevailing rate for the same
tenure. Customers can switch this off during booking.

## Reference
`FA-FD-2026-01` · Owner: Liabilities product team.

[S4] Fixed Deposits
# Fixed Deposits — Product Note

## Product Variants
- **Regular FD:** interest paid monthly / quarterly / on maturity.
- **Reinvestment FD:** compounded quarterly, single maturity payout.
- **Tax Saver FD:** 5-year lock-in, deduction under Section 80C up to ₹1.5L.
- **Senior Citizen FD:** additional 0.50% over the applicable card rate.
- **NRE / NRO FD:** available to NRIs subject to source-of-fund controls.

## Booking Channels
- Internet banking (retail).
- Mobile app.
- Any branch during business hours.
- Relationship manager for HNI customers.

## Premature Withdrawal
- Allowed on all variants except the 5-year Tax Saver FD.
- Penalty: 1.00% below the applicable card rate for the period run OR the
  booking rate, whichever is lower.
- Sweep-in FDs are broken in FIFO order to fund the linked savings account.

## Nomination
Nomination is mandatory. It can be captured at booking or updated later via
the branch or internet banking. Joint holdings must specify the operating
mandate (either or survivor / former or survivor / joint).

## Auto Renewal
Auto renewal defaults to `Reinvestment` at the prevailing rate for the same
tenure. Customers can switch this off during booking.

## Reference
`FA-FD-2026-01` · Owner: Liabilities product team.

superannuation/VRS within the prescribed rules.

- Tenure of 5 years, extendable once by 3 years.
- Quarterly interest at government-notified rates.
- Deposit limits per scheme rules; joint accounts with spouse allowed.

## Tax
Deposits qualify under Section 80C. Interest is taxable and subject to TDS.

## Premature Closure
Allowed with penalty after the first year except death cases.

income options.

[S2] Bi Intro
# Conversational BI — Getting Started

## What It Is
The `Conversational BI` bubble routes natural-language questions to the
Text-to-SQL agent, which drafts SQL against the reporting data mart, executes
it read-only, and returns a formatted result set.

## Available Datasets
- `customers` — one row per customer, with segment, branch, onboarding date.
- `accounts` — one row per account, product, balance, status.
- `transactions` — one row per transaction, txn_type, channel, amount.

Additional derived views are added quarterly; see the DDL under
`FINANCIAL_ADVISOR/mutual_funds.md` etc. for illustrative examples.

## Good Prompts
- "How many customers opened SAVINGS accounts?"
- "Top 5 customers by savings balance in Mumbai branches."
- "Average NEFT transaction amount last month by channel."
- "List customers with dormant SAVINGS accounts and balance under 5000."

## Guardrails
The engine will refuse to run SQL that:
- Writes data (INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / DROP / ALTER / ATTACH).
- References tables outside the whitelisted set.
- Returns more than 5,000 rows in a single call.

## Limitations
- Text2SQL cannot answer questions that depend on documents (use the RAG
  bubbles for those).
- It does not yet handle time-series joins across all history — restrict to
  90 days for stable results.

## Reference
`CBI-INTRO-2026-01` · Owner: BI Platform team.

[S3] Senior Citizen Savings
# Senior Citizen Savings Scheme

## Eligibility
Individuals aged 60 and above; 55-60 for those who retired under
superannuation/VRS within the prescribed rules.

## Features
- Tenure of 5 years, extendable once by 3 years.
- Quarterly interest at government-notified rates.
- Deposit limits per scheme rules; joint accounts with spouse allowed.

## Tax
Deposits qualify under Section 80C. Interest is taxable and subject to TDS.

## Premature Closure
Allowed with penalty after the first year except death cases.

Advisory note: compare SCSS with the Senior Citizens Savings and monthly
income options.

# Savings Account Products

## Product Range
- Basic savings: zero-balance variant per RBI guidelines.
- Regular savings with tiered interest.
- Salary accounts with bundled benefits.
- Premium savings with lifestyle and banking privileges.

## Eligibility
Resident individuals, HUFs in select variants, and minors through guardians.
NRI variants are offered under NRE/NRO schemes.

## Interest
Interest is credited quarterly based on daily balances, as per prevailing
rates published on the website.

## Value-Adds
Debit cards, digital banking, sweep facilities and insurance covers vary by
variant and are detailed in the product one-pager.

Advisory note: confirm the latest features from the product master before
quoting to customers.

# Savings Account Products

## Product Range
- Basic savings: zero-balance variant per RBI guidelines.
- Regular savings with tiered interest.
- Salary accounts with bundled benefits.
- Premium savings with lifestyle and banking privileges.

## Eligibility
Resident individuals, HUFs in select variants, and minors through guardians.
NRI variants are offered under NRE/NRO schemes.

## Interest
Interest is credited quarterly based on daily balances, as per prevailing
rates published on the website.

## Value-Adds
Debit cards, digital banking, sweep facilities and insurance covers vary by
variant and are detailed in the product one-pager.

Advisory note: confirm the latest features from the product master before
quoting to customers.

# Compensation Review Cycle

## Annual Cycle
Compensation review is effective 1 April. Rating inputs from the appraisal close in March
feed the increment matrix published by the Rewards team.

## Market Benchmarking
Every role is benchmarked against the banking sector median using annual market surveys.
Positions below the 25th percentile are prioritised for corrections.

## Increment Drivers
Increment is driven by performance rating, position-in-range and business affordability.
The matrix is approved by the compensation committee.

## Communication
Revised compensation letters are released in June. Any query must be raised through the
HR service portal within 30 days of release.

# Walkthrough: Capacity Add Change

## When This Applies

A Capacity Add change is planned, covering defined components only.

## Step-by-Step

1. Draft the CR with impact assessment and the risk score.

2. Attach test evidence and the rollback plan.

3. Obtain approvals per the matrix.

4. Implement inside the approved window.

5. Complete the post-implementation review.

## Watch Points

No scope expansion inside the window.

Incident linkage is mandatory for production changes.

## Policy code

CR-WALK-CAPACITY-2026-01 | Owner: Change Management Office.

[S2] Change Request Standard
# Change Request (CR) Standard

## Definition
A **Change Request** is any planned addition, modification or removal of a
production or production-adjacent component that could affect service
availability, integrity or compliance.

## CR Categories
| Category | Approval | Freeze windows apply? |
|---|---|---|
| Standard | Pre-approved template, no CAB | Yes |
| Normal | CAB approval | Yes |
| Emergency | Emergency CAB (E-CAB) | Yes, with waiver |

## Mandatory CR Fields
- Business justification.
- Impact assessment (services, users, data).
- Roll-back plan with owner and time budget.
- Test evidence (unit, integration, UAT sign-off).
- Communication plan.
- Downtime window (if any).

## Freeze Windows
No production CRs during:
- Financial year-end close (last week of March, first week of April).
- Half-yearly close (last week of September, first week of October).
- Regulatory reporting window (2 business days before submission deadline).

## Approval Matrix
| Change scope | Approver |
|---|---|
| Non-prod, single team | Team lead |
| Prod, single service | Service owner |
| Prod, cross-service or data | CAB |
| Regulatory / customer-facing | CAB + Compliance sign-off |

## References
- Standard code: CR-STD-2026-01
- Owner: Change Advisory Board (CAB) secretariat.

[S3] How do I raise a Change Request (CR) for a policy update?
Q: How do I raise a Change Request (CR) for a policy update?
A: Log a CR in the Change Management portal. Attach the impact assessment, business justification and roll-back plan. CRs affecting production data require CAB approval.

- Basic savings: zero-balance variant per RBI guidelines.
- Regular savings with tiered interest.
- Salary accounts with bundled benefits.
- Premium savings with lifestyle and banking privileges.

## Eligibility
Resident individuals, HUFs in select variants, and minors through guardians.
NRI variants are offered under NRE/NRO schemes.

## Interest
Interest is credited quarterly based on daily balances, as per prevailing
rates published on the website.

## Value-Adds
Debit cards, digital banking, sweep facilities and insurance covers vary by
variant and are detailed in the product one-pager.

Advisory note: confirm the latest features from the product master before
quoting to customers.

## Key Metrics
- Successful change rate.
- Unplanned/emergency change ratio.
- Change-induced incident rate.
- Post-implementation review completion.
- Calendar adherence.

## Targets

with CAB monthly.

## Reporting
A monthly change dashboard is published to senior management.

## Drill-Down

[S4] Bi Intro
# Conversational BI — Getting Started

## What It Is
The `Conversational BI` bubble routes natural-language questions to the
Text-to-SQL agent, which drafts SQL against the reporting data mart, executes
it read-only, and returns a formatted result set.

## Available Datasets
- `customers` — one row per customer, with segment, branch, onboarding date.
- `accounts` — one row per account, product, balance, status.
- `transactions` — one row per transaction, txn_type, channel, amount.

Additional derived views are added quarterly; see the DDL under
`FINANCIAL_ADVISOR/mutual_funds.md` etc. for illustrative examples.

## Good Prompts
- "How many customers opened SAVINGS accounts?"
- "Top 5 customers by savings balance in Mumbai branches."
- "Average NEFT transaction amount last month by channel."
- "List customers with dormant SAVINGS accounts and balance under 5000."

## Guardrails
The engine will refuse to run SQL that:
- Writes data (INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / DROP / ALTER / ATTACH).
- References tables outside the whitelisted set.
- Returns more than 5,000 rows in a single call.

## Limitations
- Text2SQL cannot answer questions that depend on documents (use the RAG
  bubbles for those).
- It does not yet handle time-series joins across all history — restrict to
  90 days for stable results.

## Reference
`CBI-INTRO-2026-01` · Owner: BI Platform team.

[S4] Bi Intro
# Conversational BI — Getting Started

## What It Is
The `Conversational BI` bubble routes natural-language questions to the
Text-to-SQL agent, which drafts SQL against the reporting data mart, executes
it read-only, and returns a formatted result set.

## Available Datasets
- `customers` — one row per customer, with segment, branch, onboarding date.
- `accounts` — one row per account, product, balance, status.
- `transactions` — one row per transaction, txn_type, channel, amount.

Additional derived views are added quarterly; see the DDL under
`FINANCIAL_ADVISOR/mutual_funds.md` etc. for illustrative examples.

## Good Prompts
- "How many customers opened SAVINGS accounts?"
- "Top 5 customers by savings balance in Mumbai branches."
- "Average NEFT transaction amount last month by channel."
- "List customers with dormant SAVINGS accounts and balance under 5000."

## Guardrails
The engine will refuse to run SQL that:
- Writes data (INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / DROP / ALTER / ATTACH).
- References tables outside the whitelisted set.
- Returns more than 5,000 rows in a single call.

## Limitations
- Text2SQL cannot answer questions that depend on documents (use the RAG
  bubbles for those).
- It does not yet handle time-series joins across all history — restrict to
  90 days for stable results.

## Reference
`CBI-INTRO-2026-01` · Owner: BI Platform team.

# Conversational BI — Getting Started

## What It Is
The `Conversational BI` bubble routes natural-language questions to the
Text-to-SQL agent, which drafts SQL against the reporting data mart, executes
it read-only, and returns a formatted result set.

## Available Datasets
- `customers` — one row per customer, with segment, branch, onboarding date.
- `accounts` — one row per account, product, balance, status.
- `transactions` — one row per transaction, txn_type, channel, amount.

Additional derived views are added quarterly; see the DDL under
`FINANCIAL_ADVISOR/mutual_funds.md` etc. for illustrative examples.

## Good Prompts
- "How many customers opened SAVINGS accounts?"
- "Top 5 customers by savings balance in Mumbai branches."
- "Average NEFT transaction amount last month by channel."
- "List customers with dormant SAVINGS accounts and balance under 5000."

## Guardrails
The engine will refuse to run SQL that:
- Writes data (INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / DROP / ALTER / ATTACH).
- References tables outside the whitelisted set.
- Returns more than 5,000 rows in a single call.

## Limitations
- Text2SQL cannot answer questions that depend on documents (use the RAG
  bubbles for those).
- It does not yet handle time-series joins across all history — restrict to
  90 days for stable results.

`CBI-INTRO-2026-01` · Owner: BI Platform team.

# Conversational BI — Getting Started

## What It Is
The `Conversational BI` bubble routes natural-language questions to the
Text-to-SQL agent, which drafts SQL against the reporting data mart, executes
it read-only, and returns a formatted result set.

## Available Datasets
- `customers` — one row per customer, with segment, branch, onboarding date.
- `accounts` — one row per account, product, balance, status.
- `transactions` — one row per transaction, txn_type, channel, amount.

Additional derived views are added quarterly; see the DDL under
`FINANCIAL_ADVISOR/mutual_funds.md` etc. for illustrative examples.

## Good Prompts
- "How many customers opened SAVINGS accounts?"
- "Top 5 customers by savings balance in Mumbai branches."
- "Average NEFT transaction amount last month by channel."
- "List customers with dormant SAVINGS accounts and balance under 5000."

## Guardrails
The engine will refuse to run SQL that:
- Writes data (INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / DROP / ALTER / ATTACH).
- References tables outside the whitelisted set.
- Returns more than 5,000 rows in a single call.

## Limitations
- Text2SQL cannot answer questions that depend on documents (use the RAG
  bubbles for those).
- It does not yet handle time-series joins across all history — restrict to
  90 days for stable results.

## Reference
`CBI-INTRO-2026-01` · Owner: BI Platform team.

# Product Note: Savings Accounts

## Overview

Savings Accounts serve customers with daily-balance interest and variant-based value adds.

## Key Features

Features and limits are as per the current product master.

Interest, fees and charges follow the published tariff.

## Advisory Cues

Confirm the latest variant details before quoting to customers.

Document customer decisions and consent.
